hot.title: Impulsive Buying Tendencies and Personality: Cognitive and Affective Aspects
hot.abstract: Impulsive buying is a growing problem in modern society with significant financial and psychological consequences, and it is necessary to examine the mechanisms underlying it. Understanding the mechanisms driving this behavior is crucial. Impulsive buying consists of two key aspects: a cognitive aspect, characterized by a lack of planning and reflection, and an affective aspect, involving emotional responses that can occur before, during, or after a purchase. This study aims to explore the relationship between personality traits, as measured by the HEXACO model, and tendencies toward impulsive buying. Specifically, it examines how the HEXACO traits differentially predict the cognitive and affective components of impulsive buying tendencies. Data were collected from a sample of 420 students, with 32 excluded due to incomplete responses, resulting in a final sample of 388 students (155 men, 233 women) with an average age of 22.8. Hierarchical regression analyses revealed that HEXACO personality domains significantly predicted overall impulsive buying tendencies. As expected, Honesty–Humility and Conscientiousness were negatively associated with impulsive buying, while Emotionality and Extraversion positively predicted impulsive buying tendencies. Moreover, Honesty–Humility, Conscientiousness, and Extraversion significantly predicted the cognitive component of impulsive buying, while Honesty–Humility and Emotionality were significant predictors of the affective component. These findings suggest the importance of educating individuals, from an early age, on the negative consequences of impulsive buying, effective money-saving strategies, and the principles of mental accounting.

hot.title: How perceived sustainability influences consumers’ clothing preferences
hot.abstract: In this study, we explored innovative approaches to sustainable fashion design, focusing on the increasingly prominent issue of sustainability in the global fashion industry. By analyzing consumer feedback in online communities, particularly through a systematic study of user comments on clothing products on the JD.com website, this paper reveals consumers' attitudes, expectations, and suggestions regarding sustainable fashion. The findings provide new directions for improvements in sustainable clothing design. We collected data using Python web scraping technology from the Chinese e-commerce platform JD.com and employed the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) method for text topic modeling. This approach successfully identified three main themes: perceived quality, perceived value, and sensory comfort. Additionally, we employed multivariate analysis of variance to assess consumers' perceptions. Survey data show that consumers demonstrat higher levels of perceived quality, value, purchase intention, and intention to repurchase sustainable clothing compared to traditional apparel. The research findings help apparel companies understand consumer needs regarding sustainability, providing theoretical support for designers and confirming the importance of emphasizing eco-friendly materials and sustainable production in new product development. This research not only provides actionable insights for the fashion industry but also contributes to the ongoing discourse on sustainable design strategies globally.

hot.title: Measuring Companies’ Environmental and Social Impacts: An analysis of ESG Ratings and SDG Scores
hot.abstract: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) ratings are central to sustainable investing and research but face criticism for inaccurately reflecting corporate sustainability performance. In response, new metrics have emerged that assess companies’ impacts on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This article compares four ESG ratings with two SDG scores, revealing no correlation between them. It then evaluates the alignment between these sustainability ratings and how investors and regulators assess corporate (un)sustainability. The findings show that SDG scores capture how these stakeholders judge companies’ negative and positive impacts on sustainable development, while ESG ratings do not. This implies that SDG scores have high, and ESG ratings low, construct validity for assessing corporate sustainability performance. These results underscore that concepts like ESG, corporate sustainability, and company impact can be used complementarily but not interchangeably. The practical implication is that sustainable investors should prioritize sustainable development impacts next to avoiding ESG risks.

hot.title: The push-pull-mooring model of consumer service switching: a meta-analytical review to guide future research
hot.venue: Journal of Service Theory and Practice
hot.abstract: Purpose For nearly 2 decades, the push-pull-mooring (PPM) model has been used frequently by scholars to explain consumers’ service switching intention and behavior. However, heterogeneity and incomparability between PPM model studies are prevalent issues: The chosen predictor variables, their categorization, their measurement, reported effect sizes, and effect directions vary considerably. By addressing these issues, the present meta-analytical review enables future researchers applying the PPM model to identify relevant variables and use valid measurements. Design/methodology/approach Based on 148 empirical studies employing the PPM model, the variables used to predict consumers’ service switching intention and behavior, their frequency of use, their categorization into push, pull, and mooring factors, and their measurement are assessed. The effect sizes and directions of the relationships between these variables and consumers’ service switching intention and behavior are analyzed using meta-analytic structural equation modeling. Additionally, the predictive capacity of this model and the influence of moderators are assessed. Findings Among the 148 empirical studies, 382 different independent variables were used. The three most frequently used and distinctly categorized independent variables are dissatisfaction (push), alternative attractiveness (pull), and switching costs (mooring). Overall, 152 unique sources were cited to measure these variables and the dependent variables. Dissatisfaction and alternative attractiveness increase switching intention, which positively affects switching behavior, while switching costs decrease switching intention. The model explains 30% of the variance in switching intention and 31% of the variance in switching behavior. Originality/va

hot.title: Willingness to pay a premium for eco-label products in China: a mediation model based on quality value
hot.abstract: Sustainable consumption plays an important role in achieving sustainable development. Eco-labels can help to convey this message to consumers. In China, the new carbon label represents a new kind of sustainable eco-label; as such, the relationship between carbon labeling and consumers' willingness to pay (WTP) a premium is worth studying. This paper explores the impact of carbon label recognition on WTP a premium, which is also affected by the perceived value of quality attributes and effective advertising campaigns. The results show that the former plays an intermediary role in carbon label recognition and premium payment intention, while the latter regulates the relationship between perceived value of quality attributes and premium payment intention. The research shows that when consumers are aware of carbon labeling, they are more willing to pay higher prices for products as they believe the quality of these products to be higher. For others, effective advertising campaigns can encourage paying a premium. This not only provides suggestions for enterprises promoting green products and for governments wishing to raise environmental awareness via guidance and education but also promotes the sustainable development of green products.

hot.title: The role of robo-advisors in behavioural finance, shaping investment decisions
hot.abstract: This study focuses on using artificial intelligence-driven financial robo-advisors in the investment decision-making domain by retail investors. Based on heuristic and prospect theory, the researcher aims to examine how AI-powered financial robo-advisors (AIPFRA), through their perceived interactivity, personalisation, autonomy, algorithm interpretation and structural assurance, influence retail investors’ loss aversion and overconfidence biases, ultimately enhancing robo-advisor usage in investment decision-making. Using purposive sampling, data from 461 retail investors were collected and analysed through structural equation modelling using SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that, except for structural assurance, robo-advisors’ perceived personalisation, interactivity, autonomy and algorithm transparency substantially mitigated investors’ overconfidence and loss-aversion biases, enhancing robo-advisor usage for investment decision-making. The study highlights the significance of financial literacy in moderating the relationship between biases and the use of robo-advisors. The study contributed by extending Heuristic and Prospect Theories to the AI-driven robo-advisor investment ecosystem. The study comprehensively explains how AI-powered robo-advisor design features impact investor psychology and adoption by bridging behavioural biases such as loss aversion and overconfidence with technology mechanisms like interactivity, personalisation, autonomy, algorithm interpretability and structural assurance. The results can help financial institutions implement user-centric advisory tools and help fintech developers create more bias-aware robo-advisors.

hot.title: The Impact of 7Ps Green Marketing Mix on Customer Commitment and Willingness to Pay a Premium Price: Evidence from Vietnam
hot.abstract: As consumers prioritize environmental issues and sustainable development, using green elements in marketing strategy has become valuable. This research examines how the 7Ps green marketing mix influences customer commitment and willingness to pay a premium price for green products, focusing on the role of green brand loyalty, association, and perceived quality. A PLS-SEM analysis of survey data from 571 young Vietnamese consumers reveals that different green 7Ps components exert distinct effects on green consumer-based brand equity (CBBE). While prior research largely focuses on green product, price, place and promotion, limited attention has been given to green human factors, process, and physical evidence, which this study addresses. The findings of this study not only confirm the significant influence of green CBBE dimensions on consumer commitment and willingness to pay a premium price but also enriches the green marketing and consumer behavior literature. Moreover, these provide practical strategies for businesses and policymakers in emerging markets to effectively leverage green marketing, strengthen consumer commitment, implement premium pricing strategies, and contribute to advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

hot.title: Secondhand fashion consumers exhibit fast fashion behaviors despite sustainability narratives
hot.abstract: The fashion industry contributes 2-8% of global greenhouse gas emissions, driven by rising clothing consumption and the proliferation of fast fashion. Fast fashion accelerates environmental harm through rapid production cycles, low costs, and short garment lifespans. Secondhand clothing markets are often promoted as a sustainable alternative, promising extended use and reduced waste. These markets have grown rapidly, with global sales reaching $177 billion in 2022 and projected to double by 2027. Despite this growth, few studies have empirically examined whether secondhand purchasing displaces or merely supplements primary market consumption. This study addresses that gap using a nationally representative survey of 1,009 U.S. consumers. We find that secondhand consumption is positively correlated with new clothing purchases (r = 0.58, p < 0.01), particularly among younger consumers and frequent shoppers. Cluster and principal component analyses reveal that highly engaged secondhand consumers also exhibit high overall consumption and short garment retention. Although many report high sustainability knowledge, such knowledge does not reliably predict sustainable behavior. Drawing on rebound and moral licensing theories, we suggest that secondhand purchases may psychologically or economically justify continued overconsumption. These findings challenge assumptions about resale's environmental benefits and support policy interventions to realign resale practices with sustainability goals.

hot.title: From perceived green product quality to purchase intention: the roles of price sensitivity and environmental concern
hot.abstract: Purpose This research seeks to address the existing gaps in the literature by rigorously investigating the influence of consumers’ perceived green product quality (PPQ), price sensitivity to green products (PRS) and environmental concern (ENC) on their intention to purchase green products (GPI) within the context of green circular economies. Furthermore, the study will explore the role of PRS as a mediator and ENC as a moderator by applying the price-expectancy model (PEM) and social exchange theory (SET). Design/methodology/approach The purposive sampling technique was employed to analyse 412 online survey responses from consumers, utilising partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The findings indicate a positive relationship between PPQ and PRS and PRS and GPI, contradicting the hypothesised negative associations. This suggests that as consumers become increasingly price-sensitive, they perceive green products to possess higher quality without diminishing their purchase intentions. Additionally, PPQ is positively associated with GPI, implying that enhanced perceptions of quality directly contribute to an increased intention to purchase green products. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that while ENC moderates the relationship between PPQ and PRS, its practical significance is limited. Practical implications This research emphasises to marketers that they should prioritise quality features while addressing PRS, particularly for environmentally concerned consumers, which can effectively shape consumers’ GPI. Originality/value This study’s originality lies in its integration of PRS and ENC within green consumerism. This offers valuable insights into green marketing and provides marketers with practical strategies to tackle the challenge

hot.title: Unveiling the enigma of blind box impulse buying curiosity: The moderating role of price consciousness
hot.abstract: This study explores the causes of curiosity-driven impulse buying in blind boxes using the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) model and adaptation level theory. It examines how store environment and product factors contribute to customer curiosity, incorporating price consciousness into the overall framework. Insights from an online survey of 306 Chinese respondents indicate that environmental factors and specific product characteristics positively influence consumer curiosity, while price consciousness has a negative moderate effect. The findings also show that customer curiosity stimulates impulse buying behavior and mediates the relationship between store atmosphere, surprise, and perceived novelty. This study identifies both objective and subjective factors behind blind box impulse buying and offers relevant suggestions for governments and consumers on managing impulse buying.

hot.title: Perceived Price Fairness as a Mediator in Customer Green Consumption: Insights from the New Energy Vehicle Industry and Sustainable Practices
hot.abstract: This paper explores how to promote consumer identification and acceptance of green products in the field of sustainable consumption and green marketing. Specifically, this paper examines how green factors affect consumers’ willingness to purchase new energy vehicles (NEVs) and focuses on the mediating role played by perceived price equity in this process. It is found that consumers’ green self-identity, green product experience, and green product innovation have a significant positive impact on their willingness to purchase NEVs, while perceived price fairness plays an important mediating role in this process. When consumers perceive that the pricing of NEVs is fair, they are more inclined to purchase them. Through the analysis of China’s new energy vehicle market, this paper puts forward suggestions to optimize the promotion strategy of green products from the perspective of price fairness, with a view to providing theoretical support and practical guidance for relevant enterprises. As China is the world’s number one country in terms of NEV ownership, studying its market consumption willingness not only reveals the unique characteristics of the Chinese market but also provides lessons and references for the future development of the new energy vehicle market in other countries, which is of great exemplary significance.

latest.title: A 2-layered game-theoretic deep learning model for predicting lodging demand: SHAP and nash equilibrium
latest.venue: Journal of Revenue and Pricing Management
latest.abstract: Abstract Forecasting tourism demand is critical for pricing and revenue management, yet most advanced machine learning models operate as “black boxes,” limiting interpretability and trust. This study introduces an explainable, game-theoretic hybrid deep learning framework for predicting short-term rental demand. This study incorporates game theory in two layers: a cooperative game and a competitive game. Using 729,888 daily observations from 1,852 Airbnb listings in Ann Arbor, Michigan, we compare traditional models (regression, SARIMAX) with advanced architectures (FCNN, LSTM, Transformer, and a Transformer–LSTM hybrid). Game theory is used in two layers: cooperative game (SHAP) and competitive game (classic Nash equilibrium). SHAP creates an explainable deep learning model to quantify each feature’s contribution. The best-performing model (FCNN) was further used to simulate a 3x3 pricing game between pairs within 4 submarkets. Results show that deep learning models significantly outperform traditional baselines, while SHAP-based feature attribution and clustering enhance transparency and strategic insight. The competitive games shed light on the characteristics and dynamics of each submarket. This research offers insights to revenue managers, policymakers, and operators.

latest.title: Technostress and telemedicine in rural communities: insights from healthcare professionals in the Italian Dolomites
latest.abstract: Introduction: In Italy, many facilities have started adopting telemedicine services since their regulation in 2020.Rural areas mainly benefit from telemedicine implementation due to their geographic features.We investigated the interests, attitudes, and perceptions of healthcare providers operating in the Italian Dolomites regarding the adoption of telemedicine.Furthermore, we explored the relationship between technostress and the intention to integrate telemedicine services during daily practices.Methods: We developed a structured interview protocol based on existing literature and following the key principles of constructivist grounded theory to investigate five areas of interest in telemedicine.After the interview, participants completed the Italian version of the Technostress Creators Scale (TCS) to evaluate the current technostress experienced in work activities, and a TCS-adapted version to measure technostress values generated through telemedicine services.Results: A content analysis of the interviews highlighted four main factors that can help communities more readily accept telemedicine services: the convenience of not having to travel, the ageing population, cost savings, and a sense of community.Regarding the scales, there were positive significant correlations between most of the subscales.Discussion: Our findings confirm that telemedicine fosters perceived security and service quality in rural settings.Despite moderate technostress, professionals remain supportive, highlighting the role of perceived usefulness.Key barriers include low digital literacy and reduced social contact, underscoring the need for strong patient-provider relationships and targeted digital r

latest.title: From Predictive Analytics to Supervised Agentic Decision Intelligence: Transforming Retail, CPG and Supply Chain Operations Through AI
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This research paper examines the evolution of enterprise analytics from traditional Business Intelligence and predictive modelling toward supervised agentic decision intelligence. The study focuses on Retail, Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), Marketing Measurement and Supply Chain Management, exploring how Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML) and specialized AI agents can improve enterprise decision-making. The paper presents Naukr.ai as an industry case study of a vertical AI platform focused on Retail and CPG analytics. It examines the company's four primary Agent Hubs: Supply Chain Agent Hub – Demand forecasting, inventory optimization, replenishment intelligence and store signals. Media Agent Hub – Agentic Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), media measurement and marketing budget optimization. Reporting Agent Hub – Conversational analytics, automated reporting and business intelligence. Category Management Agent Hub – Pricing, promotions, assortment, shelf and consumer intelligence. A key focus is the supervised agentic modelling approach, which combines AI-assisted analytical workflows with statistical modelling, model diagnostics and human validation. The paper proposes a conceptual framework connecting enterprise data integration, predictive intelligence, specialized AI agents, human oversight and operational decision-making. It also discusses the opportunities and challenges associated with enterprise AI adoption, including data quality, model explainability, statistical reliability, governance and organizational readiness. This publication is a conceptual research paper and industry case analysis based on academic literature and publicly available company information. Company-reported outcomes are identified as such and have not been independently verifie

latest.title: Leakage-resistant graph learning for risk propagation and risk-constrained control in construction supply networks
latest.abstract: Introduction Construction supply network decisions require both predecision warning from information available before operations unfold and topology-aware diagnosis after the disruption context becomes visible. We introduce an auditable framework that separates these regimes through a strict start-of-week information contract and connects risk scores to safety-gated resource allocation. Methods We combined public SUCCESS construction-logistics records with a frozen queue-flow mechanism producing paired counterfactual outcomes on a heterogeneous network with 302 nodes and 1,277 edges. Models were trained on pilots A and B, selected on pilot C, and evaluated on pilot D. The strict contract excluded all week-t outcomes, service levels, and shock-source indicators. Complementary evaluations comprised context-aware diagnosis, a construction consolidation center (CCC) outage panel, leave-one-project-out evaluation, and an independent SupplyGraph boundary test. Six resource policies were compared through validation-only selection and a held-out Pareto audit. Results Under the strict contract, the graph convolutional network achieved the highest held-out area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.2397 and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.8161 for 4,252 node-weeks with 60 positives. In the context-aware regime, relational GraphSAGE achieved an AUPRC of 0.5702, exceeding the matched multilayer perceptron (MLP) by 0.0803. Across eight positive pairs involving CCC outages, GraphSAGE achieved an AUPRC of 0.5845 versus 0.4994 for the MLP, with a positive pair-specific advantage in each case. The calibrated-risk guardrail identified an aggregate service improvement of 0.827% but screened the allocation out because the affected sites and failu

latest.title: When the algorithm feels like mine: personalisation depth, algorithmic transparency and psychological ownership in continued streaming engagement
latest.venue: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines whether artificial intelligence (AI) personalisation depth and algorithmic transparency relate to continued engagement with streaming platforms through consumers’ psychological ownership of the recommendation stream, and over what range of privacy concern the transparency route holds. Design/methodology/approach A 14-day, two-wave panel of streaming subscribers in Türkiye (N = 450) was analysed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and re-estimated with covariance-based SEM. A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment (N = 236) manipulated both features. Findings Personalisation depth showed an indirect-only mediation pattern through ownership in the estimated model, with a direct path practically equivalent to zero within a pre-specified bound; the pattern replicated under random assignment. Ownership carried 45 per cent of the association between transparency and engagement, and a direct path accounted for the rest. The transparency–ownership link was no longer significant above a privacy-concern level of about 4.5 (7-point scale), a region holding roughly two in five respondents. Platform involvement strengthened the personalisation route; no group difference was detected for transparency. Research limitations/implications Participants were subscribers aged 18–35 in three Turkish cities, engagement was self-reported and ownership and engagement were measured on the same occasion. Practical implications Ownership measures can complement viewing and churn metrics when personalisation is evaluated, and layered explanations let users choose how much detail they see. Originality/value For interactive marketing, the study recasts the AI feed as a possession consumers co-produce, not exposure firms deliver. It tests, and does

latest.title: Analysis of Instagram Digital Marketing and Product Quality, on Repurchase Intention in Tenpura Jakarta
latest.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effects of Instagram digital marketing and product quality on customers' repurchase intention at Tenpura Jakarta, a restaurant located in Blok M, South Jakarta. A quantitative research design with an associative approach was employed. Data were collected through questionnaires administered to 100 respondents selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression analysis with IBM SPSS Statistics. The results revealed that digital marketing had a positive and statistically significant relationship with repurchase intention, with a reported correlation coefficient (r) of 0.420 and a significance level of p < 0.001. Conversely, product quality was not significantly associated with repurchase intention (r = ?0.019, p = 0.849). The overall regression model was statistically significant (F = 10.492), with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.178, indicating that digital marketing and product quality collectively explained 17.8% of the variance in repurchase intention. These findings suggest that Instagram digital marketing was more strongly associated with customers' repurchase intention than product quality in the context of Tenpura Jakarta. The study highlights the importance of optimizing Instagram digital marketing strategies and recommends examining additional factors, such as brand image and customer experience, to better understand and potentially enhance customers' repurchase intention.

latest.title: Strategies to Improve Supply Chain Efficiency in Industrial-Scale Catering Services (Case Study on Morowali Mine Catering Company, Central Sulawesi)
latest.abstract: This study examined operational efficiency in industrial-scale catering services in the Morowali mining region of Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, through an integrated assessment of supply chain management (SCM), inventory management, and menu engineering. The research addressed operational challenges associated with high-volume food production, including inventory discrepancies, supply delays, and unplanned menu modifications. Employing a qualitative case study approach, data were collected through in-depth interviews, field observations, and reviews of operational documentation at an industrial catering company. Informants included personnel directly involved in procurement, goods receiving, warehousing, and food production. The findings revealed that supply chain processes were insufficiently coordinated across departments, contributing to inconsistencies between operational planning and implementation. Manual and partially digitized inventory recording practices were associated with discrepancies between recorded inventory levels and actual physical stock. Furthermore, menu planning was not consistently aligned with raw material availability, resulting in unplanned menu substitutions, increased food costs, and food waste. Collectively, these findings suggested that operational inefficiencies were associated with inadequate integration among supply chain operations, inventory control, and menu planning rather than a single isolated operational problem. Accordingly, the study recommended adopting integrated digital information systems, strengthening standard operating procedures (SOPs), and aligning menu planning with accurate inventory records and reliable supply information to improve operational efficiency. The findings provided practical insights into strengthening i

latest.title: Expanding a university-based social enterprise: organizational change across 15 years
latest.abstract: Introduction Social enterprises combine social purpose and commercial activity to address societal challenges, yet limited longitudinal evidence explains how they develop as they expand, particularly when operating within established institutions. This study examines the factors supporting expansion in a university-based social enterprise and how their function and importance change across stages of development. Methods We conduct a 15-year longitudinal case study of an enterprise delivering substance use prevention to secondary school students through face-to-face and digital formats. Evidence includes trial and survey data, organizational records, governance and funding documentation, and an extensive body of peer-reviewed publications. Using a social innovation lens, the study examines the roles of university actors, schools, government, funders and industry across the expansion process. Results Expansion was accompanied by increasing interdependence between the enterprise and the university. The university provided credibility, expertise, resources and institutional support, while the enterprise contributed to the university’s research activity and social mission. Technology also changed how work was coordinated as the organization developed. Initially embedded in the program offering, digital systems increasingly supported communication, collaboration, implementation monitoring and knowledge sharing across staff, schools, university actors and external stakeholders. As the enterprise expanded, roles and implementation processes became more structured, alongside greater requirements for technological oversight, security and accountability. This was important for replicability as the program introduced new platforms and expanded nationally. Discussion These findings

latest.title: Too crowded to be adventurous: the effect of social crowding on consumer switching behavior
latest.abstract: Introduction Global urbanization has inevitably increased the density of individuals in public spaces, exerting considerable influence on marketing strategies and consumers. Despite expanding research on how consumers are influenced by social crowding, consensus among researchers remains elusive. Drawing on conservation of resources (COR) theory, this research investigates how social crowding affects consumer switching behavior. Methods Across five studies, including a quasi-experimental field study, we examine the effect of social crowding on switching intentions and test risk aversion motivation as an explanatory pathway, as well as shared consumption and crowding aversiveness as boundary conditions. Results Social crowding significantly decreases switching intentions, with η 2 ranging from 0.03 to 0.16. Mediation analyses provide evidence consistent with risk aversion motivation as an explanatory pathway. Importantly, this effect disappears when consumers engage in shared consumption or when the crowding is non-aversive. Discussion These findings offer a resource-based interpretation of consumer responses to crowding. From the COR perspective, maintaining familiar choices may serve a protective function when crowding is appraised as a threat to valued resources. Practically, managers can mitigate the negative effect of crowding on switching behavior by encouraging shared consumption and providing risk-reducing cues.

latest.title: From rights to reality: gender essentialism and subjective wellbeing among LGBTQ+ youth in Buenos Aires
latest.abstract: Argentina may be considered a regional leader in gender and sexual diversity policy, yet relatively little is known about LGBTQ+ adolescents' lived experiences. As a first descriptive step toward addressing this gap, this study examined differences in essentialist beliefs about gender and sexuality and subjective wellbeing among secondary school students in Buenos Aires, comparing LGBTQ+ youth with their non-LGBTQ+ peers. Data were collected through an anonymous self-report questionnaire administered to 1,037 students (ages 16–18) across 21 public and private schools. LGBTQ+ status was derived from independent measures of gender identity and sexual attraction, yielding an estimated LGBTQ+ prevalence of 23.5%, a figure that challenges potential assumptions about the group's representational size in school settings. Results indicate that LGBTQ+ students report significantly lower subjective wellbeing than their non-LGBTQ+ peers, particularly regarding perceived social support and optimism about the future. At the same time, LGBTQ+ students exhibit significantly lower levels of essentialist beliefs about gender and sexuality, both in their normative judgments of gender roles and in their beliefs about the biological basis and immutability of gender and sexual attraction. A control task on shyness showed no group differences. Together, these findings showed the coexistence of lower subjective wellbeing and less essentialist beliefs about gender and sexuality among LGBTQ+ adolescents, within the legal and institutional context prevailing at the time of data collection, highlighting the need to examine how formal rights relate to adolescents' lived experiences of inclusion.

latest.title: Music with monaural beats for anxiety reduction and mood enhancement in individuals with moderate trait-anxiety
latest.abstract: Monaural beats embedded in music are a popular anxiety-relief intervention, yet implementation parameters and efficacy remain poorly understood. Across two studies of online participants with moderate trait anxiety, we tested whether theta-frequency (4–7 Hz) monaural beats in music produce anxiolytic and mood-enhancing effects beyond the same music alone, whether the salience of the beats relative to the music influences effects, and whether the effect of beats generalizes across heterogeneous musical stimuli. State anxiety, valence and arousal were measured before and after a 25-min listening period. In Study 1, participants ( N = 207) were randomly assigned to hear music without beats (Music-Only control) or the same piece with monaural beats blended at three different salience levels: Low-, Moderate-, or High-Beatmix. The Low- and Moderate-Beatmix conditions yielded greater anxiety reductions than Music-Only ( p adjusted = 0.047, β = −0.46, and p adjusted = 0.047, β = −0.46 respectively), whereas Music-Only reduced anxiety more than the High-Beatmix condition ( p adjusted = 0.047, β = 0.42), indicating that overly salient beats might disrupt anxiolytic effects. Time × Condition interactions were not significant for valence or arousal. In Study 2, participants ( N = 259) were randomized to one of four stylistically varied tracks, with or without beats at the Moderate-Beatmix level. Averaged across tracks, Beatmix conditions produced greater anxiety reductions ( p < 0.0001, β = −0.49) and positive-valence increases ( p = 0.029, β = 0.28) than Music-Only. As in Study 1, the Time × Condition interaction was nonsignificant for arousal. These studies provide some of the first evidence that adding monaural beats to music has anxiolytic effects beyond music alone, that effic

latest.title: Building a Culture of Continuous Improvement: A Review of Effective Strategies
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: Continuous improvement (CI) is increasingly recognized as an essential strategy for organizations striving to enhance efficiency, competitiveness, and overall productivity. CI involves a systematic, incremental approach to improvement that emphasizes ongoing refinement rather than drastic, one-time changes. This paper examines a range of strategies for building and sustaining a CI culture, particularly focusing on the role of methodologies like Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and Agile, each with unique attributes conducive to different types of organizations. The study adopts a mixed-method research approach that combines quantitative surveys and qualitative interviews with industry professionals to assess the effectiveness and challenges associated with CI practices. Results indicate that leadership commitment, employee engagement, and a strong feedback system are fundamental to successfully embedding CI within an organization. Findings suggest that CI, when treated as an integral part of the organizational culture, can significantly impact productivity, efficiency, and employee satisfaction. However, the study also identifies several limitations, including potential resistance to change and resource constraints. These findings contribute to the body of knowledge on CI by providing practical insights into the strategies necessary to foster an environment of continuous growth and development.

latest.title: Legislative Reforms in Consumer Protection for the Digital Economy
latest.venue: Journal for Civil and Criminal Law for Legislative Studies (JCCLLS)
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of the digital economy has fundamentally transformed consumer markets, enabling unprecedented access to goods, services, and information across borders. E-commerce platforms, digital payment systems, online marketplaces, and algorithm-driven services now dominate global trade, creating both opportunities and significant risks for consumers. Traditional consumer protection laws, designed for physical marketplaces and localized transactions, struggle to address challenges such as cross-border disputes, data exploitation, platform accountability, algorithmic manipulation, dark patterns, counterfeit goods, and inadequate redress mechanisms. This study examines contemporary legislative reforms aimed at strengthening consumer protection in the digital environment, focusing on emerging legal frameworks that regulate online trade, digital services, and platform responsibilities. Using a doctrinal and analytical research methodology, the study reviews statutes, regulatory policies, judicial decisions, and international guidelines to evaluate how modern legal systems are adapting to digital commerce realities. The research identifies key reform trends, including enhanced transparency requirements, stronger liability for online intermediaries, protection against unfair digital practices, improved dispute resolution mechanisms, data privacy integration, and cross-border cooperation frameworks. It also highlights persistent challenges such as enforcement gaps, jurisdictional conflicts, technological asymmetry between regulators and corporations, and the evolving nature of digital fraud. The findings suggest that effective consumer protection in the digital economy requires a holistic approach combining legal reform, technological regulation, international collabo

latest.title: Evaluating the Role of Data Analysis in Business Process Transformation Projects
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: This study examines the impact of data analysis on business process transformation (BPT) projects, focusing on how analytical insights drive strategic, data-based decisions that improve organizational processes and overall performance. As businesses navigate increasingly competitive environments, BPT projects have emerged as essential tools for enhancing efficiency, agility, and customer satisfaction. Data analysis, which includes techniques like descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics, enables companies to identify improvement opportunities, streamline processes, and enhance decision-making accuracy. The research leverages case studies and qualitative data from industry interviews to highlight the role of data analysis in identifying inefficiencies, predicting market trends, and aligning operations with business goals. Results indicate that organizations employing data analysis in BPT projects are more likely to realize transformative outcomes, though challenges persist, including data quality, integration, and skill gaps.

latest.title: Exploring the Synergy Between Six Sigma and Lean Methodologies in Process Improvement
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: This paper investigates the integration of Six Sigma and Lean methodologies for process improvement in organizational settings. While Six Sigma focuses on reducing process variability through statistical analysis, Lean emphasizes eliminating waste to optimize efficiency. The synergy between these two methodologies, often called Lean Six Sigma, combines their strengths to enhance both efficiency and quality within processes. This study uses simulation-based research to demonstrate how Lean Six Sigma can streamline processes, reduce cycle times, and improve quality. Results indicate that organizations utilizing Lean Six Sigma experience significantly higher efficiency levels, cost reductions, and improved customer satisfaction compared to those using Lean or Six Sigma alone.

latest.title: Optimizing Supply Chain Analytics with SAP S/4 HANA and Data Visualization Tools
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: Supply chain optimization is critical for achieving operational efficiency and reducing costs in today's competitive business environment. SAP S/4 HANA, an enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, offers advanced capabilities for integrating, analyzing, and improving supply chain processes. Combined with modern data visualization tools, businesses can extract actionable insights and enhance decision-making. This paper explores the integration of SAP S/4 HANA with data visualization platforms like Power BI and Tableau to address challenges such as demand forecasting, inventory management, and supplier performance analysis. By leveraging real-time data analytics and intuitive visual representations, organizations can achieve significant performance improvements in their supply chain operations.

latest.title: Measuring the Success of Business Process Reengineering in Cost Reduction and Efficiency
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: Business Process Reengineering (BPR) aims to restructure and radically redesign business processes to achieve significant improvements in cost reduction, efficiency, and productivity. In recent years, companies have increasingly adopted BPR to respond to global competition, technological advancements, and shifting customer expectations. This paper examines the effectiveness of BPR in achieving cost reduction and operational efficiency through a detailed analysis of recent case studies and empirical research. By exploring the impact of BPR on organizational structures, resource utilization, and process workflows, this study highlights key success factors and barriers to BPR implementation. Findings reveal that BPR can yield significant cost savings and efficiency gains, though the success rate heavily depends on organizational readiness, employee engagement, and sustained leadership commitment.

latest.title: Evaluating the Use of Data-Driven KPIs for Operational Excellence in Large Organizations
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: In today’s competitive and rapidly evolving business landscape, large organizations are increasingly turning to data-driven Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) as strategic tools to achieve operational excellence. By leveraging data-driven KPIs, organizations can continuously monitor performance, adjust operations in real-time, and make informed decisions that align with their strategic goals. This study provides a comprehensive examination of the role, effectiveness, and challenges of implementing data-driven KPIs within large organizations. Using a mixed-methods approach involving quantitative analysis of operational metrics and qualitative insights from industry leaders, the research highlights the transformative potential of data-driven KPIs in enhancing productivity, efficiency, and agility. Findings reveal that data-driven KPIs contribute to streamlined processes, improved alignment between operational activities and strategic objectives, and a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. However, challenges such as ensuring data accuracy, achieving seamless integration across departments, and overcoming employee resistance were also identified. Recommendations are offered to optimize KPI implementation, emphasizing data governance and cross-departmental collaboration for maximizing the impact of data-driven KPIs on organizational performance.

latest.title: Environmental, Social and Governance Practices and Corporate Financial Performance
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices have become increasingly relevant to corporate valuation, risk management, investment decisions, and long-term financial sustainability. However, conventional empirical studies frequently treat ESG as a single aggregated score, despite substantial variation in the financial relevance of environmental, social, and governance dimensions. This study proposes an explainable machine-learning framework for examining how individual ESG pillars and firm-level sustainability indicators influence corporate financial performance.The research addresses ESG-score heterogeneity by combining structured financial variables with standardized environmental, social, and governance indicators instead of relying exclusively on a provider-generated aggregate rating. Multiple indicators of corporate financial performance, including profitability, market valuation, capital efficiency, and downside financial risk, are considered to capture heterogeneous economic effects. The proposed framework further investigates nonlinear relationships, interaction effects, and sector-dependent thresholds that may remain undetected in conventional linear ESG–performance models.

latest.title: Review of Data Analytics Applications in Oracle HCM Cloud for Enhancing Employee Experience and Engagement
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: This paper presents an in-depth analysis of the role of data analytics within Oracle Human Capital Management (HCM) Cloud in improving employee experience and engagement. It examines how Oracle HCM Cloud leverages data analytics tools to gain insights into employee satisfaction, engagement levels, and performance metrics. By evaluating previous research and analyzing the functionality of Oracle HCM Cloud’s analytical capabilities, the study highlights data analytics' impact on enhancing employee experience and fostering a productive, engaged workforce. Findings suggest that data-driven HR practices in Oracle HCM Cloud significantly contribute to optimized workforce management and employee alignment with organizational goals, ultimately leading to better retention and satisfaction.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Strategic Approaches to Process Improvement in a Rapidly Changing Business Environment
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: The global business environment is undergoing continuous and rapid changes, primarily driven by advancements in technology, evolving customer expectations, and increasing competitive pressures. To remain competitive, organizations need robust process improvement strategies that enable them to adapt to these changes efficiently. This research investigates strategic approaches that enable effective process improvement, focusing on three core components: adaptability through agile methodologies, efficiency through lean management, and resilience through continuous improvement culture. The study utilizes both quantitative and qualitative methods, analyzing survey responses and conducting interviews across multiple industries. Results indicate that organizations that implement a hybrid approach—combining agile principles, lean strategies, and technology integration—can adapt more readily to change and achieve sustained performance. This paper contributes practical recommendations for managers, shedding light on best practices that can be customized based on industry and organizational structure.

latest.title: Cross-Functional Leadership in Digital Transformation: Impact on ERP and HCM Implementation Success
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: This paper investigates the role of cross-functional leadership in driving successful Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Human Capital Management (HCM) system implementations during digital transformation initiatives. Digital transformation requires an integrated approach, where leaders coordinate across functions to align strategies and foster an adaptive culture. Utilizing a mixed-method approach that includes quantitative data analysis and case studies, this study analyzes how cross-functional teams contribute to better ERP and HCM project outcomes, such as on-time delivery, cost efficiency, and user adoption. Findings suggest that cross-functional leadership, characterized by collaborative, adaptable, and strategic skills, is a critical factor in overcoming project challenges and achieving implementation success. Organizations pursuing digital transformation should prioritize building cross-functional teams with strong leadership to maximize ERP and HCM benefits.

latest.title: Future-Proofing HR Operations with Oracle HCM Cloud’s Continuous Innovation Framework
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: In today's rapidly evolving business landscape, organizations face an increasing need for flexibility, scalability, and efficiency in their Human Resources (HR) operations. The Oracle Human Capital Management (HCM) Cloud has emerged as a pivotal tool for HR professionals seeking to future-proof their operations. Oracle HCM Cloud's Continuous Innovation Framework ensures that HR processes stay aligned with business needs by delivering constant updates, advanced features, and AI-powered capabilities. This manuscript delves into how Oracle HCM Cloud, through its continuous innovation strategy, helps organizations streamline HR tasks, optimize workforce management, and drive business growth. We explore its impact on key HR areas, including recruitment, talent management, payroll, and employee engagement. The paper further discusses the importance of adopting an adaptable HR system that evolves with changing workforce demands and business requirements.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Integrating ERP and HCM Solutions: A Framework for Seamless Data Migration and Process Optimization
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Human Capital Management (HCM) are critical systems within organizations, often requiring integration for improved operational efficiency, optimized data management, and enhanced human resource practices. This paper proposes a structured framework for the seamless integration of ERP and HCM systems, focusing on data migration methodologies, best practices for process optimization, and addressing the common challenges encountered. Through a combination of literature review, case analysis, and methodological recommendations, the study presents a comprehensive approach to achieving a unified system, aiming to enhance data reliability, accessibility, and operational workflows within enterprises.

latest.title: Secure Complaint Intake Systems: Balancing Fraud Detection and Customer Experience
latest.venue: International Journal of Medical Research And Innovation in Applied Science (IJMRIAS)
latest.abstract: Secure complaint intake systems have emerged as critical infrastructures in industries where customer trust, regulatory compliance, and operational transparency are paramount. While digital complaint channels such as online forms, mobile applications, and chatbots have increased accessibility, they have also created opportunities for fraudulent submissions, identity theft, and manipulative complaint practices. Organizations face the dual challenge of ensuring robust fraud detection without compromising customer experience, fairness, and responsiveness. This study explores the architectural frameworks, technological mechanisms, and governance models that underpin secure complaint intake systems. Drawing on multi-sectoral literature, the manuscript highlights the role of advanced analytics, artificial intelligence (AI)-powered fraud detection, and adaptive security controls in safeguarding intake processes. Simultaneously, it examines how human-centered design, trust-building communication, and complaint resolution efficiency contribute to maintaining positive customer experiences. The research underscores that balancing fraud prevention and customer satisfaction requires integrating regulatory compliance, user-centric design, and adaptive intelligence into complaint management platforms.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Client Relationship Management Strategies in ERP and HCM Implementation: Insights from Oracle HCM Projects
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: This study investigates the critical role of client relationship management (CRM) strategies in the successful implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Human Capital Management (HCM) solutions, with a focus on Oracle HCM projects. CRM strategies such as effective communication, customized solutions, comprehensive training, and robust post-implementation support are essential for project success and client satisfaction. By analyzing the impact of these strategies on key project metrics, this paper highlights their significance in achieving alignment between client expectations and project deliverables. Results indicate that a strong CRM approach not only ensures timely project completion but also enhances user adoption and fosters long-term client relationships. Practical recommendations for improving CRM in ERP/HCM implementations are provided, offering valuable insights for practitioners and organizations aiming for project excellence.

latest.title: Oracle HCM Cloud and Employee Self-Service Models: Transforming Workforce Engagement through Digital Solutions
latest.venue: Global Journal of Innovative Research Perspectives (GJIRP)
latest.abstract: The rapid digitization of Human Capital Management (HCM) has enabled organizations to improve workforce engagement and operational efficiency. Oracle HCM Cloud, coupled with Employee Self-Service (ESS) models, exemplifies this shift by providing a robust platform for enhancing employee experience, streamlining HR processes, and fostering a self-sufficient workforce. This paper explores the role of Oracle HCM Cloud and ESS in transforming workforce engagement, analyzing current literature, and employing qualitative research to evaluate the impact of these technologies on employee productivity and satisfaction. Findings suggest that integrating Oracle HCM and ESS results in increased engagement, cost savings, and operational efficiency, highlighting the need for ongoing digital transformation in HR.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Acute Stress Detection through Typing Behaviors, Smartphone Sensors and Machine Learning Techniques
latest.venue: Indian Journal of Science and Technology
latest.abstract: Objectives: To examine whether acute stress can be recognised from smartphone typing behaviour and device motion without wearable sensors, and to identify the classifier family best suited to such data. Method: A browser-based application recorded keystroke events together with accelerometer and gyroscope readings (2 Hz) while 288 participants typed simple number series (calm condition) and mental-arithmetic sequences (stress condition), yielding 2,016 samples. Five keystroke timing features and the inertial features were combined, and ten supervised classifiers were trained and tested on the same stratified 80:20 split using accuracy, AUC and weighted and macro precision, recall and F1-score. Findings: Ensemble methods outperformed the linear, probabilistic, distance-based and neural models. XGBoost achieved the best result, with 89.30% accuracy and an AUC of 95.42%, and Random Forest was close behind (88.72%, 95.32%); Naïve Bayes was weakest (57.98%). Weighted and macro F1 scores of the leading models differed by less than 0.3 points, indicating balanced detection of both classes. The accuracy exceeds the 87.56% reported by the closest smartphone motion-sensor study on 46 participants, and the ranking of XGBoost ahead of Random Forest agrees with recent wearable-sensor studies. Unlike deep models applied to dense physiological signals, the multilayer perceptron performed poorly on these compact behavioural features, which indicates that tree ensembles suit this type of data better. Novelty: Keystroke dynamics and smartphone inertial sensing are combined in one installation-free, synchronised protocol and benchmarked with ten classifiers on a cohort six times larger than the closest smartphone study. Keywords: Acute Stress Detection, Keystroke Dynamics, Smartphone Sens

latest.title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE IN SAUDI FINTECH FIRMS: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF ENTREPRENEURIAL ORIENTATION - A PATH ANALYSIS APPROACH
latest.abstract: This study aims to identify the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on the financial performance of fintech firms in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) and to examine whether entrepreneurial orientation (OE) plays a mediating role in this relationship. A comprehensive survey method was adopted to collect data from all fintech firms licensed in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by the Saudi Arabian Monetary Authority (SAMA), with the study population consisting of 96 companies. A quantitative approach was applied in the data analysis, using path analysis to investigate both the direct and indirect relationships among the study variables. The findings indicate that AI does not have a direct impact on the financial performance of Saudi Fintech Firms. However, an indirect effect emerges when entrepreneurial orientation acts as a mediating variable. This suggests that AI influences financial performance through its effect on entrepreneurial orientation. This study provides scientific and quantitative insights for decision-makers in fintech firms in Saudi Arabia, helping them make sound strategic decisions that enhance overall performance. This understanding can help decision-makers in these firms break traditional stagnation, fostering innovation and growth that contribute to the advancement of the Saudi digital economy.

latest.title: HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS: MODERN TRENDS, PRACTICES & CHALLENGES FOR THE 21ST CENTURY
latest.abstract: Human resource management (HRM) and industrial relations (IR) are undergoing substantial change as organisations respond to digital technologies, global competition, shifting workforce expectations, new employment arrangements and evolving labour regulation. The relationship between these domains is increasingly interdependent: strategic HRM influences recruitment, capability development, performance and employee experience, while industrial relations institutions shape the legitimacy, fairness and sustainability of organisational decisions. This paper examines the principal trends, practices and challenges influencing HRM and IR in the twenty-first century, with particular attention to the Indian employment context and its interaction with global developments. It adopts a structured narrative review of established scholarship, recent peer-reviewed studies and institutional publications. The synthesis identifies five connected areas of change: digital and algorithmic HRM; skills development and employability; employee well-being and inclusion; changing forms of worker representation; and renewed emphasis on social dialogue and workplace governance. The analysis indicates that technology can improve administrative efficiency and decision support, but may also intensify surveillance, reproduce bias and weaken employee autonomy when implemented without transparency and consultation. Similarly, individualised employee engagement cannot fully substitute for collective voice and institutional bargaining. The paper proposes an integrated framework in which responsible HRM, meaningful employee participation and constructive industrial relations jointly support organisational performance, decent work and employment sustainability.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: STRATEGIC INTEGRATION OF HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND MARKETING For SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS PERFORMANCE
latest.abstract: In a current business environment, several companies have understood that they should integrate their human resource management (HRM) and marketing strategies to achieve sustainable business performance. HRM is more about development of employee skills, building commitment and effectiveness of the organization's employees and marketing is more about customer satisfaction, brand value, market competitiveness and long-term customer relationships. The synergic operation of such two functions can lay the foundation for the development and sustainability of an organisation. The purpose of this paper is to analyze the relationship between employee engagement and organizational culture on internal marketing, customer experience and organizational competitiveness and to explain how the integration of HRM and marketing can enhance the sustainable performance of the enterprise. It focuses on the importance of employee motivation, employee talent development as the basis for creating value for both internal and external parties, collaborative leadership and customer-oriented employee practices. The opportunities of cross functional co-ordination for operational efficiency, innovation, strengthening the brand reputation and responsible business practice is also explored in the paper. Organisations can meet new customer expectations and new business needs by providing a combination of human capital development and market-oriented strategies. The study highlights the importance of more than just individual departmental success for sustainable performance; it requires strategies that are integrated with the organisation and which link employee wellbeing with customer value and the longer-term businesses goals. The findings and the discussion should provide some guidance for the manage
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Innovation Direction of Intelligent Products - Research on Personalized Product Design System Based on Generative AI
latest.abstract: In the context of consumption upgrade and intelligent manufacturing, personalized customization has become a core trend in product innovation. Generative AI (AIGC) is gradually a new tool, for the automation product design. This paper puts forward an AI-driven personalized product design system, that integrates engineering constraints and business dimensions. This is built on a diffusion generation model combined with a dual-cycle generative-evaluation architecture, and we use the smart lunch box as an empirical case to verify its feasibility. Through our research, workflow reengineering and quantitative evaluation, our study implecates that the system achieves an engineering feasibility for generated solutions, compared to unconstrained AIGC generation. The design cycle is reduced greatly, representing an efficiency gain. This research not only provides new tools and for product design but also offers a feasible path to achieve mass customization.

latest.title: Breaking Barriers with Skills: Lived Experiences of Women Entrepreneurs to Explore the Skills Behind the Success of Business Stories
latest.venue: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development
latest.abstract: This qualitative study explores the essential entrepreneurship skills that help women run efficient, effective businesses and achieve success. This research employed Heidegger's hermeneutic phenomenology. The study collected data through semi-structured interviews with 36 female service-industry entrepreneurs from July 2026 to August 2026, until data saturation was achieved. The purposive sampling method was employed. Thematic analysis was used to analyze the data and develop themes using NVivo. The results indicate that success in business operations requires a wide range of skills, including financial expertise, leadership, technological proficiency, artificial intelligence, big data analysis, social media management, industry-specific knowledge, adaptability to innovation, creativity, interpersonal skills, emotional intelligence, resilience, time management, networking, and risk management. The results of the study are useful for policymakers, incubation centers, STEVA, TVETA, the Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training, provincial education ministries, and public and private training institutions. Furthermore, this research is beneficial for academic scholars, researchers, and female entrepreneurs. The study uses Martha Nussbaum’s capabilities framework to examine how women entrepreneurs’ skills, agency, real freedoms, and opportunities are shaped by social, cultural, economic, and institutional conditions. By centering women’s lived experiences, it extends the framework beyond business outcomes to examine the skills they draw on to pursue the work and lives they value.

latest.title: Monitoring service operations in digital banking platform ecosystems through theory-guided LLM analytics: Insights into service quality, operational risk, and customer experience
latest.abstract: Digital banking platforms operate as complex service ecosystems involving banks, technology providers, payment infrastructures, and regulators, creating challenges for monitoring service performance, operational risk, and accountability. Understanding how customers evaluate these dimensions remains important to digital service management and technology-adoption research. This study develops a theory-guided large language model–structural equation modeling (LLM–SEM) framework that transforms unstructured customer reviews into theoretically grounded indicators for behavioral analysis. Drawing on UTAUT-3, perceived risk theory, and attribution theory, the framework uses structured chain-of-thought prompting with LLaMA 3.1-8B to extract indicators of service quality, operational risk, customer experience, behavioral outcomes, and actor attribution from customer reviews of leading smart banking applications in Saudi Arabia. The resulting indicators are examined using PLS-SEM and attribution-oriented text mining. Performance expectancy, trust, and hedonic motivation exhibited strong associations with usage experience, which was strongly associated with behavioral intention; behavioral intention, in turn, was strongly associated with recommendation intention. System performance and service delay risks emerged as salient operational-risk correlates of behavioral intention, whereas financial risk showed a limited association. Customers predominantly associated positive and negative service outcomes with the focal platform rather than with banks or regulators. This pattern supports the concept of platform-centered accountability, whereby operational responsibility may be distributed across ecosystem actors while perceived accountability is concentrated on the primary service inte
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Malaysia's silent epidemic: the staggering cost of unhealthy lifestyles
latest.abstract: Introduction Malaysia faces a large and growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) linked to modifiable behavioural risk factors, with substantial implications for healthcare spending and economic productivity. This paper quantifies the current NCD burden attributable to major lifestyle risks in Malaysia and estimates the avertable health and economic gains from aligning population behaviours with World Health Organization (WHO) recommendations. Methods Using the Preventable Risk Integrated ModEl (PRIME), we model the annual number of disease cases attributable to eight behavioural risk factors, including diet (salt, fats, fibre, fruit and vegetables, and free sugars via an energy intake and BMI pathway), physical inactivity, alcohol and tobacco consumption. We then monetise the resulting disease burden using disease-specific direct treatment costs and indirect productivity losses from absenteeism and presenteeism. Results Our estimates indicate a larger NCD-related economic burden than reported in previous Malaysian assessments, although differences in coverage and productivity valuation limit direct comparability. Our research implies that approximately 7.7 million annual disease cases are attributable to the behavioural risks considered, corresponding to a principal estimated economic burden of about USD 41.9 billion (USD 14.8 billion in direct costs and USD 27.1 billion in indirect costs). Excess sugar intake, high salt consumption, and smoking account for the largest shares of this attributable burden. Under a counterfactual in which dietary and activity patterns meet WHO guidelines and smokers fully substitute combustible cigarettes with lower-exposure non-combustible alternatives, we estimate that roughly 647,000 disease cases and USD 3.7 billion in annua
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: COMPARATIVE GOVERNANCE OF DIGITAL PLATFORMS AND AI-DRIVEN CARTELISATION: TOWARDS COMPETITION POLICY FRAMEWORK FOR VIKSIT BHARAT
latest.abstract: Digital platforms have become the principal infrastructure through which contemporary commerce, communication, and information flow. Their intermediary position, combined with data accumulation and network effects, generates durable market power that traditional ex-post competition law struggles to discipline within meaningful time frames. The rise of algorithmic pricing compounds this difficulty by enabling forms of coordination that do not require explicit human agreement, thereby straining the doctrinal foundations of both Section 3 of the Competition Act, 2002 and Article 101 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. This article undertakes a comparative analysis of the governance frameworks adopted in India, the European Union, the United States, and the United Kingdom, and examines the distinct typologies of algorithmic collusion identified in the economic and legal literature. It concludes by proposing institutional and doctrinal reforms suited to India's Viksit Bharat @2047 objectives, arguing for a calibrated hybrid model that combines ex-ante gatekeeper regulation with strengthened ex-post enforcement and algorithmic accountability mechanisms.

latest.title: Data-Driven Economic Intelligence Framework for Future Market Analysis and Policy Planning
latest.abstract: As more economic data and market intelligence become available, there is greater scope for enhancing future market analysis and policy formulation. Economic data analysis, market forecasting, risk assessment, and policy analysis are currently undertaken separately, hence their inability to act as integrated tools for decision-making. In this study, a Data-Driven Economic Intelligence Framework is proposed where economic data analysis, market intelligence, forecasting, scenarios analysis, and policy formulation are brought together under one integrated analytical framework. The framework assesses four factors; Economic Activity, Market Outlook, Risk Level, and Policy Readiness which will be used to compute Economic Intelligence Index. Four scenarios, Baseline, Growth, Risk, and Policy Adjustment, will be used to analyze future economic conditions. The findings of this illustration show that the Growth scenario shows high economic activity and market outlook while the Risk scenario exhibits poor market performance and high-risk level. The Policy Adjustment scenario indicates improved market environment as well as policy readiness in the best case. It is evident from the results obtained that integrated economic intelligence would help in detecting risk, analyzing market opportunities, forecasting and implementing policies. The suggested framework serves as an effective structure for decision-making in changed economic environment by governments, investors, and companies. Further research on validating the framework using actual data and improvement in forecasting via artificial intelligence and real-time economic information would be valuable.

latest.title: Do the Corporate Governance Framework Mechanism Affect Sustainability Reporting in Food Beverage Companies?
latest.venue: Journal of Accounting Finance Taxation and Auditing (JAFTA)
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of corporate governance mechanisms on sustainability reporting within food and beverage (F&B) companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2021–2024 period. The research is motivated by increasing stakeholder demands for transparency regarding environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosures, as well as the significance of sustainability reporting as a form of legitimacy for a company’s internal responsibilities—reflected in its business strategy and long-term sustainability. The study utilizes secondary data obtained from companies' financial and sustainability reports. Panel data regression analysis is employed to test the impact of the independent variables—specifically corporate governance mechanisms, comprising board size, the presence of female directors, independent directors, and foreign directors—on sustainability reporting. The findings indicate that corporate governance mechanisms do not influence the level of sustainability reporting. None of the governance variables were found to have a significant effect on promoting sustainability reporting within these companies. Consequently, the implementation of corporate governance roles, particularly within the F&B sector, has yet to effectively enhance sustainability reporting. Keywords: sustainability reporting; female, independent and foreign directors; ESC.

latest.title: Circular Economy and Agricultural Decarbonization: An Integrated Multilevel Governance and Implementation Framework in Brazil
latest.abstract: Agriculture is the foundation of food systems but faces growing challenges. According to the United Nations, 40% of the world’s land is already degraded, affecting both agricultural productivity and global food security. This study aimed to conduct an integrative literature review and a documentary analysis to map the evolution of international and national frameworks, highlighting their contributions to the Brazilian agribusiness. The methodology was based on a systematic literature review, crossing data from scientific databases (Scopus, Web of Science) with primary legal regulations. The analysis showed that the Brundtland Report (1987) and the Paris Agreement (2015) laid the foundations for sustainable development and shaped policies such as emissions accounting mechanisms. Focusing on the Brazilian context, the National Circular Economy Strategy and the Ecological Transformation Plan (2025) establish guidelines for integrating circular practices into the sector, including the use of organic waste, reverse logistics, bioeconomy, and agri-food systems. The ISO 59000 family standard and PR2030 Recommended Practice provide technical frameworks for measuring and standardizing circularity in agro-industrial chains. The discussion converges on a conceptual proposal of a multilevel framework specifically designed for the Brazilian regulatory scenario. However, gaps remain regarding traceability, the integration of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), and circularity metrics. It is expected that legal and regulatory coordination offers strategic opportunities to reposition agribusiness as a driver of the circular economy and decarbonization.

latest.title: PRICING STRATEGY OPTIMIZATION FOR TRADITIONAL SCENTED CANDLE PRODUCTS IN DIFFERENTIATED LUXURY GOODS MARKETS
latest.abstract: Pricing strategy was a factor of competitive advantage in the markets for luxury goods in which product value, brand and differentiation are determinants of consumer’s choices. The approach may allow premium positioning and competitive advantage. This research investigates Pricing Strategy Optimization (PSO) for traditional scented candles, focusing on Consumer Price Perception (CPP), Brand Equity (BE), Sales Volume (SV), Customer Retention (CR), and Overall Market Performance (OMP).
