latest.title: What is compassion connected to, and does it differ by gender and age? A network analysis of compassion, self-compassion, mindfulness, empathy and mental health
latest.abstract: Abstract Compassion is an emotional state experienced in response to witnessing the suffering of others, accompanied by an internal motivation to help. When directed toward the self, it is referred to as self-compassion. Previous research suggests that compassion and self-compassion are closely related to mindfulness and empathy, contributing to reductions in anxiety and depression and to the enhancement of positive affect. Accordingly, this study employed network analysis to explore the complex structure of interactions among these psychological variables. A total of 1,020 Korean adults completed measures of compassion, self-compassion, mindfulness, empathy, well-being, and negative affect (depression, anxiety, and stress). An EBICglasso network was estimated in R (version 4.5.1). Centrality indices were computed, and subgroup networks were constructed by gender and age to compare structural differences. The results showed that compassion was closely connected to empathy, whereas self-compassion was more strongly linked to mindfulness and well-being; the capacities to feel, tolerate, and alleviate suffering emerged as central nodes. In the gender-based networks, compassion and self-compassion among men tended to be organized primarily around cognitive factors, whereas women exhibited a pattern in which the behavioral motivation for compassion was activated relatively immediately, even in the absence of emotional responding. In the age-based networks, the influence of suffering tolerance was most pronounced in middle-aged adults, while the role of empathy diminished and the role of mindfulness expanded in older adults. By examining compassion at the level of its constituent elements and visualizing the interaction structure among related variables, this study provides a

latest.title: Pemanfaatan Microsoft Excel Dalam Pengelolaan Keuangan Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) Perspektif Hukum Ekonomi Syariah
latest.abstract: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) need orderly financial records to monitor business activities, assess performance, and make responsible economic decisions. For Muslim-owned or sharia-oriented MSMEs, financial administration also has a normative dimension: transactions should be recorded transparently, agreements should be clear, and business practices should avoid riba, gharar, and maysir. This article examines the use of Microsoft Excel in MSME financial management from the perspective of Islamic economic law. It applies a descriptive qualitative literature-review method combined with a normative-conceptual analysis of sharia business principles, relevant regulations, and studies on spreadsheet-based accounting and sharia-oriented MSMEs. The literature indicates that Excel can assist transaction recording, cash-flow monitoring, cost calculation, inventory control, and preparation of financial summaries. From an Islamic economic law perspective, these functions may support the principles of amanah, shiddiq, ‘adl, transparency, and protection of wealth (hifz al-mal), provided that the workbook records the substance of transactions accurately. For transactions using contracts such as murabahah, mudharabah, musyarakah, or ijarah, the records should identify the contract, parties, object, price or capital contribution, agreed margin or profit-sharing ratio, payment schedule, and outstanding obligations as relevant. Excel itself does not certify sharia compliance; that assessment depends on the validity of the contract and the actual conduct of the parties. The article concludes that Excel is a practical initial tool for MSMEs when supported by clear procedures, adequate user knowledge, internal checks, and accounting treatment appropriate to the transaction and

latest.title: Pengaruh Economic Value Added, Earning Per Share, dan Ukuran Perusahaan Terhadap Kelayakan Investasi Saham pada Perusahaan Sektor Telekomunikasi yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of Economic Value Added (EVA), Earnings Per Share (EPS), and firm size on stock investment feasibility in telecommunications companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2022–2025. Stock investment feasibility is proxied by the Price Earnings Ratio (PER). This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from quarterly financial statements. The population consists of 17 telecommunications companies, from which 11 companies were selected through purposive sampling based on the availability of complete quarterly financial statements. The final dataset comprises 176 observations. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, t-tests, and an F-test with IBM SPSS Statistics version 25. The results show that EVA, EPS, and firm size each have a positive and statistically significant effect on PER. Simultaneously, the three independent variables have a significant effect on PER. The coefficient of determination indicates that approximately 34.3% of the variation in PER is explained by EVA, EPS, and firm size, while the remaining variation is explained by other factors outside the research model. These findings suggest that investors may consider value creation, earnings per share, and company scale as part of fundamental analysis when assessing telecommunications stocks.

latest.title: Making Sense of Employee Performance in Digital Workplaces_An Interpretative Phenomenological Study of Psychological Safety and Digital Orientation
latest.venue: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study explores how employees make sense of performance in digital workplaces through their lived experiences of psychological safety and digital orientation. Adopting a qualitative Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) approach, the study draws on in-depth interviews with eight employees working in organizations that have implemented digitally enabled work practices in Indonesia. The findings reveal three interconnected dimensions of employees' experiences. First, psychological safety provides an interpersonal environment that encourages employees to express ideas, ask questions, and learn from mistakes without fear of negative consequences. Second, digital orientation shapes employees' understanding of performance through technological adaptability, digital collaboration, and the continuous development of digital competencies. Third, the interaction between these conditions influences employees' ability to translate their digital capabilities into meaningful workplace contributions. Building on these findings, the study proposes Safe Digital Actualization as an emerging conceptual proposition, explaining how psychological safety and digital orientation converge in shaping employees' understanding and actualization of performance. The study contributes to the literature on organizational behavior and strategic human resource management by highlighting the importance of integrating psychological support with digital capability development in increasingly digitalized workplaces.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Understanding mathematics anxiety and its impact on cognitive effort in second-grade children: a pupillometry investigation
latest.abstract: Introduction Many individuals struggle with mathematics, and mathematics anxiety (MA) is associated with poor mathematics performance. The reasons for this association are unclear, but one explanation is that MA reduces the working memory capacity available for problem solving. Because changes in pupil diameter index cognitive effort, this study used pupillometry to examine whether MA is related to cognitive effort in second-grade children. Methods Ninety-eight second-grade pupils in Norway solved easy and hard addition problems while their pupil diameter was recorded with an eye tracker. Arithmetic competence, working memory, and general intelligence were measured as control variables, and the data were analysed with linear mixed models. Results Hard problems elicited more cognitive effort than easy problems. MA moderated this effect: children with higher MA showed a smaller increase in cognitive effort with increasing problem difficulty, even after controlling for arithmetic competence, working memory, and general intelligence. When only correctly solved trials were analysed, the interaction was no longer significant, but higher MA was associated with lower overall cognitive effort. Discussion Children with higher MA did not show the heightened effort predicted by working memory interference accounts; the pattern may instead reflect reduced task engagement or avoidance. Because pupil diameter change indexes overall psychophysiological effort, the precise cognitive and affective mechanisms remain unclear.

latest.title: Optimal marital strategies: how couples develop successful interaction styles
latest.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences
latest.abstract: Abstract The study of marriage dynamics and of strategies to reduce the likelihood of divorce has been an important research area for many years. Gottman's (Gottman. 1993 J. Consult. Clin. Psychol. 61, 6–15. (doi:10.1037/0022-006X.61.1.6)) research on successful marriages revealed three matched interaction styles: conflict-avoiding, validating and volatile. There has, however, been little progress in explaining how couples develop these styles of interaction and why failure to do so leads to failed marriages. In this paper, we show that these interaction styles arise as solutions to an optimal control problem where spouses jointly maximize a common goal. The validating style arises when the benefit from achieving joint happiness is balanced by the emotional cost of adopting a particular style. The ubiquitous conflict-avoider style arises naturally when spouses do not care about emotional costs. The volatile style is not an optimal solution, but volatile marriages may still be successful for spouses with highly positive natural dispositions. The problem of the spouses having different goals in marriage is relevant to marriage repair, and this problem will be studied in a later paper using differential game theory.

latest.title: Sudden Gains and Losses in Personality Change Interventions: Predictors, Outcomes, and Implications for Individualized Personality Change
latest.abstract: Recent research suggests that volitional personality change is possible through structured interventions, yet little is known about the temporal dynamics of such change. In psychotherapy, sudden gains—abrupt, substantial improvements between sessions—are robust predictors of treatment success. Based on 448 participants who completed a 12-week personality intervention, we examined whether similar sudden shifts occur in the context of volitional personality change and whether they explain differences in trait, life satisfaction, and self-esteem changes from the pre-test to the follow-up 3 months later. We compared four different measures for detecting shifts: daily and weekly personality states, generic change factors (e.g., gaining insight), and subjective progress. Sudden gains were relatively common and—with the exception of daily states—consistently associated with improvements in the targeted traits, life satisfaction, and self-esteem. Sudden gains in weekly states co-occurred with increased intervention engagement and key change processes such as gaining insight and practicing new behaviors—paralleling mechanisms found in psychotherapy. In contrast, sudden losses were less frequent and showed no meaningful negative effects for trait changes or life satisfaction. However, high dropout rates may have masked more consequential losses. These findings challenge the assumption that personality change is exclusively gradual and underscore the value of capturing dynamic, within-person fluctuations. Monitoring and leveraging such shifts may help to personalize interventions and optimize their impact. Future research should explore how sudden gains can be intentionally triggered and how interventions can be designed to support lasting change through both gradual and sudden pa

latest.title: Co-navigating care for emotional distress in South Asian men with long-term conditions: a qualitative study of patient and GP perspectives in UK primary care
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Men of South Asian (SA) origin in the UK have increased rates of long-term conditions (LTCs) and mental health problems, yet are less likely to seek help from NHS services, and Pakistani men in particular report the lowest recovery rates in NHS Talking Therapies. Co-occurring physical and mental health problems are associated with poorer outcomes. Research examining help-seeking in SA men with LTCs experiencing emotional distress is limited. Understanding this is essential to addressing inequalities in access to, experience of, and outcomes from primary care mental health support. Methods This qualitative study used online semi-structured interviews analysed through reflexive thematic analysis, underpinned by a critical realist epistemology. Participants were SA men with diabetes or coronary heart disease ( n = 17) and general practitioners (GPs) working in practices serving higher density SA populations ( n = 18), across three UK regions. Most patient participants were Muslim and first generation. Participants were recruited through community and faith centres, social media, and snowball sampling. A Patient Advisory Group of SA men was involved throughout. Results Two overarching themes were developed: (1) trust and mistrust, in primary care and in culturally-based support, and (2) co-navigating care, negotiating health beliefs between GPs and patients. SA men in our study described avoiding NHS services for emotional distress because of perceived over-medicalisation, experiences of discrimination, and divergent health beliefs, turning instead to faith-based support, family, and self-management. Both patients and GPs described the need for care that engages with patients’ cultural and religious health beliefs, built through relational continuity. Co

latest.title: A 2-layered game-theoretic deep learning model for predicting lodging demand: SHAP and nash equilibrium
latest.venue: Journal of Revenue and Pricing Management
latest.abstract: Abstract Forecasting tourism demand is critical for pricing and revenue management, yet most advanced machine learning models operate as “black boxes,” limiting interpretability and trust. This study introduces an explainable, game-theoretic hybrid deep learning framework for predicting short-term rental demand. This study incorporates game theory in two layers: a cooperative game and a competitive game. Using 729,888 daily observations from 1,852 Airbnb listings in Ann Arbor, Michigan, we compare traditional models (regression, SARIMAX) with advanced architectures (FCNN, LSTM, Transformer, and a Transformer–LSTM hybrid). Game theory is used in two layers: cooperative game (SHAP) and competitive game (classic Nash equilibrium). SHAP creates an explainable deep learning model to quantify each feature’s contribution. The best-performing model (FCNN) was further used to simulate a 3x3 pricing game between pairs within 4 submarkets. Results show that deep learning models significantly outperform traditional baselines, while SHAP-based feature attribution and clustering enhance transparency and strategic insight. The competitive games shed light on the characteristics and dynamics of each submarket. This research offers insights to revenue managers, policymakers, and operators.

latest.title: Childhood Emotional Abuse and Neuroimaging Findings: A Scoping Review
latest.abstract: Background Childhood emotional abuse (CEA) is the most prevalent subtype of childhood maltreatment globally, yet it remains the least detected due to its lack of physical markers. While neuroimaging research on childhood maltreatment broadly has implicated the prefrontal cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, and fronto-limbic networks, evidence specific to CEA has not been systematically mapped. Objectives This scoping review aimed to map the existing neuroimaging evidence on childhood emotional abuse, covering study characteristics, approaches to measuring CEA, neuroimaging modalities used, and key neurobiological findings. Methods Following JBI guidance, the PCC framework, and PRISMA-ScR reporting standards, a systematic search was conducted across Scopus and PubMed/MEDLINE with no restriction on publication year. Eligible studies used human samples with history of CEA, employed at least one neuroimaging modality (MRI, fMRI, EEG, PET, DTI, or MEG), and reported original quantitative findings. Results Nineteen articles published between 2010 and 2025 were included, predominantly from the Netherlands and the United States (14 of 19 studies), with no studies from Southeast Asia, Africa, Latin America, or Middle East. The Childhood Trauma Questionnaire was the most widely used measurement instrument (63%). Structural findings most consistently showed reduced dorsomedial prefrontal cortex volume, while functional findings revealed a paradoxical amygdala pattern: hyperactivation to emotional stimuli in task-based studies, alongside reduced connectivity in resting-state and seed-based analyses. No studies used EEG, PET, or MEG. Key gaps identified included measurement heterogeneity, geographic bias, absence of longitudinal designs, cohort clustering (notably NESDA and DASH), and li

latest.title: Financial Wellbeing and the Influencing Socioeconomic Factors: Evidence from Australian Regional Households
latest.venue: Journal of risk and financial management
latest.abstract: Financial wellbeing generally refers to people’s perception of current financial stability, their readiness to handle emergencies, and their confidence to cope financially in the future. However, financial wellbeing studies in Australia have commonly focused on urban population centres rather than regional areas. Given the far-reaching impact of financial wellbeing on people’s financial health, a clearer understanding of financial wellbeing and its influencing factors is pivotal in enhancing people’s financial wellbeing level in the regional areas as well as in the urban ones. Given this need, this study aims to identify influencing factors that will impact the state of financial wellbeing in rural Queensland—the North Burnett Region. Using the CFPB Financial Well-Being Scale and the survey method, this study finds that older people tend to enjoy a higher level of financial wellbeing as compared to younger people; financial wellbeing level improves when moving from unemployed status to full-time employed status; higher incomes are associated with higher financial wellbeing levels; investment property owners tend to have higher financial wellbeing than non-property owners; and financial wellbeing is higher for people who are satisfied with government and non-government financial support. This study also finds lower financial wellbeing levels amongst Indigenous families. The findings will have implications for the policymakers and financial advisors who assist Australian regional communities, especially young generations, Indigenous people, low-income households, and unemployed people, in sustaining their finances.

latest.title: Non-linear association of social jetlag with depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation: mediation and age/sex heterogeneity in an exploratory cross-sectional study
latest.abstract: Abstract Objectives This study examined the nonlinear associations between social jetlag (SJL), depressive symptoms, and suicidal ideation. It also tested whether inflammatory markers and depressive symptoms mediated these associations. Stratified analyses by age and sex were performed. Methods Data came from 5,838 adults in the 2017–2020 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Restricted cubic splines were used to model nonlinear relationships. Mediation analyses assessed the roles of an inflammatory burden index (CRP and neutrophil‑to‑lymphocyte ratio) and depressive symptoms. All analyses were stratified by age group and sex. Results A near U‑shaped association emerged. Zero SJL corresponded to the highest depressive symptom scores. Mild‑to‑moderate SJL (> 0 to < 2 hours) was linked to lower scores, whereas severe SJL was linked to elevated scores. This pattern was strongest in young adults (20–39 years). Among women, moderate SJL was associated with a 65% reduction in the odds of suicidal ideation, compared with no SJL. Mediation analyses showed that depressive symptoms accounted for 25.2% of the SJL–suicidal ideation association. The inflammatory burden index did not mediate this association. Conclusions Mild‑to‑moderate SJL may have certain beneficial associations with mental health outcomes in specific subgroups. The overall SJL–mental health relationship is nonlinear. The mediating pathway operates primarily through depressive symptoms, not systemic inflammation.

latest.title: Exploring the influence of socio-cultural contexts on the resilience of young women attending an all-female college in New Delhi, India
Remaking “The Unconscious” Paradigm, Act I: ...The Gap” Between Subliminal Processing and the Unconscious “Mind...
latest.abstract: Abstract The notion of subliminal processing often refers to perception that takes place below the threshold of conscious visual awareness. This is suggested to lead to behavioural and emotional changes with spontaneous and actionable evolutionary-survival and/or social-adaptation response value. Therefore, it has been suggested that the presentation of imperceptible visual elicitors can lead to responses, such as skin-conductance and heart-rate, and facial-emotional, and participant behavioural and self-report changes without conscious awareness. In a series of experiments, we disproved this theory. We showed that individually-adjusted, truly imperceptible elicitors did not induce any of these changes, when using null-hypothesis-testing, and, furthermore, provided evidence for null responses, when using Bayesian analyses. We proceeded to a series of novel and exploratory experiments on unconscious theory. We tested whether behavioural and emotional responses were reported to precede conscious awareness using overt presentations of visual-emotional elicitors. We showed evidence that the experience of physiological-emotional responses was reported to precede conscious awareness of a perceived visual-emotional content. These early responses were automatic and involuntary; they did not involve or require conscious access, or accessibility, and deliberation, and could not be physiologically restrained by conscious instruction for inhibition. We proposed that responses that can be termed unconscious, but not subliminal, are preceding, spontaneous and conditionally uninhibited experiential components of exposure to perceived, but not imperceptible, emotional elicitors. We extended that they involve genuine evolutionary-survival and social-adaptation value, compared to so-call

latest.title: When Do Family Firms “Walk the Talk” in Sustainability? The Role of Socioemotional Wealth
latest.abstract: A central debate concerns under which conditions sustainability orientation—a firm’s attitudinal disposition toward creating social and environmental value alongside economic value—translates into concrete environmental practices in some family firms but not others. Drawing on socioemotional wealth (SEW) theory, we argue that specific socioemotional priorities shape whether family firms “walk the talk” in their environmental practices. Using survey data from 182 Turkish family firms, we find that sustainability orientation is more strongly associated with environmental practices when owning families emphasize preserving the business across generations (renewal of family bonds), but not when they show stronger emotional attachment to the firm.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Online Game-based Learning via LINE Application to Enhance Parts of Speech Skills of High School Students with Hearing Impairment in the 21st Century
latest.venue: Journal of Applied Informatics and Technology
latest.abstract: This study aimed to develop and evaluate an online game-based learning tool via LINE application to enhance English parts of speech skills among high school students with hearing impairments. The research objectives were to: (1) develop the online educational game, (2) assess its efficiency, (3) compare students' pre- and post-learning achievement, (4) examine students' learning progress, and (5) investigate the relationship between post-learning achievement and student satisfaction. The sample consisted of 27 high school students with hearing impairments from Surin School for the Deaf during the first semester of the 2024 academic year, selected through purposive sampling. Research instruments included the developed online game, pre- and post-tests, and a satisfaction survey. Data were analyzed using a dependent t-test, Pearson's correlation, percentages, and mean scores. The development process yielded 8 learning units and 109 online games. The system demonstrated high functionality, with an efficiency ratio of 1.46, exceeding McGuigan's criterion of 1.00. A significant improvement in students' post-test scores compared to pre-test scores was observed (p < 0.05). The average learning gain was 15.59%, which was lower than the hypothesized 50%. A significant positive correlation was found between student satisfaction and post-learning achievement (p < 0.05). These findings suggest that the developed online game-based learning tool effectively enhances English language skills among students with hearing impairments, offering insights into innovative educational approaches for this population.

latest.title: Mudharabah adoption as institutional risk governance: evidence from coastal livelihoods in Indonesia
latest.venue: Journal of Islamic accounting and business research
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the adoption of mudharabah financing in high-risk coastal livelihoods by reframing Islamic financial contracts as instruments of institutional risk governance rather than purely normative or religious arrangements. It seeks to explain how institutional processes shape adoption decisions under conditions of environmental and income uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design is employed using survey data from 440 coastal economic actors in Indonesia. The proposed framework is tested through a serial mediation model using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Multi-group analysis is further applied to capture contextual variations across geographic settings and fishing-asset ownership structures. Findings The findings indicate that access to capital and perceived fairness do not directly influence the intention to adopt mudharabah. Their effects are fully transmitted through a sequential institutional pathway involving the institutional role of Islamic financial intermediaries, risk-management practices addressing weather and price volatility and the formation of institutional trust. Multi-group analysis reveals that these institutional pathways are significantly stronger in mainland coastal areas and among individual asset owners, suggesting that institutional risk governance operates unevenly across contexts. Practical implications The results suggest that strengthening mudharabah adoption requires more than expanding access or emphasizing Shariah compliance. Islamic financial institutions should prioritize institutional capacity for risk governance, including contract clarity, distributive fairness and operational risk-management mechanisms, particularly in vulnerable coastal environ

latest.title: THE ROLE OF INVESTMENT AND INFRASTRUCTURE AS KEY DRIVERS OF A TRANSFORMING DIGITAL ECONOMY
latest.abstract: This study examines the development of the digital economy by presenting an analysis and a series of proposals. Advancing production and management processes generally relies on artificial intelligence, data analytics, and cloud computing. Russia is one of the nations striving for digital innovation— despite facing various challenges—and consistently seeks to achieve an advanced level of technological capability. The study identifies the factors influencing growth, as well as infrastructural obstacles and through role of skills and expertise on rise professional grоwth. The availability of investment, a clear methodology, proper organization, and workforce training all contribute to accelerating the digital transformation.

latest.title: Quantifying ‘surprise’ in capuchin monkeys ( Sapajus apella )
latest.abstract: Abstract Violation-of-expectation (VoE) events offer a fascinating lens into the intersection of cognition and emotion. Research suggests that, like humans, many animals are susceptible to VoE events in many physical domains, susceptibility typically assessed through behaviours such as visual and physical exploration of a stimulus. In humans, such susceptibility has been further documented through emotional surprise, such as delight following positive surprise and frustration following negative surprise. However, evidence in animals remains relatively limited. To address this gap, this study examined behavioural, cognitive and emotional responses of capuchin monkeys (Sapajus apella) to bait-and-switch VoE events of food items. Capuchins were chosen for this study not only for their exploratory and information-seeking behaviours, but also for known emotional responses to VoE events (e.g. frustration following inequity aversion). Contrary to prior research, this study found no evidence for violation susceptibility via behavioural, cognitive or emotional responses. Overall, such findings contribute valuable information to the VoE literature in primates regarding methodology and information salience, as well as underscore the current challenges of investigating emotional surprise in animals. Future research may benefit from establishing stronger expectations (e.g. more salient stimuli), to better investigate and quantify surprise to VoE events in animal species such as capuchin monkeys.

latest.title: The role of ESG practices in mitigating stock market risk duringthe Palestinian-Israeli conflict: An event study in China
latest.abstract: Aim: This study aimed to investigate the impact of the Palestinian-Israeli conflict on the China A-shares market, and the role of environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices in companies’ risk mitigation. Methodology: An event study methodology was employed to analyse the effect of the conflict on the A-shares market. The analysis was conducted using cumulative average abnormal returns (CAAR) for 5,041 companies across multiple trading days post-event. Additionally, multiple linear regression models were utilised to explore the relationship between cumulative abnormal returns (CAR), companies’ financial performance, and their ESG scores. Results: The empirical results revealed significantly negative CAAR on the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 10th trading days post-event, indicating a negative impact of this conflict on the A-shares market. The regression results further demonstrated a negative relationship between CAR and companies’ financial performance, while CAR and ESG scores remained consistently positive. Implications and recommendations: The findings suggest that during geopolitical conflicts the market may experience heightened panic, adversely affecting stock returns, however companies with strong ESG governance tended to exhibit more stable stock returns. These results offer insights for both researchers and practitioners concerning the role of ESG practices in mitigating the adverse effects of geopolitical conflicts on stock returns. Originality/value: This study provides new evidence on the resilience of companies with strong ESG governance during geopolitical conflicts, contributing to the understanding of the interplay between ESG practices and stock market performance in geopolitical conflicts.

latest.title: Peran Pendidikan Kewirausahaan, Lingkungan Keluarga, Lingkungan Sosial Terhadap Intensi Berwirausaha Dengan Efikasi Diri Sebagai Variabel Mediasi
latest.abstract: In supporting the accomplishment of Indonesia Emas 2045, the part of MSMEs is required. In any case, when connected to the tall unemployment rate in Indonesia, which is 7.2 million individuals, it implies that there are still numerous understudies who discover it troublesome to discover work. One way to decrease the unemployment rate is by cultivating entrepreneurial eagerly among understudies. This think about points to analyze the impact of business instruction, family environment, and social environment on entrepreneurial aim, with self-efficacy as a mediating variable. The sort of investigate is informative inquire about. The populace utilized for this consider comprises of understudies who have completed enterprise instruction at colleges within the northern and eastern parts of Bandung City. The testing procedure utilized non-probability inspecting with a purposive inspecting approach, and information collection was conducted through the dissemination of surveys. The collected information were prepared and analyzed utilizing the Shrewd PLS application. The comes about of this consider show that the parts of business instruction, family environment, and social environment emphatically and altogether impact entrepreneurial expectation, with self-efficacy as a mediating variable

latest.title: Analisis Kekurangan Muatan (Cargo Shortage) Akibat Perubahan Draft pada MV. Andhika Shakilla
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the loss of cargo (cargo shortage) due to changes in draft on the MV. Andhika Shakilla during coal loading activities in the anchorage area. This problem arises due to the difference between the amount of cargo recorded in the cargo document and the results of the draught survey calculation, thus potentially giving rise to claims, financial losses, and reducing the trust of parties involved in shipping activities. This study uses a descriptive qualitative method with a case study approach. Data collection was carried out through direct observation on board the ship, interviews with parties involved in operational activities, documentation, and literature studies. The results show that changes in draft are influenced by several factors, namely ballast conditions, fuel and freshwater consumption, cargo distribution, water density, tides, trim, list, and inaccuracies in reading draft numbers. In addition, differences in measurement procedures between the loading port and the discharge port can cause an apparent cargo shortage or apparent lack of cargo. The impacts are not only technical, but also administrative and financial, such as differences in cargo calculations, claims from related parties, and economic losses. Therefore, it is necessary to strengthen the implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for draught surveys, increase monitoring of ship conditions prior to measurements, and provide regular training to crews to improve accuracy in draught surveys. This will minimize the risk of cargo shortages and improve the accuracy of cargo calculations.

latest.title: Transforming Sustainability Into Customer Loyalty: Strategic Role of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Capability in Indonesian Manufacturing Industri
latest.venue: Journal of Business Social and Technology
latest.abstract: Background: Sustainability-based practices are increasingly relevant to business-to-business manufacturing, but their contribution to customer loyalty remains uncertain. Objective: This study examines Sustainability-Based Practices, Customer Satisfaction, Customer Loyalty, and Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Capability in Indonesian manufacturing relationships. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional survey of procurement decision-makers was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Results: Sustainability-Based Practices positively influence Customer Satisfaction (β = 0.378; p < 0.001), and Customer Satisfaction positively influences Customer Loyalty (β = 0.312; p = 0.030). The direct relationship between Sustainability-Based Practices and Customer Loyalty is not significant (β = 0.096; p = 0.458). CRM Capability does not significantly moderate either proposed relationship (p = 0.675 and p = 0.286). The reported indirect effect concerns CRM Capability through Customer Satisfaction (β = 0.109; p = 0.050), which is borderline under the stipulated p < 0.05 criterion and does not establish mediation of sustainability effects. Conclusion: Customer satisfaction is associated with the relational value of sustainability practices, but sustainability does not directly predict loyalty in the reported model. Manufacturing suppliers should connect sustainability initiatives with customer-relevant performance. Interpretation requires caution because of measurement-validity concerns and unavailable verification of the original indirect-effect output.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: THE EFFECT OF CAR, NPL, LDR, AND BOPO ON NET INTEREST MARGIN (NIM) IN DIGITAL BANKS IN INDONESIA FOR THE 2021-2026 PERIOD
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital banking in Indonesia has intensified competition and put pressure on early-stage profitability. This study examines the effect of the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), Non-Performing Loan (NPL), Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR), and Operating Expenses to Operating Income (BOPO) on the Net Interest Margin (NIM), with the Net Operating Margin (NOM) as its Islamic-banking counterpart, of digital banks in Indonesia over the 2021Q4-2026Q1 period. The study is grounded in the dealership model of bank interest margins and the Risk-Based Bank Rating (RGEC) framework. A balanced panel of six digital banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange is analysed, yielding 108 quarterly observations estimated in EViews 12 with robust standard errors. Following the Chow and Hausman tests, the Random Effects Model is adopted as the main specification, with the Fixed Effects Model reported as a robustness check. The results show that BOPO has a negative and significant effect on the margin, while CAR, NPL, and LDR are not significant. The findings indicate that operating efficiency, rather than capital adequacy, asset quality, or liquidity, is the dominant determinant of the margin at the current stage of digital-banking development in Indonesia. Digital banks are therefore encouraged to strengthen cost efficiency through technology optimisation and process automation.

latest.title: AI Self-Efficacy and Transformational Leadership on Innovative Work Behavior: The Mediating Role of Work Engagement Among Jakarta Hotel Employees
latest.venue: Journal of Business Social and Technology
latest.abstract: Background: Amid ongoing technological change, the hospitality sector relies more on the innovative work behavior (IWB) of its employees to stay competitive; nevertheless, how AI self-efficacy, transformational leadership, and work engagement together drive innovation in this field remains scarcely documented. Objective: Drawing on the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) framework, this research investigates how AI self-efficacy and transformational leadership influence IWB among staff of four- and five-star hotels in Jakarta, treating work engagement as the mediating variable. Methods: A cross-sectional quantitative survey gathered responses from 180 hotel employees recruited via non-probability snowball sampling. The data were obtained through an online questionnaire and examined with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in AMOS. Results: AI self-efficacy exerted significant positive influences on both IWB and work engagement, whereas transformational leadership shaped work engagement significantly yet showed no significant direct influence on IWB. Work engagement was a significant predictor of IWB and partially carried the AI self-efficacy-IWB link, while it fully carried the transformational leadership-IWB link. Conclusion: The results show that personal and job resources reach employee innovation along distinct routes. AI self-efficacy contributes that is at once direct and indirect by way of work engagement, while transformational leadership operates mainly through engagement. To foster innovative work behavior, hotel management is advised to combine the cultivation of AI capability, the practice of transformational leadership, and initiatives that build employee engagement.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Implementation of The Guided Reading Learning Model To Improve Short Story Reading Skills In Students Kelas IV SD Negeri Lahendong
latest.venue: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study aims to improve short story reading skills through the application of the Guided Reading learning model in fourth-grade students of Lahendong State Elementary School. The method used in this study is Classroom Action Research (CAR) which is implemented in two cycles. Each cycle consists of planning, action implementation, observation, and reflection. The research subjects were 13 fourth-grade students of Lahendong State Elementary School. Data collection techniques were carried out through observation and learning outcome tests. Data were analyzed using quantitative and qualitative descriptive analysis techniques. The results of the study indicate that the application of the Guided Reading learning model can improve students' short story reading skills. In cycle I, the average student learning outcomes reached 71.15% with a classical completion rate of 61.53%. After improvements were made in cycle II, the average student learning outcomes increased to 85.76% with a classical completion rate of 84.61%. These results indicate that students' short story reading skills have improved and have exceeded the established KKTP, which is 75%. Based on the research results, it can be concluded that the application of the Guided Reading learning model can improve the short story reading skills of fourth grade students at Lahendong State Elementary School.

latest.title: ESG Disclosure, Profitability, Current Ratio, and Company Value in Indonesian Energy Companies
latest.venue: Journal of Business Social and Technology
latest.abstract: Background: The growing importance of sustainable finance has widened the information set used in corporate valuation. This is particularly relevant for Indonesian energy firms, whose market performance is shaped by a combination of environmental exposure, capital intensity, and near-term financial capacity. Objective: This study assesses whether ESG disclosure, profitability, and liquidity are statistically associated with firm value among energy-sector issuers on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2023–2025. Methods: A panel-data design was applied to 90 firm-year observations from 30 energy companies selected purposively from 91 listed firms. The analysis used annual financial statements and sustainability reports. ESG disclosure was scored against the GRI Standards 2021, profitability was measured by Return on Assets (ROA), liquidity by the Current Ratio (CR), and firm value by Price to Book Value (PBV). Panel estimation was performed in EViews 12, with specification testing indicating the use of company fixed effects. Results: In the fixed-effects regression, ESG disclosure was positively associated with PBV (coefficient = 3.379502; p = 0.0158). ROA also showed a positive association (coefficient = 0.019785; p = 0.0049), as did CR (coefficient = 0.265845; p < 0.001). The model was significant overall and produced an adjusted R² of 0.804446. Conclusion: The evidence from the observed firms indicates that sustainability disclosure and financial fundamentals are jointly relevant to market valuation. Higher ESG disclosure, profitability, and liquidity were each accompanied by higher PBV, although the non-experimental panel design permits association-based rather than causal interpretation.

latest.title: Technostress and telemedicine in rural communities: insights from healthcare professionals in the Italian Dolomites
latest.abstract: Introduction: In Italy, many facilities have started adopting telemedicine services since their regulation in 2020.Rural areas mainly benefit from telemedicine implementation due to their geographic features.We investigated the interests, attitudes, and perceptions of healthcare providers operating in the Italian Dolomites regarding the adoption of telemedicine.Furthermore, we explored the relationship between technostress and the intention to integrate telemedicine services during daily practices.Methods: We developed a structured interview protocol based on existing literature and following the key principles of constructivist grounded theory to investigate five areas of interest in telemedicine.After the interview, participants completed the Italian version of the Technostress Creators Scale (TCS) to evaluate the current technostress experienced in work activities, and a TCS-adapted version to measure technostress values generated through telemedicine services.Results: A content analysis of the interviews highlighted four main factors that can help communities more readily accept telemedicine services: the convenience of not having to travel, the ageing population, cost savings, and a sense of community.Regarding the scales, there were positive significant correlations between most of the subscales.Discussion: Our findings confirm that telemedicine fosters perceived security and service quality in rural settings.Despite moderate technostress, professionals remain supportive, highlighting the role of perceived usefulness.Key barriers include low digital literacy and reduced social contact, underscoring the need for strong patient-provider relationships and targeted digital r

latest.title: Competitive Advantage in Eco-Friendly Accommodation in Bali: Linking Green Supply Chain Management to Sustainability Performance
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the role of Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) in enhancing Sustainability Performance through Sustainable Competitive Advantage (SCA) in eco-friendly accommodation in Bali, grounded in the Natural Resource-Based View and Resource-Based View. This study examines eco-friendly accommodation in Bali as the research object, focusing on Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM), Sustainable Competitive Advantage (SCA), and Sustainability Performance as key variables. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data collected from accommodation managers. The research framework was analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), emphasizing measurement model evaluation, structural relationships, and mediation analysis to test the proposed hypotheses. The results indicate that Green Supply Chain Management significantly enhances Sustainability Performance and Sustainable Competitive Advantage. Sustainable Competitive Advantage also positively influences Sustainability Performance and acts as a significant mediator. These findings highlight that sustainability practices generate stronger performance outcomes when transformed into strategic capabilities, offering a more integrated explanation of how environmental initiatives drive competitive and sustainability advantages. This study is limited by its cross-sectional design and focus on eco-friendly accommodation in Bali. The findings suggest that managers should integrate GSCM into strategic initiatives to enhance competitiveness and sustainability. Regulators can support adoption through incentives. Future research should apply longitudinal designs and explore additional variables such as digitalization and circular economy practices. This study extends the Resource-Bas

latest.title: Body image as a moderator of the association between addictive social media use and orthorexia nervosa tendencies in physically active university students
latest.abstract: Background Social media may contribute to orthorexia nervosa tendencies through exposure to idealized health, fitness, nutrition, and appearance-related content. This study examined whether body image moderated the association between addictive social media use and orthorexia nervosa tendencies among physically active university students. Methods This cross-sectional study included 350 physically active university students aged 18–23 years who reported exercising at least once per week. Participants completed the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale, the Turkish Düsseldorf Orthorexia Scale, and the Body Cathexis Scale. Pearson correlations and moderation analysis using Hayes’ PROCESS Model 1 were conducted, controlling for the primary demographic and exercise-related covariates, with additional lifestyle variables examined in a fully adjusted sensitivity model. Results Addictive social media use and body image were not independently associated with orthorexia nervosa tendencies. In the primary parsimonious model, the interaction between addictive social media use and body image was not statistically significant ( B = −0.004, p = 0.149) and explained an additional 0.6% of the variance. In a fully adjusted sensitivity model, the interaction was statistically significant ( B = −0.012, p < 0.001) and accounted for an additional 5.1% of the variance. Thus, the primary moderation hypothesis was not supported, and the significant interaction observed in the fully adjusted model should be regarded as specification-sensitive. Conclusion The primary moderation hypothesis was not supported in the parsimonious model. A significant interaction emerged only in the fully adjusted sensitivity model, indicating that the observed moderation pattern was dependent on covariate specification

latest.title: QUALITY CONTROL OF T – BOLT CLAMP PRODUCTS USING THE SEVEN TOOLS METHOD: A CASE STUDY OF PT XYZ
latest.abstract: This research aims to identify and anticipate the dominant types of defects, so that the root causes can be analyzed and corrective actions can be proposed based on statistical quality control. The production of T‑bolt clamps at PT XYZ in 2025 revealed significant fluctuations in product quality, with an average defect rate of 2.54% from a total of 360,706 units manufactured. The peak defect rate occurred in July, reaching 4.8%, indicating systemic issues in the manufacturing process. This study aims to identify the dominant defect types, analyze their root causes, and propose corrective actions based on statistical quality control.The Seven Tools of Quality—Check Sheet, Pareto Chart, Fishbone Diagram, Histogram, Control Chart, Scatter Diagram, and Stratification—were applied to systematically evaluate production data. Results show that Dimensional Deformation was the most critical defect, accounting for 43.25% of total defects. The Fishbone Diagram revealed contributing factors across human, machine, material, method, measurement, and environmental categories. Histogram and Control Chart analyses indicated that the process was generally stable, though several periods exhibited special cause variation. The Scatter Diagram demonstrated a positive correlation (r =0.68) between workplace temperature and defect occurrence, while Stratification confirmed that Machine B produced significantly more defects than Machine A ( p<0.05).In conclusion, dimensional defects are primarily influenced by environmental conditions and machine performance. Recommended improvements include workplace temperature control, regular machine calibration, operator training, and continuous monitoring through statistical process control. These measures are expected to reduce defect rates below 3% and

latest.title: The Impact of Front Office Staff Emotional Intelligence on Guest Retention: Mediating Role of Guest Satisfaction in Five-star Hotels in Aqaba- The Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
latest.abstract: This research aims to explore the significant influence that the emotional intelligence (EI) of front office workers has on the retention of guests at five-star hotels in Aqaba City, which is located in Jordan. Within this context, it specifically investigates the function that visitors' satisfaction plays as a mediator in this interaction, drawing on current research published in between the years 2020 and 2025. The study proposes that front office staff members who are emotionally intelligent are more suited to comprehend and manage the guests' emotions, which ultimately results in increased levels of satisfaction among guests, while it is expected that this increased level of satisfaction will, in turn, lead to increased levels of visitor retention in five-star hotels in Aqaba. The study employs a quantitative research methodology with a sample comprising both guests and front office staff. The findings are expected to highlight the vital importance of training front office staff in emotional intelligence skills, as well as underscore the significance of guests' satisfaction as a key factor in building a long-term customer loyalty within the competitive hospitality environment in Aqaba. The findings of this study will also provide valuable insights , that hotel managers, decision-makers and future researchers in the field can leverage to make scientifically grounded decisions.

latest.title: Fairness, health, and socioeconomic status as predictors of subjective wellbeing among Chinese women: an interpretable machine learning approach
latest.abstract: Background Subjective wellbeing (SWB) is an important indicator of women’s quality of life and social development. Identifying key predictors of women’s SWB is important for understanding their living conditions and informing policy-oriented research. Previous studies have often relied on traditional linear models, which may not fully capture the multidimensional and nonlinear nature of women’s SWB. Methods Using data drawn from the 2023 Chinese General Social Survey (CGSS), this study applied an interpretable machine learning framework to predict SWB among Chinese women from fairness, health, and socioeconomic status (SES) indicators. Five models—Elastic Net, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and an artificial neural network (ANN)—were trained and evaluated. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to interpret the final model. Results XGBoost and LightGBM showed highly similar predictive performance, and XGBoost was selected for SHAP interpretation based on cross-validation (CV) performance. SHAP analyses showed that fairness made the largest contribution to model-predicted SWB, followed by mental health, loneliness, physical health, and subjective SES indicators. SHAP dependence plots suggested nonlinear and possible interaction-like predictive patterns involving fairness, future subjective SES, personal income, and physical health. Discussion This study demonstrates the usefulness of interpretable machine learning for examining women’s SWB and provides model-based evidence on its multidimensional predictive structure among Chinese women. The findings may inform future policy-oriented, longitudinal, and causal research on social fairness, health, SES, and women’s wellbeing.

latest.title: The authorisation of crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) in the EU under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCAR)
latest.abstract: As its title denotes, this study develops on the authorisation of crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) in the European Union (EU) under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCAR). It is structured in three Sections as follows: Section A develops on the relevant provisions of MiCAR relating to the conditions for a person to be allowed to provide crypto-asset services within the EU and the single passport regime (Article 59), as well as the application for authorisation (Article 62 and the related Delegated and Implementing Regulations), and the assessment of that application by national competent authorities (NCAs), leading to the granting or refusal of authorisation (Article 63) in accordance with the “three step” procedure set out in these two Articles. The focus of Section B turns to some specific related provisions, namely, the governance arrangements under Article 68 and the identification, prevention, management and disclosure of conflicts of interest under Article 72. Read together with Articles 62-63, these Articles reflect the MiCAR’s emphasis on effective corporate governance, sound risk management and the mitigation of conflicts of interest as essential safeguards for the provision of crypto-asset services. The concluding remarks are included in Section C.

latest.title: A hierarchical regression analysis of social physique anxiety, social comparison orientation, and coping strategies in relation to mental health among Japanese university students
latest.abstract: Introduction Protecting the mental health of young people is critical in Japan. During self-concept development, youths are particularly vulnerable to excessive social comparisons, including comparisons of achievement and physical appearance. This study examines the independent effects of social physique anxiety (SPA) and social comparison orientation (SCO) on mental health and proposes coping strategies that may buffer their negative associations. Methods T -tests, Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, Spearman rank correlation coefficients, Pearson correlation coefficients, and chi-squared tests were used for bivariate analyses. A hierarchical regression analysis was also performed to develop the model. Results Four hundred seventy-three students participated in this study. Both SPA (rs = 0.292) and SCO (rs = 0.281) were significantly and positively associated with mental health. In separate multiple regression models predicting mental health scores, Sense of Coherence was a significant predictor of better mental health (β = −0.562, p < 0.001, adjusted R 2 = 0.367), whereas the associations of SPA (β = 0.090, p = 0.105) and SCO (β = −0.002, p = 0.960) with mental health were no longer significant. A similar pattern was observed for self-efficacy (β = −0.431, p < 0.001, adjusted R2 = 0.258), with SPA (β = 0.109, p = 0.077) and SCO (β = 0.029, p = 0.553) showing no significant associations. In contrast, social support did not show a comparable effect. Discussion These findings highlight the importance of fostering internal coping resources, suggesting the need for further research on educational interventions to protect university students’ mental health.

latest.title: NRBV's strategic capabilities and SDG disclosure: Does this disclosure enhance financial performance?
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to extend the sustainable development goals (SDG) disclosure literature by examining the influence of natural resource-based view (NRBV) strategic capabilities, namely pollution prevention, green product innovation and environmental certification, on SDG disclosure practices among Indonesian companies. It also investigates the association between this disclosure and financial performance. Design/methodology/approach This study uses Indonesian companies listed in Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2021 to 2024, comprising 1,256 company-year observations from 314 companies. All data for the variables are collected from annual and sustainability reports and analyzed using panel regression. Findings This study demonstrates that NRBV-based strategic capabilities, such as pollution prevention, green product innovation and environmental certification, significantly enhance companies' SDG disclosure. However, such disclosure is associated with lower financial performance due to the substantial costs required to support SDG-related activities. Practical implications The findings of this study provide practical implications for regulators as the commitment for achieving the SDG can be actualized through stricter sustainability regulations. It can be used to encourage companies to integrate strategic capabilities provided by NRBV into business operations. Originality/value This study extends the existing literature on SDG disclosure by shifting the focus from commonly examined governance and ownership determinants to the role of NRBV's strategic capabilities. It further contributes by examining the implications of SDG disclosure for companies' financial performance within an emerging market country context like Indonesia. This study also provides

latest.title: The Instagram paradox: a mediation analysis of consumer orientations, psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions & Instagram motivations shaping purchase intention of sustainable apparel in India
latest.abstract: Introduction This study examines how distinctive consumer orientations - Thrifty, Frugal, Moral, and Shopper influence sustainable apparel purchase intention among Indian Instagram users. Grounded in Uses and Gratifications theory and the Theory of Planned Behaviour, the study examines the parallel mediating roles played by inherent psychological, cognitive and deep structures and external stimuli of Instagram motivation in rendering consumer orientation to purchase intention, thus presenting an empirical justification for the ‘Instagram Paradox’ in the framework of sustainable fashion. Methods A quantitative survey was administered to 285 Instagram users and followers of sustainable apparel brands in India, recruited via snowball sampling. Factor Analyses was conducted to validate constructs spanning consumer orientation, psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions, Instagram motivations, and purchase intention. Results K-means cluster analysis identified four distinct consumer orientation segments. Four parallel mediation models tested whether psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions along with Instagram motivation mediated the relationship between each consumer orientation and purchase intention. Discussion Across all the mediation models, psychological, cognitive and deep structure constructs emerged as the sole significant mediator, while Instagram motivation consistently failed to generate a significant indirect effect on purchase intention in any model, constituting the central empirical evidence for the Instagram Paradox.

latest.title: Do corporate governance and strategy matter in corporate goodness decisions?
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how governance mechanisms and corporate strategy jointly influence corporate goodness in an emerging market characterized by concentrated ownership and mandatory corporate social responsibility regulations. Design/methodology/approach Using a panel of 397 listed firms from an emerging market (India) between 2010 and 2023, this study analyzes the impact of governance mechanisms (ownership, boards and management) and strategic investments on corporate goodness, specifically evaluating the complex interactions among these internal governance structures. Findings Advancing the governance-environment, social and governance (ESG) literature on principal-principal conflicts, the authors find promoter-dominated ownership negatively influences corporate goodness. However, strong board and management governance actively drives corporate goodness, interactively offsetting these negative ownership impacts. Furthermore, aligning with compliance-cost perspectives, corporate goodness acts primarily as a regulatory burden without complementary strategic investments. Practical implications This study reframes corporate goodness as a strategic resource, dynamically shaped by the interactions among internal governance mechanisms rather than mere regulatory compliance. It demonstrates that the interdependent relationship among ownership, boards and management serves as a vital substitute for weak investor oversight in emerging markets. Originality/value This study reframes ESG as a strategic resource shaped by internal governance rather than mere regulatory compliance, demonstrating that governance acts as a vital substitute for weak external enforcement in concentrated-ownership environments.

latest.title: The moderating role of big five personality between physical activity and self-esteem in college students: a cross-sectional survey
latest.abstract: Objective Previous studies have indicated a close correlation between physical activity and self-esteem; however, the underlying mechanism of them remains unknown till now. This research aimed to reveal the potential moderating role of Big Five personality traits in the relationship between physical activity and self-esteem among college students in China. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 1,345 college students from Guangdong in south region of China by employing the convenience sampling. Data were collected using the Physical Activity Rating Scale, the Self-Esteem Scale, and the brief version of the Chinese Big Five Personality Inventory. Descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation analysis, one-way analysis of variance, and the moderation effect analysis were performed in turn. Results Physical activity was significantly and positively associated with self-esteem ( r = 0.217, p < 0.01). A significant increasing trend in self-esteem was observed across levels of physical activity ( F = 24.254, p < 0.001). After controlling for demographic variables, conscientiousness ( B = −0.003, p = 0.001), agreeableness ( B = −0.003, p = 0.009), and extraversion ( B = −0.002, p = 0.009) significantly and negatively moderated the association between physical activity and self-esteem. Furthermore, the positive association between physical activity and self-esteem was stronger among students with lower levels of conscientiousness ( B = 0.067, p < 0.001), agreeableness ( B = 0.076, p < 0.001), and extraversion ( B = 0.063, p < 0.001). Conclusion This study extends current understanding of the association between physical activity and self-esteem by identifying the moderating role of Big Five personality traits, and the findings provide empirical evidence suggesting

latest.title: The Effect of Product Information Quality, Last-Mile Service Quality, and Shipment Trackability on The Decision Not to Return Furniture in E-Commerce Purchases Through Customer Trust
latest.abstract: The growth of e-commerce has made furniture purchasing more convenient for customers; however, it has also introduced risks associated with discrepancies in product information, shipping damage, unclear delivery status, and product returns. This study aims to examine the effects of Product Information Quality, Last-Mile Service Quality, and Shipment Trackability on the Decision Not to Return Furniture, both directly and indirectly through Customer Trust as a mediating variable. The study employed a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design. Primary data were collected through a questionnaire comprising 46 indicators administered to 301 customers who had purchased furniture through e-commerce platforms within the preceding 12 months. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS software. The results indicate that Last-Mile Service Quality and Shipment Trackability have significant effects on Customer Trust, whereas Product Information Quality does not. Product Information Quality, Shipment Trackability, and Customer Trust significantly influence the Decision Not to Return Furniture, while Last-Mile Service Quality has no significant direct effect. Furthermore, Customer Trust mediates the relationships between Last-Mile Service Quality and the Decision Not to Return Furniture and between Shipment Trackability and the Decision Not to Return Furniture, but does not mediate the relationship between Product Information Quality and the Decision Not to Return Furniture. The model explains 55.4% of the variance in Customer Trust and 60.8% of the variance in the Decision Not to Return Furniture. These findings highlight the importance of high-quality last-m

hot.title: Trust in scientists and their role in society across 68 countries
hot.abstract: Science is crucial for evidence-based decision-making. Public trust in scientists can help decision makers act on the basis of the best available evidence, especially during crises. However, in recent years the epistemic authority of science has been challenged, causing concerns about low public trust in scientists. We interrogated these concerns with a preregistered 68-country survey of 71,922 respondents and found that in most countries, most people trust scientists and agree that scientists should engage more in society and policymaking. We found variations between and within countries, which we explain with individual- and country-level variables, including political orientation. While there is no widespread lack of trust in scientists, we cannot discount the concern that lack of trust in scientists by even a small minority may affect considerations of scientific evidence in policymaking. These findings have implications for scientists and policymakers seeking to maintain and increase trust in scientists.

hot.title: Exploring automation bias in human–AI collaboration: a review and implications for explainable AI
hot.abstract: Abstract As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, law, and public administration, automation bias (AB)—the tendency to over-rely on automated recommendations—has emerged as a critical challenge in human–AI collaboration. While previous reviews have examined AB in traditional computer-assisted decision-making, research on its implications in modern AI-driven work environments remains limited. To address this gap, this research systematically investigates how AB manifests in these settings and the cognitive mechanisms that influence it. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we reviewed 35 peer-reviewed studies from SCOPUS, ScienceDirect, PubMed, and Google Scholar. The included literature, published between January 2015 and April 2025, spans fields such as cognitive psychology, human factors engineering, human–computer interaction, and neuroscience, providing an interdisciplinary foundation for our analysis. Traditional perspectives attribute AB to over-trust in automation or attentional constraints, resulting in users perceiving AI-generated outputs as reliable. However, our review presents a more nuanced view. While confirming some prior findings, it also sheds light on additional interacting factors such as, AI literacy, level of professional expertise, cognitive profile, developmental trust dynamics, task verification demands, and explanation complexity. Notably, although Explainable AI (XAI) and transparency mechanisms are designed to mitigate AB, overly technical, cognitively demanding, or even simplistic explanations may inadvertently reinforce misplaced trust, especially among less experienced professionals with low AI literacy. Taken together, these findings suggest that although explanations may increas

hot.title: The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. We finally consider the need to ensure that innovations work for all people and thus can bridge digital health disparities, reviewing the evidence on ta

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.

hot.title: Job demands-resources and conservation of resources theories: How do they help to explain employee well-being and future job design?
hot.abstract: This paper examines the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory to understand and predict employee well-being and performance. COR theory suggests that individuals aim to acquire, protect, and maximize resources to reduce psychological distress and prevent burnout. JD-R theory posits that balancing job demands and resources affects employee well-being, behaviors, and performance. By exploring these theories together, the paper offers insights into supporting the workforce amid challenges like remote work and technological advancements. It highlights shared features and differences between the theories, unresolved issues, and research opportunities, such as operationalizing and testing COR theory and differentiating job demands and resources in JD-R theory. The paper concludes with predictions about future job design, emphasizing the need to balance job demands and resources to support employee well-being and performance, contributing to the literature by challenging and refining these theories.

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.
