latest.title: When the algorithm feels like mine: personalisation depth, algorithmic transparency and psychological ownership in continued streaming engagement
latest.venue: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines whether artificial intelligence (AI) personalisation depth and algorithmic transparency relate to continued engagement with streaming platforms through consumers’ psychological ownership of the recommendation stream, and over what range of privacy concern the transparency route holds. Design/methodology/approach A 14-day, two-wave panel of streaming subscribers in Türkiye (N = 450) was analysed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and re-estimated with covariance-based SEM. A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment (N = 236) manipulated both features. Findings Personalisation depth showed an indirect-only mediation pattern through ownership in the estimated model, with a direct path practically equivalent to zero within a pre-specified bound; the pattern replicated under random assignment. Ownership carried 45 per cent of the association between transparency and engagement, and a direct path accounted for the rest. The transparency–ownership link was no longer significant above a privacy-concern level of about 4.5 (7-point scale), a region holding roughly two in five respondents. Platform involvement strengthened the personalisation route; no group difference was detected for transparency. Research limitations/implications Participants were subscribers aged 18–35 in three Turkish cities, engagement was self-reported and ownership and engagement were measured on the same occasion. Practical implications Ownership measures can complement viewing and churn metrics when personalisation is evaluated, and layered explanations let users choose how much detail they see. Originality/value For interactive marketing, the study recasts the AI feed as a possession consumers co-produce, not exposure firms deliver. It tests, and does

latest.title: Sustainable values and consumer responses in cosmetic retailing: cross-cultural evidence
latest.venue: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper investigates how environmental and ethical values shape consumer responses in the cosmetics retail context, focusing on detachment from brands that use chemical ingredients or engage in animal testing, as well as preferences for green and cruelty-free products across cultural and generational contexts. Design/methodology/approach We conducted three online survey studies in Italy (n = 310), Thailand (n = 198) and Czechia (n = 535). The first two studies examined how environmental values predict detachment from brands associated with animal testing or chemical ingredients, with brand attitude towards green and cruelty-free products tested as a mediator. The third study analysed how environmental and ethical values predict favourable attitudes towards cruelty-free cosmetics and willingness to purchase such products among Generation Z. Mediation was evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples and the bias-corrected percentile method. Findings In Italy and Thailand, environmental values predict detachment from brands associated with animal testing or chemical ingredients, and this effect is fully or partially mediated by brand attitudes towards green and cruelty-free cosmetics. In Czechia, environmental and ethical values directly predict higher willingness to buy cruelty-free products. Results support an attitude-to-behaviour pathway while revealing cross-cultural and generational differences in effect sizes with implications for retail decision-making. Originality/value This research provides multi-country evidence on how environmental and ethical values shape consumer reactions in the cosmetics sector. It advances understanding of value-driven detachment and purchase intentions for cruelty-free products and offers actionable insights for retailer

latest.title: Analysis of Instagram Digital Marketing and Product Quality, on Repurchase Intention in Tenpura Jakarta
latest.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effects of Instagram digital marketing and product quality on customers' repurchase intention at Tenpura Jakarta, a restaurant located in Blok M, South Jakarta. A quantitative research design with an associative approach was employed. Data were collected through questionnaires administered to 100 respondents selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression analysis with IBM SPSS Statistics. The results revealed that digital marketing had a positive and statistically significant relationship with repurchase intention, with a reported correlation coefficient (r) of 0.420 and a significance level of p < 0.001. Conversely, product quality was not significantly associated with repurchase intention (r = ?0.019, p = 0.849). The overall regression model was statistically significant (F = 10.492), with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.178, indicating that digital marketing and product quality collectively explained 17.8% of the variance in repurchase intention. These findings suggest that Instagram digital marketing was more strongly associated with customers' repurchase intention than product quality in the context of Tenpura Jakarta. The study highlights the importance of optimizing Instagram digital marketing strategies and recommends examining additional factors, such as brand image and customer experience, to better understand and potentially enhance customers' repurchase intention.

latest.title: Digital Transformation and Green Marketing Strategy in Shaping Consumer Purchase Intention: Evidence from UNIQLO Indonesia
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of fast fashion has worsened environmental damage through textile waste, carbon emissions, and resource use, pushing brands to adopt digital transformation and eco-focused marketing. UNIQLO is in a tricky spot: while promoting sustainability digitally, its fast fashion label raises questions about the authenticity of its environmental claims, sparking debates about its ecological accountability. This study looks at the factors that shape purchasing intentions towards UNIQLO by expanding the Theory of Planned Behaviour through environmental concern and green marketing. Using an exploratory quantitative method with PLS-SEM, data was collected from 225 UNIQLO customers in Indonesia through purposive sampling. The results show that environmental awareness, social influence, and green marketing significantly affect purchase intentions, with green marketing being the most influential, explaining 61.8% of the variation. UNIQLO should strengthen transparency and digital verification to reinforce its sustainable identity.

latest.title: Consumer financial behavior, digital payments, and financial debt during ritualized consumption
latest.abstract: Ritualized consumption combines emotional engagement, digital purchasing, and financial debt, yet these dynamics remain underexplored in crisis-affected economies. This study examines how Christmas shopping routines, gift-selection practices, and online payment methods are associated with Christmas spirit and Christmas debt among Lebanese consumers. The framework integrates Ritual Theory, Gift-Giving and Social Exchange theories, Normative Social Influence Theory, Hedonic Consumption Theory, and Self-Control Theory. Online survey data from a sample of 284 Lebanese consumers were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Christmas shopping routines showed the strongest association with Christmas spirit (β = 0.472, p < 0.001), while shopping routines and Christmas spirit showed the strongest associations with Christmas debt (both β = 0.380, p < 0.001). Christmas spirit significantly mediated the associations between all three antecedents and Christmas debt, supporting partial mediation. The findings indicate that ritualized, relational, and technologically enabled consumption practices are associated with both positive festive engagement and greater Christmas-related financial obligations. The study contributes to consumer behavior, consumer finance, and digital consumption research by integrating cultural, emotional, technological, and financial perspectives. It offers implications for retailers, policymakers, and digital payment providers seeking to promote responsible spending and financial transparency during high-consumption periods.

latest.title: How Does Cognitive Dissonance Explain Why Consumers Justify Expensive Purchases After the Fact (Post-Purchase Rationalization), And What Does This Mean for Return-Policy Design?
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: This paper explores the cognitive dissonance theory developed by Leon Festinger (Festinger, 1957) as an answer to explain why consumers in their normal practices justify their high-cost purchases after they make them. This is often referred to as post-purchase rationalization and/or "buyer's remorse management". Based on the social-psychological literature on dissonance reduction, the consumer-behaviour research on post-purchase evaluation (Oliver, 1980; Sweeney, Hausknecht, & Soutar, 2000), and the current literature on retail returns (National Retail Federation & Happy Returns, 2024, 2025), the paper proposes a framework that integrates purchase involvement, decision irreversibility, and self-concept threat with the intensity of post-purchase dissonance and the rationalization strategies consumers use to manage it. The paper then moves on to the implications of this psychology for the firm, that is, the design of return policies. The ease at which a consumer can reverse a purchase decision has a direct effect on the psychological dynamics of dissonance, with lenient return policies making customers more likely to convert to a purchase and causing a window where dissonance can arise as an actual return. The paper utilizes data from the National Retail Federation, Janakiraman, Syrdal, and Freling (2016) meta-analysis of the U.S. retail return literature, and other secondary sources to illustrate that there were an estimated $890 billion worth of U.S. retail returns in 2024 (16.9% of sales), a slight decrease to estimated $849.9 billion worth of U.S. retail returns in 2025 (15.8%), and leniency dimensions (e.g. monetary, temporal, effort, scope and exchange) have an asymmetric influence on purchase and return behaviour. latest.title: Reducing Thermoplastic Diversity— A Path to Enhanced Circularity
latest.abstract: This paper shows that reducing thermoplastic diversity can improve circularity without compromising key performance. Based on 63 interviews and a stakeholder workshop across the Swedish plastics value network, it identifies highest near-term feasibility in high-volume Northern European consumer applications, especially packaging and PE, PP, and PET flows, where design, collection, and recycling can be aligned. More demanding applications remain conditional, and advanced structural composites are outside the current evidence base. Respondents link reduction not only to cleaner material flows and stronger recycling markets, but also to production and economic value: larger volumes of fewer polymers, lower inventory and changeover costs, less start-up waste, and more stable processing. These gains depend on maintaining application-specific properties. Three priorities emerge: (i) circular design; (ii) phasing out hazardous materials while prioritising recyclable polymers; and (iii) aligned regulation across the value network. The results support a staged, application-specific “fewer, better” strategy—not universal substitution.

latest.title: Strategies to Improve Supply Chain Efficiency in Industrial-Scale Catering Services (Case Study on Morowali Mine Catering Company, Central Sulawesi)
latest.abstract: This study examined operational efficiency in industrial-scale catering services in the Morowali mining region of Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, through an integrated assessment of supply chain management (SCM), inventory management, and menu engineering. The research addressed operational challenges associated with high-volume food production, including inventory discrepancies, supply delays, and unplanned menu modifications. Employing a qualitative case study approach, data were collected through in-depth interviews, field observations, and reviews of operational documentation at an industrial catering company. Informants included personnel directly involved in procurement, goods receiving, warehousing, and food production. The findings revealed that supply chain processes were insufficiently coordinated across departments, contributing to inconsistencies between operational planning and implementation. Manual and partially digitized inventory recording practices were associated with discrepancies between recorded inventory levels and actual physical stock. Furthermore, menu planning was not consistently aligned with raw material availability, resulting in unplanned menu substitutions, increased food costs, and food waste. Collectively, these findings suggested that operational inefficiencies were associated with inadequate integration among supply chain operations, inventory control, and menu planning rather than a single isolated operational problem. Accordingly, the study recommended adopting integrated digital information systems, strengthening standard operating procedures (SOPs), and aligning menu planning with accurate inventory records and reliable supply information to improve operational efficiency. latest.abstract: The main methodological contribution is treating consumer behaviour as an endogenous, probabilistic system component whose response to information and incentives can be parameterised and tested rather than assumed as fixed. Behavioural responses are modelled as functions of incentive type, communication frequency, timing, and decay over time. This enables systematic testing of strategies such as point-of-sale information, brand communication, recurring engagement (e.g., recurring customer reminders), second-hand market promotion, and varying levels of monetary incentives. These behavioural parameters are linked to material flows within a modular circular value chain, allowing analysis of how individual decisions scale to system-level environmental and economic outcomes. Applied to a denim case study, the model shows how changes in consumer response probabilities alter the distribution between virgin production, reuse, repair, remanufacturing, and recycling. In the illustrative denim experiment, progressively stronger intervention conditions reduce modelled virgin-material demand, 100-year global warming potential (GWP 100 ) and cost. Overall, the findings show that circular business model performance can be sensitive to consumer participation, while the magnitude of the effect remains conditional on the behavioural and technical assumptions. The tool enables pre-implementation testing of incentive strategies, offering a novel decision-support approach for companies and policymakers seeking to align consumer behaviour with circular economy innovations. The same structure identifies which consumer-response and decay parameters require empirical calibration.

latest.title: Investigation of restaurant customers’ behavioral intentions with goal-directed behavior theory
latest.abstract: Behavioral intentions are critical determinants of customer loyalty and competitive advantage in the highly competitive restaurant sector. Understanding these intentions requires an integrated view of psychological, emotional, and cognitive processes, combining motivational theory with memory-related mechanisms in gastronomic decision-making. Existing studies often overlook the dynamic interplay between attitudes, social influences, anticipated emotions, perceived control, past experiences, and cognitive recall in shaping restaurant choices. This three-wave longitudinal study applies the Model of Goal-Directed Behavior (MGB) to a sample of 386 restaurant customers in Istanbul, Türkiye, incorporating memory as a novel moderating variable to illuminate cognitive dimensions of consumer choice. Structural Equation Modeling results showed positive associations of perceived behavioral control, positive anticipated emotions, attitudes, subjective norms, and frequency of past behavior with desire. Desire and frequency of past behavior were positively associated with behavioral intentions, whereas the direct association between perceived behavioral control and intentions was not statistically significant. Memory moderation received differing levels of support across the examined pathways: the interaction involving past behavior was positive and statistically significant, whereas evidence for the desire intention interaction was borderline. The interaction involving perceived behavioral control was not statistically significant. Negative anticipated emotions were not significantly associated with desire in this sample. latest.title: Consumer acceptance and market viability of artisanal granadilla wine in Puno, Peru: a concept test using the marketing mix and purchasing behavior approach
latest.abstract: Background Fruit wines from non-traditional sources offer opportunities to add value to underutilized agricultural resources and generate economic alternatives in regional contexts. In the Puno region of Peru, granadilla ( Passiflora ligularis ) production faces limited profitability due to lack of processing infrastructure and commercial channels. Objective This study analyzes consumer acceptance and market viability of DIVINO artisanal granadilla wine in Puno, Peru, using the marketing mix framework to understand how product, price, place, and promotion elements influence purchasing behavior. Method A concept test was conducted with 50 potential consumers in Puno. Data were collected using a structured 24-item questionnaire measuring marketing mix perceptions and purchasing behavior on a five-point Likert scale. Analysis included descriptive statistics, Spearman’s correlation, and exploratory multiple linear regression. Results Results show favorable product concept perception: availability via WhatsApp and social media reached 83.0% acceptance; personal recommendations, 81.6%; and price of S/27.00 (approximately 8.00 USD), 78.7%. Correlational analysis revealed a significant relationship between Marketing Mix Strategies and Purchasing Behavior (Rho = 0.834, p < 0.01), with Product (Rho = 0.844) and Promotion (Rho = 0.745) dimensions exerting the greatest influence. In this exploratory analysis, the multiple regression model suggested Product ( β = 0.386) and Promotion ( β = 0.251) as potential predictors of purchasing behavior ( R 2 = 0.739). Given the limited sample size ( n = 50), these preliminary results require confirmation in larger studies. The scale showed high internal consistency ( α = 0.962). latest.title: Expanding a university-based social enterprise: organizational change across 15 years
latest.abstract: Introduction Social enterprises combine social purpose and commercial activity to address societal challenges, yet limited longitudinal evidence explains how they develop as they expand, particularly when operating within established institutions. This study examines the factors supporting expansion in a university-based social enterprise and how their function and importance change across stages of development. Methods We conduct a 15-year longitudinal case study of an enterprise delivering substance use prevention to secondary school students through face-to-face and digital formats. Evidence includes trial and survey data, organizational records, governance and funding documentation, and an extensive body of peer-reviewed publications. Using a social innovation lens, the study examines the roles of university actors, schools, government, funders and industry across the expansion process. Results Expansion was accompanied by increasing interdependence between the enterprise and the university. The university provided credibility, expertise, resources and institutional support, while the enterprise contributed to the university’s research activity and social mission. Technology also changed how work was coordinated as the organization developed. Initially embedded in the program offering, digital systems increasingly supported communication, collaboration, implementation monitoring and knowledge sharing across staff, schools, university actors and external stakeholders. As the enterprise expanded, roles and implementation processes became more structured, alongside greater requirements for technological oversight, security and accountability. This was important for replicability as the program introduced new platforms and expanded nationally. Discussion These findings

latest.title: Too crowded to be adventurous: the effect of social crowding on consumer switching behavior
latest.abstract: Introduction Global urbanization has inevitably increased the density of individuals in public spaces, exerting considerable influence on marketing strategies and consumers. Despite expanding research on how consumers are influenced by social crowding, consensus among researchers remains elusive. Drawing on conservation of resources (COR) theory, this research investigates how social crowding affects consumer switching behavior. Methods Across five studies, including a quasi-experimental field study, we examine the effect of social crowding on switching intentions and test risk aversion motivation as an explanatory pathway, as well as shared consumption and crowding aversiveness as boundary conditions. Results Social crowding significantly decreases switching intentions, with η 2 ranging from 0.03 to 0.16. Mediation analyses provide evidence consistent with risk aversion motivation as an explanatory pathway. Importantly, this effect disappears when consumers engage in shared consumption or when the crowding is non-aversive. Discussion These findings offer a resource-based interpretation of consumer responses to crowding. From the COR perspective, maintaining familiar choices may serve a protective function when crowding is appraised as a threat to valued resources. Practically, managers can mitigate the negative effect of crowding on switching behavior by encouraging shared consumption and providing risk-reducing cues.

latest.title: Logistic Coordination Strategy and Customer Satisfaction of Manufacturing Firms in Rivers State: The Mediating Role of Consumer Closeness
latest.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MARKETING AND COMMUNICATION STUDIES
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationship between logistic coordination strategy and customer satisfaction among manufacturing firms in Rivers State, Nigeria, with consumer closeness as a mediator. Drawing on the resource-based view, relational view, and social exchange theory, it investigates how information sharing, activity coordination, and joint planning influence service satisfaction, expectation fulfilment, and overall satisfaction. A cross-sectional survey of 198 managers from 72 firms registered with the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria yielded usable data analysed via multiple regression and Baron and Kenny mediation procedures with bootstrapping. Results show that all three dimensions of logistic coordination strategy positively and significantly predict customer satisfaction, with information sharing exerting the strongest effect. Consumer closeness partially mediates the relationship, indicating that coordination benefits are transmitted partly through enhanced communication, relationship interaction, and customer understanding. The findings highlight the dual importance of operational coordination and relational closeness for delivering superior customer experiences in infrastructure-challenged emerging-market settings and offer practical guidance for managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen manufacturing competitiveness in Rivers State.

latest.title: The Effect of Instagram Social Media Marketing and Product Quality on Purchase Decisions of H'zhazu MSME Products in East Ciputat, South Tangerang
latest.venue: International Journal of Management Science and Application
latest.abstract: Social media marketing and product quality are important considerations in consumer purchasing decisions, particularly for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) operating in competitive markets. However, further empirical investigation is needed to understand how these factors are associated with purchasing decisions in the context of traditional-snack MSMEs. This study examines the individual and joint associations of Instagram social media marketing and product quality with purchase decisions among consumers of H'Zhazu MSME products in East Ciputat, South Tangerang. A quantitative cross-sectional design with an associative approach was employed. The study population comprised 348 consumers, from which 78 respondents were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics version 29. The results revealed that Instagram social media marketing had a positive and statistically significant association with purchase decisions (B = 0.512; β = 0.437; t = 4.103; p < 0.001). Product quality also demonstrated a positive and statistically significant association (B = 0.541; β = 0.465; t = 4.371; p < 0.001). Furthermore, the regression model was statistically significant (F = 110.734; p < 0.001), with an R² of 0.747, indicating that the two predictors jointly accounted for 74.7% of the observed variation in purchase decisions within the sample. This study contributes context-specific empirical evidence concerning the relationship between digital marketing and product quality in a traditional-snack MSME. The standardized coefficients indicate that product quality had a slightly stronger association with purchase decisions than Instagram social media marketing. These findings s

latest.title: Customer Satisfaction with Online Food Delivery Services in Melaka, Malaysia
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of online food delivery (OFD) services has transformed consumer purchasing behavior, particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic. This study investigates customer satisfaction factors influencing the use of OFD services in Melaka, Malaysia. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed, involving users of major food delivery platforms including GrabFood and Foodpanda. The study examined four dimensions affecting satisfaction: quality of delivery platform, quality of delivery service, convenience, and quality of delivered food. Findings indicate that customers demonstrate high satisfaction with food quality, order accuracy, delivery personnel professionalism, app usability, and payment flexibility. However, neutral perceptions remain concerning delivery fees, platform satisfaction, and delivery time predictability. The findings suggest that service providers should focus on improving delivery consistency, pricing transparency, and platform functionality to enhance overall customer satisfaction. This study contributes to the understanding of consumer behavior in the Malaysian OFD sector and offers practical implications for service providers and policymakers.

latest.title: Strategic Drivers of E-Retailer Loyalty in Emerging Markets: A Management-Oriented Analysis of E-Service Quality and Trust in Online Reviews
latest.abstract: This study examines how e-service quality, perceived price fairness, and trust in online reviews are associated with e-retailer loyalty in Kazakhstan and Türkiye. A cross-sectional online survey generated 288 complete responses from consumers with prior online-shopping experience. The principal analytical sample comprised 284 respondents from Kazakhstan and Türkiye. E-service quality was modelled as a higher-order construct comprising system efficiency, fulfilment, and privacy, while perceived price fairness, trust in online reviews, and loyalty were specified as first-order constructs. The proposed relationships were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), bootstrapped mediation analysis, predictive assessment, robustness checks, measurement-invariance analysis, and exploratory multi-group comparison. The model explained 65.8% of the variance in trust in online reviews and 70.3% of the variance in e-retailer loyalty. E-service quality showed a strong positive association with trust and the largest total association with loyalty. Trust was positively associated with loyalty and partially mediated the relationship between e-service quality and loyalty. Perceived price fairness showed no significant direct association with loyalty but contributed indirectly through trust, indicating an indirect-only mediation pattern. The main structural relationships remained stable after response-quality screening and demographic adjustment. Cross-country coefficient differences were not statistically significant. However, full compositional invariance was not established for higher-order e-service quality, so national comparisons should be interpreted as exploratory. latest.title: Antecedents of consumer attitude towards online private label brands: a study of an emerging Asian market
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the digital signals and mechanisms involved in shaping consumer attitude towards online private label brands (OPLBs) in an emerging digital market under conditions of heightened uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach A multi-method design focused on the cosmetics and personal care sector was employed. Study 1 used a survey of 637 OPLBs consumers in Pakistan. Study 2 employed a 2 × 2 experimental design that manipulated social media influencer reputation and heuristic cues (high vs low) and included 232 participants. Findings Social media influencer reputation, consumer confidence and bandwagon positively affect consumer attitude towards OPLBs. While heuristic cues have no direct effect in the survey, experimental evidence shows that they influence attitude under conditions of heightened salience. Across both studies, consumer confidence and bandwagon effect mediate the effects of social media influencer reputation and heuristic cues on consumer attitude towards OPLBs. Originality/value This study extends signaling theory by positioning OPLBs as a distinct digital retail context in which consumers rely heavily on externally observable digital signals. It develops a unified signaling framework explaining how source-based credibility signals and popularity-based engagement signals shape consumer attitude through receiver-side mechanisms of evaluative certainty and conformity in uncertainty-rich emerging markets.

latest.title: PENGARUH KUALITAS PELAYANAN DAN NIAT PEMBELIAN TERHADAP KEPUASAN KONSUMEN PADA LOVING NATURE (LN) FORTUNATE COFFEE PEKANBARU
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of service quality and purchase intention on consumer satisfaction at Loving Nature (LN) Fortunate Coffee Pekanbaru. The research method used is a quantitative method with an explanatory research design. The population in this study were consumers of LN Fortunate Coffee Pekanbaru during the period of December 2025 to February 2026 totaling 120 consumers. The sampling technique used was simple random sampling with a total sample of 30 respondents. Data collection techniques were carried out using questionnaires with a Likert scale. The data analysis technique used multiple linear regression analysis with the help of SPSS version 26.The results showed that service quality had a positive and significant effect on consumer satisfaction with a t-count value of 3.635 and a significance value of 0.001 < 0.05. Purchase intention also had a positive and significant effect on consumer satisfaction with a t-count value of 3.941 and a significance value of 0.001 < 0.05. Simultaneously, service quality and purchase intention had a significant effect on consumer satisfaction with an F-count value of 35.235 and a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05. The Adjusted R Square value of 0.710 indicates that 71% of consumer satisfaction can be explained by service quality and purchase intention, while the remaining 29% is influenced by other variables outside this study.

latest.title: Frontier Markets, Marginal Flows: Vietnamese Private Outward Investment in Africa and South Asia, 2015–2025
latest.venue: International Journal of Humanities Education and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Vietnam’s outward foreign direct investment (OFDI) is expanding and diversifying geographically, yet flows to Africa and South Asia remain marginal despite their prominence in policy discourse. This study examines the gap between investment potential and Vietnamese private-sector OFDI in four frontier markets: South Africa, Egypt, India, and Bangladesh. Drawing on secondary data from Vietnam’s Foreign Investment Agency, UNCTAD, the International Trade Centre, and the World Bank for 2015–2025, the study employs a descriptive, comparative design combining share analysis, compound growth rates, concentration measures, min–max normalized composite scoring, and a two-dimensional potential–performance matrix. The findings reveal substantial geographic concentration: three destinations account for approximately half of cumulative registered Vietnamese OFDI capital, whereas the four focal markets collectively account for well below 1%, despite representing more than 1.7 billion consumers. All four markets score substantially higher on the composite attractiveness index than Vietnam’s traditional investment destinations, placing them in the matrix’s high-potential, negligible-presence quadrant. This mismatch is associated with deficiencies in home-country institutional support, including gaps in trade agreements, investment guarantees, market intelligence infrastructure, and financing mechanisms tailored to small and medium-sized private enterprises entering distant frontier markets. The findings suggest that home-country support constraints, rather than weak host-country market fundamentals, are central to understanding Vietnam’s limited private investment in these regions. hot.title: Exploring automation bias in human–AI collaboration: a review and implications for explainable AI
hot.abstract: Abstract As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, law, and public administration, automation bias (AB)—the tendency to over-rely on automated recommendations—has emerged as a critical challenge in human–AI collaboration. While previous reviews have examined AB in traditional computer-assisted decision-making, research on its implications in modern AI-driven work environments remains limited. To address this gap, this research systematically investigates how AB manifests in these settings and the cognitive mechanisms that influence it. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we reviewed 35 peer-reviewed studies from SCOPUS, ScienceDirect, PubMed, and Google Scholar. The included literature, published between January 2015 and April 2025, spans fields such as cognitive psychology, human factors engineering, human–computer interaction, and neuroscience, providing an interdisciplinary foundation for our analysis. Traditional perspectives attribute AB to over-trust in automation or attentional constraints, resulting in users perceiving AI-generated outputs as reliable. However, our review presents a more nuanced view. While confirming some prior findings, it also sheds light on additional interacting factors such as, AI literacy, level of professional expertise, cognitive profile, developmental trust dynamics, task verification demands, and explanation complexity. Notably, although Explainable AI (XAI) and transparency mechanisms are designed to mitigate AB, overly technical, cognitively demanding, or even simplistic explanations may inadvertently reinforce misplaced trust, especially among less experienced professionals with low AI literacy. hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.

Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment

hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.
