hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: Abstract This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: The Vector Grounding Problem
hot.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) produce seemingly meaningful outputs, yet they are trained on text alone without direct interaction with the world. This leads to a modern variant of the classical symbol grounding problem in AI: can LLMs' internal states and outputs be about extra-linguistic reality, independently of the meaning human interpreters project onto them? We argue that they can. We first distinguish referential grounding—the connection between a representation and its worldly referent—from other forms of grounding and argue it is the only kind essential to solving the problem. We contend that referential grounding is achieved when a system's internal states satisfy two conditions derived from teleosemantic theories of representation: (1) they stand in appropriate causal-informational relations to the world, and (2) they have a history of selection that has endowed them with the function of carrying this information. We argue that LLMs can meet both conditions, even without multimodality or embodiment.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Digital literacy, digital accessibility, human capital, and entrepreneurial resilience: a case for dynamic business ecosystems
hot.abstract: This study examines the role of digital literacy, digital accessibility, and human capital in fostering entrepreneurial resilience among entrepreneurs in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These countries serve as exemplary models in digital transformation, particularly in navigating crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Grounded in the resource-based view and the theory of dynamic capabilities, this research investigates how these factors contribute to entrepreneurial resilience. This study employs structural equation modeling to analyze survey data from 317 individuals with entrepreneurial experience. According to the findings, digital literacy, accessibility, and human capital significantly enhance innovation, strengthening entrepreneurial resilience. Agility is identified as a key moderator, amplifying the positive impact of these competencies on resilience. Although the success of entrepreneurial ecosystems has often been attributed to entrepreneurial actors, resource providers, connectors, or entrepreneurial intentions, this study underscores the importance of fostering digital competencies and agility to build resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems. It offers policymakers and business leaders insights into the mechanisms that enhance resilience in dynamic and crisis-affected environments where the digital landscape is rapidly evolving.

hot.title: Global supply chains : why they emerged, why they matter, and where they are going
hot.venue: Graduate Institute Geneva Institutional Repository (Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies)
hot.abstract: Global supply chains have transformed the world. They revolutionised development options facing poor nations – now they can join supply chains rather than having to invest decades in building their own. Offshoring of labour-intensive manufacturing stages and the attendant international mobility of technology launched era-defining growth in emerging markets – a change that fosters and is fostered by domestic policy reform. Historic income gaps are narrowing as the North de-industrialises and the South industrialises -- a reversal-of-fortunes that constitutes perhaps the most momentous global economic change in the last 100 years. Global supply chains, however, are themselves rapidly evolving. The change is in part due to their own impact (income and wage convergence) and in part due to rapid technological innovations in communication technology, computer integrated manufacturing, 3D printing, etc. This paper looks at why global supply chains (GSCs) matter, the economics of their unbundling, and their implications for policy. It finishes with a discussion of factors affecting the future of global supply chains. The paper begins by putting global supply chains into historical perspective.

hot.title: Understanding the Role of Financial Literacy in Enhancing Economic Stability and Resilience in Montenegro: A Data-Driven Approach
hot.abstract: Financial literacy has emerged as a crucial factor in promoting economic stability and resilience, particularly in Montenegro. With the increasing complexity of financial products and the growing need for individuals to make sound financial decisions, the importance of financial literacy cannot be overstated. This study employs a quantitative, survey-based approach to explore the association between financial literacy levels and measures of economic stability, including savings rates, active debt management, and access to financial products. Data were collected through a representative, two-stage stratified sample of 1000 Montenegrin adults aged 18–79, ensuring comprehensive geographic coverage across all Montenegrin municipalities and balanced representation by gender and age. This stratification enables a detailed analysis of financial literacy trends across the population. Correlation analysis reveals that higher levels of financial literacy are associated with better financial practices, such as increased savings and responsible credit use, thereby enhancing economic resilience at the household level. Moreover, improved financial literacy contributes to sustainability by fostering long-term financial stability, reducing inequalities, and promoting inclusive economic growth. The findings suggest that financial literacy can mitigate the impact of economic shocks, emphasizing the need for policies that promote financial education as a tool for sustainable development. This study contributes to the literature on financial literacy in emerging economies and offers actionable insights for policymakers in Montenegro and similar contexts, highlighting financial education as a pathway to individual and national economic resilience.

hot.title: Greenwashing and market value of firms: An empirical study
hot.abstract: In the modern business environment, green or sustainable claims mushroom, with companies striving to improve their green practices for climate change and sustainability. However, with increasing expectations of sustainable performance, companies encounter mounting financial pressure, which may create opportunities to exploit sustainable efforts to their advantage. Many companies assert environmental-friendly measures to mask their true activities, the phenomenon, known as greenwashing, fuels public scepticism about the sincerity of their green message. This study employs an event study methodology to explore how the stock market values greenwashing announcements through 121 worldwide greenwashing announcements since the 2015 Paris Agreement. Our findings reveal that a modest negative association between greenwashing announcements and stock market reactions. Notably, the market reaction to greenwashing announcements is more negative for firms with greater environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance than for weak ESG performance. The study further finds that there are more negative reactions to announcements providing solid evidence of greenwashing. The companies operating in the manufacturing industry suffer more market value losses than those operating in the service industry. Compared with other stock markets, the Asia-Pacific market experiences negative reactions to greenwashing. This study contributes to the signalling theory and advances the literature on corporate sustainable practices by offering empirical insights within a global context.

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Methodology for Designing University Business Curricula with an Impact on the Family Economy
hot.abstract: Advances in Consumer Research (Abbreviated as Adv. Consum. Res.) is a distinguished journal based in the United States and published by Sheridan Books. The journal is highly regarded in the academic community, particularly within the fields of Business, Management, and Accounting, with a specific focus on Marketing.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: The impact of digital HRM system and digital transformation on HR efficiency with organizational agility as a moderator
hot.abstract: The study focuses on understanding the moderation effect of organizational agility in the impact of digital HRM system and digital transformation on HR efficiency in organizations intending to excel in the digital era. This study examines the association between digital HRM systems, digital transformation, and HR efficiency, considering the moderating role of organizational agility. Based on the study model, the authors proposed five hypotheses to be tested in this study. They adapted the study instrument based on quantitative descriptive approach and distributed 500 questioners to collect 385 responses. The study’s findings reveal that both digital HRM systems and digital transformation impact HR efficiency. The significant findings were that digital HRM systems (β = 0.456, p < 0.001) and digital transformation (β = 0.194, p = 0.006) have a positive and significant impact on HR efficiency. In addition, organizational agility serves as a moderator in the relationship between digital HRM systems and HR efficiency (β = 0.154, p = 0.025) but has no effect on the relationship with digital transformation (β = − 0.075, p = 0.248). This study contributes to the literature by demonstrating the role of digital HRM systems and digital transformation as key organizational resources that enhance HR efficiency. It also highlights how organizational agility and digital capabilities serve as dynamic resources, contributing to an organization’s adaptability and sustained competitive advantage. The future research directions and limitations are presented at the end.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The past, present, and future of sustainability marketing: How did we get here and where might we go?
hot.abstract: The ever-increasing concerns about global sustainability have sparked intense debates and actions across various sectors, with marketing playing a pivotal role in influencing both the problem and potential solutions. This article maps the historical trajectory of sustainability marketing, analyzes current trends, and explores future directions to enhance sustainability within marketing practice. We show that sustainability marketing has historically centered on resource conservation and green marketing , but in recent years its scope has expanded to encompass a broader range of topics. These include the circular economy , anti-consumption, regulatory frameworks, innovation, carbon emissions , as well as the social and ethical considerations inherent in sustainability marketing. We propose three main areas within which sustainability marketing might expand in the future: system-driven changes, business-driven changes, and consumer-driven changes. Our analysis aims to deepen the understanding of sustainability marketing and inspire marketers to explore questions and solutions that will contribute to a sustainable future.

hot.title: Exploring the role of health consciousness and environmental awareness in purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods: an extended TPB model
hot.abstract: Background: With the increasing rise of green consumption concepts, consumers are becoming more concerned with the health and environmental attributes of products. However, research on purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods remains relatively limited, particularly regarding the specific impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness. There is a clear gap in the literature addressing these factors. Method: Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study constructs a relationship model between health consciousness, environmental awareness, attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods. A total of 372 valid survey samples were collected, and data analysis was performed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 28.0 software to validate the theoretical model and research hypotheses. Results: Structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis reveals that all hypotheses are significantly supported, and the model demonstrates good fit. Mediation effect analysis further reveals the impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness on purchase intentions, indicating that they influence consumer intentions indirectly through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. Conclusion: Health consciousness and environmental awareness not only significantly affect consumers' purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods through direct paths but also have important indirect effects through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. This study provides a new perspective for the theoretical development of green consumer behavior and offers valuable practical insights for businesses and policymakers in promoting green consumption and sustainable products.

hot.title: What you see is not what you get: ESG scores and greenwashing risk
hot.abstract: This paper shows that ESG scores capture a company’s greenwashing behavior. Greenwashing accusations are most prevalent among large companies with high ESG scores. We empirically employ a novel theoretical model that distinguishes between the communication of a company’s environmental efforts (apparent environmental performance) and its actual environmental impact (real environmental performance). The correlation of the apparent (real) environmental performance with ESG scores is significantly positive (negative). Therefore, ESG scores are unsuitable for measuring real environmental impact. Thus, investors focusing on high ESG-rated companies may unknowingly increase their greenwashing risk exposure, and academics may use misleading information to assess greenwashing risk. • ESG scores are positively correlated with greenwashing cases. • ESG scores mainly measure the apparent rather than the real environmental performance. • Higher analyst coverage limits the exaggeration of apparent environmental performance.

hot.title: Cognitive offloading or cognitive overload? How AI alters the mental architecture of coping
hot.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from being a specialized technological tool to an intimate presence in everyday life. Smart assistants organize our schedules, predictive systems anticipate our needs, and therapeutic chatbots promise to listen when no human is available (Zhang & Wang, 2024). The diffusion of AI into mental health care is often framed in highly optimistic terms: technologies that reduce stigma, democratize access, and provide affordable, always-on support (M & N, 2025;Sivasubramanian Balasubramanian, 2023). From meditation applications and emotion-tracking wearables to conversational agents offering cognitive-behavioral interventions, AI is marketed as an efficient and reliable partner in the pursuit of wellbeing (Balcombe, 2023).Beneath this enthusiasm lies a paradox. On one hand, AI enables cognitive offloading: the use of external aids to reduce mental effort and conserve resources for more meaningful activities (Grinschgl & Neubauer, 2022;Risko & Gilbert, 2016). This process can support adaptive coping, helping individuals regulate stress and sustain mental health. On the other hand, the same tools may create cognitive overload: an erosion of introspection, over-reliance on algorithmic feedback, and anxiety induced by hyper-monitoring and optimization (Grinschgl et al., 2021;Skulmowski, 2023). The question is not whether AI is good or bad for mental health but how it is reshaping the very architecture of coping (Gerlich, 2025). This article examines the psychology of this paradox. First, it places copings in mainstream psychological theory. Then it considers the promise of AI to lighten burdens through cognitive offloading. Next, it considers the risks of cognitive overload and theoretical insights that illuminate this conflict. Through practic

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Hotel certifications are not only crucial for environmental sustainability, but also serve as

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
hot.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies sparked a rapid development of smartphone applications designed to help individuals experiencing mental health problems through an AI-powered chatbot agent. However, the safety of such agents when dealing with individuals experiencing a mental health crisis, including suicidal crisis, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed the ability of 29 AI-powered chatbot agents to respond to simulated suicidal risk scenarios. Application repositories were searched and the app descriptions screened in search of apps that claimed to be beneficial when experiencing mental distress and offered an AI-powered chatbot function. All agents were tested with a standardized set of prompts based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale designed to simulate increasing suicidal risk. We assessed the responses according to pre-defined criteria based on the ability to provide emergency contact information and other factors. None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate. Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding. These findings raise concerns about the deployment of AI-powered chatbots in sensitive health contexts without proper clinical validation.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Barriers and Enablers of AI Adoption in Human Resource Management: A Critical Analysis of Organizational and Technological Factors
hot.abstract: This paper examines the key factors recognized as transformative in the field of human resource management (HRM) and explores their influence on the global adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). While AI holds significant promise for enhancing HRM efficiency, employee engagement, and Decision Making, its implementation presents a range of organizational, technical, and ethical challenges that organizations worldwide must navigate. Change aversion, data security worries, and integration expenses are major roadblocks, but strong digital leadership, company culture, and advancements in NLP and machine learning are key enablers. This paper presents a complex analysis that questions the common perception of AI as only disruptive by delving into the relationship between power dynamics, corporate culture, and technology infrastructures. In this paper, we bring together research from several fields to help scholars and practitioners understand the nuances of AI adoption in HRM, with an emphasis on the importance of inclusive methods and ethical frameworks.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: AI-Driven Financial Transparency and Corporate Governance: Enhancing Accounting Practices with Evidence from Jordan
hot.abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into financial transparency and corporate governance has reshaped how organizations ensure accountability, regulatory compliance, and risk management. This study examines the impact of AI-driven financial transparency on corporate governance and regulatory reform, specifically focusing on Jordan. Utilizing a stratified random sampling approach, data was collected from 564 corporate professionals across key economic sectors, including banking, insurance, services, and industry. A combination of structural equation modeling (SEM) and multiple regression analysis was employed to test the relationships between AI-driven transparency, governance mechanisms, and regulatory frameworks. The results indicate that AI significantly enhances corporate governance effectiveness by improving financial reporting accuracy, risk management, and executive decision-making. Additionally, AI adoption facilitates regulatory compliance by automating monitoring processes and reducing human errors in financial disclosures. However, the findings highlight challenges related to bias in AI algorithms, data privacy concerns, and the need for regulatory adaptation. The study also underscores the necessity of localized AI governance frameworks tailored to Jordan’s corporate landscape to maximize AI’s potential benefits. These findings contribute to the growing body of knowledge on AI-driven governance and provide actionable insights for policymakers, corporate executives, and financial regulators.

hot.title: Cyber Shopping Beyond Boundaries: The Metaverse Revolution in e‐Commerce and Consumer Behavior
hot.abstract: The metaverse is swiftly flattering an important player in the e‐commerce domain. It provides innumerable opportunities and indicates a revolutionary paradigm shift in e‐commerce. Online businesses can now create virtual storefronts that enable immersive, lifelike product exploration within the metaverse, in contrast to traditional brick‐and‐mortar stores that cater to local customers. Current research offers a novel conceptual framework based on theories of interactive media effects and the stimulus–organism–response paradigm to understand consumer purchase intentions in the metaverse. Carefully gathered data from 342 survey participants were then examined using the analytical tools of structural equation modelling (SEM) and importance–performance map analysis (IPMA). The results of the study shed light on how much perceived augmentation and interaction affect consumers’ cognitive and emotive reactions, including feelings of realism, immersion, and telepresence. Remarkably, these reactions have a significant influence on how customers behave. The study’s distinctive worth is found in its creative recommendations, which can help tech firms and metaverse developers improve the purchasing experience in this dynamic digital environment.

hot.title: A Comparison of Responses from Human Therapists and Large Language Model–Based Chatbots to Assess Therapeutic Communication: Mixed Methods Study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consumers are increasingly using large language model-based chatbots to seek mental health advice or intervention due to ease of access and limited availability of mental health professionals. However, their suitability and safety for mental health applications remain underexplored, particularly in comparison to professional therapeutic practices. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how general-purpose chatbots respond to mental health scenarios and compare their responses to those provided by licensed therapists. Specifically, we sought to identify chatbots' strengths and limitations, as well as the ethical and practical considerations necessary for their use in mental health care. METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study to compare responses from chatbots and licensed therapists to scripted mental health scenarios. We created 2 fictional scenarios and prompted 3 chatbots to create 6 interaction logs. We recruited 17 therapists and conducted study sessions that consisted of 3 activities. First, therapists responded to the 2 scenarios using a Qualtrics form. Second, therapists went through the 6 interaction logs using a think-aloud procedure to highlight their thoughts about the chatbots' responses. Finally, we conducted a semistructured interview to explore subjective opinions on the use of chatbots for supporting mental health. The study sessions were analyzed using thematic analysis. The interaction logs from chatbot and therapist responses were coded using the Multitheoretical List of Therapeutic Interventions codes and then compared to each other. RESULTS: We identified 7 themes describing the strengths and limitations of the chatbots as compared to therapists. These include elements of good therapy in chatbot responses, conversational style of c

hot.title: Effect of anthropomorphism and perceived intelligence in chatbot avatars of visual design on user experience: accounting for perceived empathy and trust
hot.abstract: Introduction The rapid advancement of intelligent chatbots has transformed human-AI interaction, offering novel opportunities to enhance user experience (UX) through psychological and design interventions. However, the mechanisms by which chatbot design features influence UX remain understudied, particularly regarding the roles of emotional and cognitive mediators. Methods This study employed a 2 × 2 within-subjects experimental design with 160 participants to investigate the effects of anthropomorphism (high vs. low) and perceived intelligence (high vs. low) in chatbot avatars on UX. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was utilized to analyze the mediating roles of perceived empathy and trust in this relationship. Results Direct effects of anthropomorphism and perceived intelligence on UX were nonsignificant. However, their combined influence was significantly mediated by perceived empathy and trust ( β = 0.48, * p * < 0.01). Specifically, highly anthropomorphic avatars correlated with elevated empathy ( β = 0.32) and trust ( β = 0.27), which in turn improved UX. Discussion These findings underscore the importance of emotional engagement over mere intelligence in designing effective chatbots. This research contributes unique insights into the complex mechanisms governing user interactions with intelligent chatbots, emphasizing the need for design strategies that prioritize emotional connections and cognitive ease.

latest.title: Too crowded to be adventurous: the effect of social crowding on consumer switching behavior
latest.abstract: Introduction Global urbanization has inevitably increased the density of individuals in public spaces, exerting considerable influence on marketing strategies and consumers. Despite expanding research on how consumers are influenced by social crowding, consensus among researchers remains elusive. Drawing on conservation of resources (COR) theory, this research investigates how social crowding affects consumer switching behavior. Methods Across five studies, including a quasi-experimental field study, we examine the effect of social crowding on switching intentions and test risk aversion motivation as an explanatory pathway, as well as shared consumption and crowding aversiveness as boundary conditions. Results Social crowding significantly decreases switching intentions, with η 2 ranging from 0.03 to 0.16. Mediation analyses provide evidence consistent with risk aversion motivation as an explanatory pathway. Importantly, this effect disappears when consumers engage in shared consumption or when the crowding is non-aversive. Discussion These findings offer a resource-based interpretation of consumer responses to crowding. From the COR perspective, maintaining familiar choices may serve a protective function when crowding is appraised as a threat to valued resources. Practically, managers can mitigate the negative effect of crowding on switching behavior by encouraging shared consumption and providing risk-reducing cues.

latest.title: DOES RELIGIOUS PROXIMITY MATTER? UNIVERSITY BRAND AWARENESS AMONG MADRASAH ALIYAH STUDENTS IN SEMARANG
latest.venue: EDUCATOR Jurnal Inovasi Tenaga Pendidik dan Kependidikan
latest.abstract: Increasing competition among higher education institutions has made university branding an important strategic consideration in attracting prospective students. This study aims to analyze and compare the level of brand awareness of Universitas Islam Negeri (UIN) Walisongo, Universitas Negeri Semarang (UNNES), and Universitas Diponegoro (UNDIP) among Madrasah Aliyah students in Semarang City. A quantitative comparative approach was employed involving 231 Grade 12 students from 18 Madrasah Aliyah institutions selected through proportional simple random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring five dimensions of brand awareness, namely brand recall, brand recognition, top-of-mind awareness, brand confidence, and brand familiarity. Data analysis was conducted using One-Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), followed by the Least Significant Difference (LSD) post-hoc test. The results reveal significant differences in brand awareness among the three universities (F = 125.219, p < 0.001). The pairwise comparison shows that UNDIP has the highest level of brand awareness, followed by UNNES, while UIN Walisongo records the lowest level. These findings indicate that religious and educational proximity does not automatically generate stronger brand awareness toward an Islamic higher education institution among Madrasah Aliyah students. The study highlights the need for Islamic higher education institutions, particularly PTKIN, to strengthen institutional positioning through consistent branding, integrated digital communication, clearer academic differentiation, and sustained engagement with prospective students. Future studies should examine factors such as institutional reputation, digital engagement, brand trust, word of mouth, and perceived academic q

latest.title: Rethinking retail patronage: beyond customer loyalty towards reciprocal customer–retailer relationships
latest.venue: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This research clarifies retail patronage by combining consumer insights with bibliometric analysis to address conceptual fragmentation and support consistent measurement. Design/methodology/approach We combined qualitative interviews (n = 68) with a bibliometric analysis of 233 articles using Bibliometrix. Five experts provided an interpretive evaluation of the integrated findings. Findings Retail patronage emerges as a multidimensional relational construct integrating behavioural, intentional, and attitudinal components while remaining conceptually distinguishable from loyalty and love. The literature structures around antecedents and methodological foundations. Patronage occurs when repeated behaviour is relationally interpreted rather than situational. Practical implications Retailers should complement behavioural metrics with relational indicators to distinguish routine purchasing from genuine patronage and design relationship-focused loyalty programmes. Originality/value The study integrates consumer perspectives and intellectual foundations, positioning retail patronage as a reciprocal relational exchange construct to provide a basis for scale development. It explains why repetition can occur without loyalty and loyalty without patronage. The findings suggest that retail patronage extends beyond behavioural loyalty by reflecting reciprocal customer–retailer relationships grounded in ongoing relational exchange.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Sprinkle, Smell, Remember: How Sensory Salience and Ritualistic Use of Domino's Oregano Drive Nostalgia-Mediated Repurchase Intention and Brand Recall
latest.venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
latest.abstract: Sensory cues serve as potent drivers of consumer behavior, yet their influence on nostalgia-mediated brand outcomes remains underexplored in the context of food service branding. This study investigates how sensory salience and ritualistic usage behaviors associated with Domino's oregano sachets influence repurchase intention and brand recall through three mediating mechanisms: nostalgic feelings, sensory pleasure, and emotional comfort. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional design, we collected data from 350 urban consumers with recent Domino's purchasing experience. Structural equation modeling via partial least squares (PLS-SEM) was utilized to test a comprehensive sensory-emotional branding framework. Results reveal that sensory salience, frequency of exposure, perceived uniqueness, and ritualistic usage behavior significantly predict mediating variables (nostalgic feelings, sensory pleasure, and emotional comfort), which subsequently enhance repurchase intention and brand recall. Notably, sensory pleasure emerged as the strongest direct predictor of both outcome variables (β = 0.283 for brand recall, β = 0.280 for repurchase intention, p < 0.001). The model explains 87.6% of variance in brand recall and 88.9% in repurchase intention, demonstrating the explanatory power of the sensory-emotional framework. This research extends sensory branding literature by conceptualizing micro branding cues as ritualistic touchpoints and contributes practical insights for leveraging sensory marketing in highly competitive food service environments.

latest.title: Food preferences, religion and online food delivery behaviour in India
latest.abstract: Online food delivery (OFD) platforms increasingly operate in culturally heterogeneous markets where patronage may be conditioned on social identities and functional considerations. This study examines whether dietary orientation is associated with three dimensions of OFD engagement – adoption, ordering frequency and multihoming – and whether these associations vary across religious contexts in India. Using survey data from 507 respondents, probit and negative binomial models with marginal effects are employed. The findings indicate that vegetarianism is associated with lower OFD engagement across all three dimensions. The association with adoption is statistically significant among Hindu/Jain respondents, but not among respondents from other religious groups. However, the formal interaction between dietary orientation and religion is not statistically significant, indicating that these sub-group patterns should be interpreted as conditional associations rather than definitive evidence of moderation. Nevertheless, the negative interaction coefficient provides a descriptive indication that the association between vegetarianism and OFD adoption may be attenuated across religious contexts, particularly in larger samples and especially among Hindus/Jains. Education is positively associated with OFD adoption and multihoming, while age and gender are associated with ordering frequency. The findings contribute to OFD research by highlighting dietary orientation as a potentially relevant basis for behavioural segmentation alongside conventional consumer characteristics. For OFD operators, the results suggest that dietary segmentation may inform market strategy, but specialised services or infrastructure should be guided by granular market research on segment size, demand intensi

latest.title: From awe to emotional brand attachment: a cognitive appraisal perspective on VR brand experiences
latest.abstract: Purpose Prior research on awe in relation to virtual reality (VR) has treated awe as a response to technological stimuli, leaving the consumer appraisals through which awe arises underexplored. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory, this paper aims to address this gap by investigating whether aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals of a VR brand experience predict awe and whether awe mediates the relationships between these appraisals and emotional brand attachment. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via a survey of 334 Generation Z participants who experienced an in-person brand encounter via a VR headset and were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in LISREL. Findings Aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals positively predict awe, which, in turn, predicts emotional brand attachment. Awe also mediates the relationships between each of the three appraisal and emotional brand attachment. Originality/value At the intersection of the cognitive psychology of VR and emotional branding, this paper reframes the origins of awe in VR brand experiences, shifting from a stimulus-centred to an appraisal-centred account. It also identifies aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals as the experiential predictors of awe and extends emotional branding to self-transcendent emotions by showing how awe translates experiential appraisals into emotional brand attachment.

latest.title: Exploring Corporate Sustainability Reporting and the Potential of Greenwashing
latest.abstract: Companies are encouraged to disclose their sustainability performance to enhance corporate transparency and accountability. Sustainability reporting is not limited to formal sustainability reports but also extends to social media platforms. This study aims to explore corporate sustainability reporting on social media and the potential for greenwashing. A netnographic approach was employed, utilizing two online communities, Danone Indonesia and Greenpeace Indonesia, to address the research questions. The findings indicate that Danone Indonesia actively uses social media to report on its sustainability activities, with a primary focus on the food and health pillar. While this social media reporting has been well-received by the public and community members, the company still faces negative sentiment regarding its AQUA product line, stemming from allegations of greenwashing linked to claims of "purity" that are perceived as excessive. The public has also highlighted the issue of plastic packaging waste, a concern that has led to complaints against Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) manufacturers like Danone Indonesia. Consequently, companies are expected to go beyond merely cultivating an image on social media; they must undertake concrete actions and packaging innovations, supported by synergy among the government, manufacturers, and consumers.

latest.title: THE CORRELATION BETWEEN PAYLATER USAGE AND DISCOUNT PROMOTIONS WITH THE CONSUMERIST BEHAVIOR OF COLLEGE STUDENTS
latest.abstract: ABSTRACTThe problem from this research indicate that the majority of college students in the Economics Education Program at STKIP PGRI Lumajang are experiencing a shift in their consumption patterns toward consumerism. This study aims to examine the relationship between the use of PayLater services and discount promotions with students’ consumerism behavior. The research method used in this study by quantitative descriptive method with correlation analysis. Data were collected by questionnaires and analyzed using Pearson’s correlation, t-tests, F-tests, and the coefficient of determination. The research findings indicate that the use of paylater services has a strong positive correlation with the consumerist behavior of students in the Economics Education program. Another finding shows that discount promotions have a strong positive relationship with the consumerism behavior of students in the Economics Education program. Finally conclude this study, the simultaneous use of paylater services and discount promotions has a strong positive correlation with the consumerism behavior of students in the Economics Education program. Contributions to the Economics Education Program are expected to improve financial literacy through seminars, training sessions, or educational programs on the use of financial services. latest.title: Moderating Effect of Self-Brand Congruity on Purchase Intention of Luxury Brands
latest.abstract: This study examines moderating effect of self-brand congruity on purchase intention of luxury brands. A cumulative approach to analyze purchase intention of luxury brands is presented by combining the behavioral aspects of consumers and personality of the brand. The driving forces that lead to a brand purchase are very important. The question arises that what are the drivers of the luxury brand purchase intention considering the fact that in many cases the same benefits can be acquired from an ordinary brand. Certainly, the functional benefits are the same but there might be some drivers or attitudes that derive luxury brands purchase. This paper identifies those factors (self-expression attitude and self-presentation attitude) and empirically investigates their relationship with consumer’s purchase intention of luxury brands. This study also examines mediating role of affective attitude in relationship between social function attitudes and purchase intentions towards luxury brands. Data is collected from 400 customers living in Lahore and Gujranwala cities, Pakistan. Multiple regression is employed to test relationship between social function attitudes and purchase intention. Bootstrapping method has been used to check the mediation and moderation. Findings show that social function attitude (self-expression & self-presentation attitude) positively influence the purchase intentions towards luxury brand. Moreover, findings confirm mediating role of affective attitude and moderating role of self-brand congruity. This shows that brand personality is very important factor in brand positioning specially for luxury brands where symbolic benefits are far more important than functional benefits.

latest.title: AVATARS AS EXTENSIONS OF THE SELF: A SELF-CONGRUITY PERSPECTIVE ON BRAND ENGAGEMENT IN METAVERSE ENVIRONMENTS
latest.abstract: The fast development of avatar-mediated interaction has shifted the consumer-brand interaction process from traditional screen-based and physical environment to immersive metaverse environment. In this regard, the current paper aims to provide an overview of the theory and empirics on the topic of self-congruity in avatar-mediated consumer-brand interaction in metaverse environment. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework was used to select peer-reviewed literature on this topic from Scopus, Web of Science, and the Korean Citation Index. Of 347 papers screened, 28 papers met inclusion and exclusion criteria. This paper reviews four dominant theories that guide consumer behavior in the context of avatars: the digital doppelgänger theory, embodied self-extension theory, dual congruity integration theory, and cross-reality transference theory. As per the findings, it is found that the configurational features of avatars, such as similarity in appearance, anthropomorphism, customization, and avatar intimacy, have an impact on avatar-self congruence, which in turn affects flow and affective responses, which are psychological mechanisms connected with virtual purchase intention, real purchase intention, and brand loyalty. Avatar-self congruence is also different from the conventional brand-self congruence on account of digital embodiment, mutual identity influence, cross-reality spill-over, and ambiguity contingent process. In light of the synthesis, the proposed study develops a structural model comprising of eight latent variables and ten hypotheses using structural equation modeling. This study provides the research gaps both in methodology and theories along with a research agenda comprising longitudinal designs, experimen

latest.title: Operational strategies for managing purchase decisions in festival shopping: Analyzing the role of fear of missing out (FOMO) in the digital transformation era
latest.venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
latest.abstract: Purpose: For most consumers who experience fear of missing out, regret related to falling behind trends outweighs regret related to financial costs. In fact, the intensity of the attraction created through fear of missing out is positively correlated with impulse buying, which potentially reduces self-control during shopping activities. Hence, fear of missing out is considered a psychological disorder that affects the mental health of the individual. Therefore, this study aims to explain the reactive-behavioral outcomes (e.g., impulsive buying decisions) by emphasizing the perceptual drivers of the 'Fear Of Missing Out' (FOMO) phenomenon within the context of festival shopping opportunities in the digital transformation era.Methodology: This study is a basic-applied research based on its purpose and a mixed research based on its research strategy. The qualitative strategy used in the first stage of the research is grounded theory and the quantitative strategies used in this survey-correlational research. The qualitative participants included marketing and sales consultants as well as professors of business, marketing, and e-commerce, 10 of whom were selected as participants through non-probability judgmental sampling. The statistical population of the quantitative part of the study is people who visited various festivals and made various purchases.The sampling method in the quantitative section was random, and the sample size was determined to be 221 participants based on relationship of Cohen. To prevent sample attrition, about 240 questionnaires were distributed in this study and 229 questionnaires were returned to the researcher.Findings: The results showed that perceptual drivers (positive customer perception of the brand, deceptive advertising, customer experience,

latest.title: Brand Love, Customer Brand Engagement, and Brand Pride as Predictors of Brand Defense among Indonesian iPhone 17 Series Users
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines how brand love, customer brand engagement, brand pride, and regulatory focus are associated with brand defense among Indonesian iPhone 17 Series users. Cross-sectional data from 350 respondents recruited through purposive sampling were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. Brand love was positively associated with customer brand engagement, which was positively associated with brand defense. The direct association between brand love and brand defense was nonsignificant, whereas the indirect association through customer brand engagement was significant, supporting a pattern of indirect-only mediation. Brand pride also showed a positive direct association with brand defense. Promotion focus and prevention focus did not significantly moderate either the brand love-engagement association or the corresponding indirect association, indicating that regulatory focus did not function as a boundary condition in this context. Together, the proposed predictors explained 50.9% of the variance in brand defense. The findings extend the consumer-brand relationship perspective by identifying customer brand engagement as a relational pathway linking brand love with brand defense and brand pride as a complementary identity-related predictor. These findings provide insight into why consumers defend identity-relevant premium brands and highlight engagement and brand pride as important considerations for brand management.

latest.title: Impact of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love: Evidence from the Luxury Fashion Industry in Egypt
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love in the luxury fashion industry in Egypt, building upon literature on the effect of packaging attributes as a multidimensional concept that extends beyond its protective function to include visual, functional, environmental, and experiential attributes on brand love towards luxury fashion brands. This study is theoretically grounded in the combination of the Cue Utilization Theory, Signaling Theory, and Attachment Theory to examine how packaging attributes shape consumers' emotional responses and strengthen brand love. This research employed a quantitative approach, using an online questionnaire to collect data from 440 luxury fashion consumers via River sampling, and the relationships were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics software using Multiple linear regression. Results demonstrated that packaging attributes have significant impact on brand love, with each packaging attribute contributing differently to brand love; thereby, visual, functional, and experiential packaging attributes positively impact brand love, whereas environmental packaging attributes were not a statistically significant predictor of brand love. Findings contribute evidence from the Egyptian market, offering practical implications for luxury fashion brands and marketers, highlighting packaging as a strategic tool to strengthen consumers’ emotional attachment to the brand, and supporting competitiveness in the luxury fashion market.

latest.title: The Indonesian hedonic trap: Exploring consumer attitudes and legal risks in counterfeit luxury purchases
latest.abstract: The relationship between hedonism, the impression of legal danger, and customer attitudes about luxury fashion counterfeit products is explored in this study. Data was collected from 385 respondents in East Java, Indonesia, using multistage sampling and using structural equation modelling (SEM) analysis, with a focus on those who had previously purchased counterfeit products. The results show that consumer perceives and intention to buy for counterfeit luxury products are positively influenced by hedonism. However, this effect is considerably moderated by legal risk perception, which lowers intention to buy among individuals who are legally risk orientated. This study provides an overview of the consumption of counterfeit products by integrating legal (risk perception) and psychological (hedonism) perspectives. Further psychological and socioeconomic elements influencing the purchase of counterfeit products should be investigated in future studies. These results can be used by policymakers and brand owners to create effective consumer education initiatives and legal enforcement strategies to minimise the use of counterfeit products.

latest.title: Why Parent Brand Trust Is Not Enough? Entitativity, Perceived Quality, and Perceived Risk in Life Insurance Trust Transfer
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This research investigates the mechanisms by which trust transfers from prominent parent brands to their affiliated life insurance sub-brands in Indonesia. While consumers may trust established conglomerates, this trust may not automatically translate into credibility for their life insurance extensions. The study examines how entitativity, operationalized as perceived similarity and brand tie, together with perceived quality and perceived risk, facilitate sub-brand trust and behavioral intention. Using a quantitative survey approach, data from 483 valid respondents were evaluated via Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The analysis identified a significant but weak direct effect of parent brand trust on sub-brand trust. This shows that a reputable parent brand may help establish initial trust, but cannot substitute for the consumer’s own evaluation of the life insurance sub-brand. Clearer parent–sub-brand unity, higher perceived quality, and lower perceived risk promote trust in the sub-brand, which is a significant driver of behavioral intention. This data was limited to only Indonesian respondents. This study contributes to trust transfer literature by conceptualizing entitativity as a higher-order construct in hierarchical brand relationships, offering practical guidance for life insurance companies to leverage parent brand equity through service excellence and clearer brand integration.

latest.title: Innovative Operation Ideas of Guangxi Agricultural Assistance Platform from a Demand-Side Orientation: A Case Study of "Mang Xiaozhong"
latest.abstract: In recent years, with the deep penetration of the digital economy into rural areas and the rapid development of agricultural e-commerce in Guangxi, the demand-side oriented agricultural assistance model has emerged as an innovative form of agricultural product circulation. In response to problems in the upward distribution of characteristic agricultural products in Guangxi—including disconnection between production and marketing, high loss in circulation links, difficulties in brand transformation, and seasonal capital shortage at the production end—the "Mang Xiaozhong" platform constructs four interconnected operation strategies: customized pre-sale, two-way exchange among production areas, rule-based trust design, and consumer-side pre-purchase crowdfunding. These strategies adapt to the industrial reality of decentralized smallholder production and staggered listing of multiple categories in Guangxi. The research shows that the demand-side oriented, asset-light third-party service model can address the practical bottlenecks of county-level agricultural assistance e-commerce in Guangxi, and has reference value for the construction of similar platforms.

latest.title: Pengaruh Analisis Brand Identity dan Brand Image terhadap Brand Awareness Produk iPhone di Kalangan Generasi Z (Studi pada Mahasiswa FEB Universitas Pancasila)
latest.abstract: This research aims to determine the influence of Brand Identity and Brand Image on Brand Awareness of iPhone products among Generation Z. The respondents in this study were iPhone users from the Faculty of Economics and Business at Universitas Pancasila. The sampling method used was non-probability sampling with a purposive sampling technique, and the total sample tested consisted of 100 respondents. The data collection instrument used was a questionnaire distributed through Google Forms. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression analysis, classical assumption tests, hypothesis testing, and processed using SPSS 22. The results of the study indicate that Brand Identity has a positive effect on Brand Awareness, Brand Image has a positive effect on Brand Awareness, and Brand Identity and Brand Image simultaneously have a positive effect on Brand Awareness.

latest.title: Pengalaman Pengunjung Nissin Café dan Emporium: Studi Kualitatif Experiential Marketing dalam Pengenalan Produk
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan mengeksplorasi pengalaman pengunjung Nissin Café & Emporium melalui lima dimensi experiential marketing serta menafsirkan keterkaitannya dengan pengenalan produk PT Nissin Biscuit Indonesia. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan observasi langsung dan wawancara daring terhadap tiga pengunjung yang dipilih secara purposif berdasarkan pengalaman berkunjung dan membeli atau mengonsumsi produk. Pernyataan wawancara yang terdokumentasi diorganisasi secara tematik dengan kerangka Strategic Experiential Modules, yaitu sense, feel, think, act, dan relate. Hasil menunjukkan pengalaman sensorik berupa aroma biskuit dan tampilan produk; kesan emosional mengenai suasana kafe dalam lingkungan pabrik; persepsi pembelajaran tentang proses produksi dan pengendalian kualitas; ketertarikan untuk mencoba atau membeli produk; serta niat membagikan pengalaman kepada orang lain. Analisis menempatkan tur industri, kafe, dan Emporium sebagai titik interaksi yang menyediakan bentuk pengenalan produk yang berbeda. Temuan berkontribusi pada pemahaman kontekstual tentang pengalaman pengunjung dalam lingkungan manufaktur pangan yang menggabungkan aktivitas edukatif dan komersial. Karena terbatas pada tiga informan dan kutipan wawancara yang tersedia, penelitian tidak dapat membuktikan peningkatan objektif pengetahuan, brand awareness, transaksi, atau loyalitas konsumen.

latest.title: THE MEDIATING FUNCTION OF PERCEIVED CREDIBILITY IN THE IMPACT OF SUSTAINABILITY REPORT QUALITY ON INVESTOR TRUST
latest.venue: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationship between investor trust and perceived sustainability reporting quality, paying special attention to the mediating function of perceived credibility. The study creates an integrated framework based on signaling theory and information asymmetry theory to explain how investors understand sustainability disclosures and convert their evaluations into trust in reporting firms. In particular, the study looks at the direct connections between investor trust, perceived sustainability reporting quality, and perceived credibility. It also evaluates whether credibility may explain the relationship between investor confidence and reporting quality. Individual investors and representatives of institutional investors in Vietnam provided survey data. With investor type included as a control variable and bootstrapping used to assess the mediating link, covariance-based structural equation modeling was used to analyze the suggested correlations. The results show that investor trust and perceived credibility are positively correlated with higher perceived sustainability reporting quality. Additionally, investor trust and perceived credibility are positively correlated, and the relationship between reporting quality and trust is partially mediated by perceived credibility. These results imply that sustainability disclosures boost investor confidence by increasing the credibility that investors assign to company information in addition to its perceived quality. The scientific uniqueness of the study is the identification of perceived credibility as a unique explanatory mechanism that links investor trust in an emerging capital market with sustainability reporting quality. The study expands on current debates on sustainability disclosure and investor decis

latest.title: Customer Focus Program (CFP) in a Regulation-Constrained Category: A Field-Based Qualitative Study of Distribution and Merchandising Execution in India's Organized Cigarette Trade
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose: In categories where mass advertising and open promotion are legally prohibited, the sales and distribution system becomes the main route through which a firm can express customer orientation. This paper examines how a Customer Focus Program (CFC) operates at the point of sale in the cigarette sales and distribution network of a large Indian fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) organisation. Design/methodology/approach: The study is a descriptive, qualitative, field-observation-based case study conducted over a two-month period (15 May to 15 July 2026) in the Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) territory of Maharashtra. Observations were recorded during accompanied market visits across convenience, grocery, wholesale, sub-wholesale, stockist, moped and van direct-selling channels, using a four-field recording format (objective, activity observed, practical observation, relevance to customer focus). Observations were mapped to an Availability–Visibility–Freshness (AVF) framework and to an eight-step CFC field-execution flow. Findings: Four findings emerge. (1) Availability is produced by layered, complementary coverage formats rather than by any single actor. (2) Effective execution must be segment-aware and margin-aware, because retailers' stocking and promotion choices respond jointly to product segment and trade pricing structure. (3) Merchandising and planogram discipline is the primary visibility lever when above-the-line promotion is unavailable. (4) The salesman–retailer relationship is the mechanism that sustains the program. Originality/value: The paper offers a field-grounded account of customer orientation as enacted at the last mile in a heavily regulated category, an area where the marketing-channels and customer-orientation literatures rarely meet. It proposes

latest.title: Cross-Sectoral Patterns of Circular Consumption Behaviours: Evidence from R-Strategies
latest.abstract: Transitioning to a circular economy requires not only systemic and technological change but also consumer engagement in circular practices. While circular economy research has extensively examined R-strategy frameworks, existing studies have largely focused on organisational and supply-side perspectives, with limited attention to how these strategies are reflected in consumer behaviour across product domains and how such behaviours can be addressed through policy. This study investigates reported circular consumption behaviour across three key product sectors: household appliances, consumer electronics and apparel. Drawing on data from a survey of 1,000 adult consumers in Poland, the analysis focuses on seven consumer-relevant R-strategies derived from the wider 9R framework: Refuse, Rethink, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Repurpose and Recycle. The study examines sector-specific reported prevalence, cross-sectoral reach and associations between analogous behaviours across sectors. The results show that prolonged product use, mapped to Rethink in this study, is the most commonly reported practice and has the broadest cross-sectoral reach. Refuse and Repurpose show lower prevalence and narrower cross-sectoral reach. At the same time, analogous circular practices are positively associated across product sectors, indicating that circular consumption is sector-sensitive but partly interconnected. Exploratory CART analyses further indicate that these pairwise associations are accompanied by hierarchical and subgroup-specific cross-sectoral patterns. These findings provide new insights for consumer policy. They suggest value in considering both sector-sensitive instruments and broader practice-based approaches. Product longevity represents a relatively widespread cross-sectoral pract

latest.title: Consumer Complaints, Loyalty Risk, and Cancellation Intention in Digital Subscription Platforms: A Text Mining Analysis
latest.abstract: This study examines consumer complaints regarding digital video subscription platforms using data collected from Şikayetvar, Türkiye’s largest online consumer complaint platform. The study aims to identify the dominant themes underlying consumer complaints, compare thematic distributions across platforms, and explore loyalty-related textual indicators and explicit cancellation-related expressions embedded in complaint texts. A total of 2,005 complaints related to Netflix, Exxen, and Gain were analyzed. After a series of preprocessing steps, complaint texts were vectorized using TF-IDF and analyzed using Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF). Seven major complaint themes were identified, including billing and refund issues, subscription management problems, technical access difficulties, content-related concerns, promotional issues, sports broadcasting and live-stream access problems, and payment security complaints. Chi-square analysis revealed significant differences in thematic complaint distributions across platforms. In addition, loyalty risk indicators differed significantly among platforms according to Kruskal–Wallis test results. Logistic regression analysis showed that platform type and complaint themes were significantly associated with explicit cancellation-related expressions identified in the complaint texts. The findings suggest that online complaint data can provide valuable insights into customer dissatisfaction patterns and may serve as a useful monitoring tool for identifying potential loyalty-related risks in digital subscription services. The study contributes to the growing literature on text mining and digital consumer behavior by providing evidence from Turkish-language complaint data and offering a reproducible framework for complaint-based cust
