Data analysis and hypothesis testing were performed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 4.0. The results showed that, except for the direct effects of information usefulness and quantity pressure, which were not statistically significant, all hypothesized relationships were supported. Additionally, the findings confirmed the moderating effect of financial capacity and the relevance of demographic controls in explaining impulsive buying behavior. The study offers insights for marketers and policymakers and provides recommendations for future research. This study also advances the theoretical understanding of consumer behavior in e-commerce by affirming psychological theories that link heightened emotional arousal to diminished self-control, thereby fostering impulsive purchasing.

hot.title: “Being” with the brand in the metaverse: Strengthening brand anthropomorphism to foster brand love
hot.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
hot.abstract: This study examines brand experience within a virtual reality-based (VR) metaverse by proposing a model to understand the influence of telepresence and brand avatar social presence (BASP) on brand anthropomorphism (BA) and the relationship between BA and brand love. A survey of 349 Generation Z users on Roblox showed a positive impact of telepresence and BASP on BA, which fosters brand love. The findings highlight the unexpected and controversial moderating role of VR attitudes. This research contributes to the literature on VR perceptions and BA and offers valuable managerial insights into consumer–brand encounters in VR-based metaverses.

hot.title: Are Retail Consumers Willing to Pay for All Circular Products? A Study on Consumer Perception of the Circular Economy in Retail
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The planetary crisis, stemming from overconsumption and unsustainable production patterns, necessitates a shift towards balanced economic, environmental and social growth. The circular economy presents a promising solution by promoting material recirculation. While its success relies on collaboration among various stakeholders, consumers are crucial for accepting circular economy products and business models. However, despite increasing environmental awareness, the literature shows that many consumers resist purchasing previously used products due to perceived inferiority, risk and low quality, which could hinder the adoption of circular economy products. Understanding consumer behaviour, particularly their willingness to buy and pay for circular economy products, is essential for businesses seeking to promote sustainable consumption and achieve market growth. This study investigates consumer perceptions of circular economy, using simplified terms of reused, recycled and recovered, across 11 product categories through a quantitative survey of 607 Australian respondents. The results indicate that personal financial benefits are prioritised over ecological reasons, and there is variability in perceived product performance across categories. Additionally, price sensitivity and affordability play a key role in consumer decision‐making. Notably, while younger and male consumers show a greater inclination to purchase circular economy products, the broader consumer base remains unwilling to pay a premium. These insights can guide businesses and policymakers in developing targeted strategies emphasising price, functionality and quality to enhance consumer acceptance and adoption of circular economy products. We advance theory by demonstrating that consumer decisions ar

hot.title: Exploring the Duality of Perceptions: Insights into Uncertainties, Aversion and Appreciation Towards Algorithmic HRM
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The human resource management (HRM) function has witnessed the rapid integration of algorithms into incumbent processes; however, significant employee resistance and aversion to algorithmic decision‐making have also been reported. Research on algorithmic HRM practices indicates an underlying duality of perceptual responses by HRM professionals towards this technology. We seek to understand how HRM professionals experience algorithmic HRM use and determine if there are bright sides to its organizational integration. We undertake a qualitative, open‐ended study based on written responses to open‐ended questions from 58 respondents in the United Kingdom and the United States of America. The data were thematically analyzed using grounded theory, which revealed four themes representing HRM professionals' overarching perspectives on why algorithmic HRM precipitates aversion or appreciation. The first two themes highlight HRM professionals' perceived subjective uncertainty regarding algorithmic HRM and its perceived negative effects on the organization. The third theme acknowledges the positive effect of algorithmic HRM, and the final theme discusses three critical coping strategies (embrace, avoid, and collaborate) that HRM professionals adopt to counteract their experienced fears. Our findings suggest that HRM professionals adopt a cautiously fearful rather than a wholly adverse outlook towards algorithmic HRM, wherein aversion and appreciation appear to emerge simultaneously. We contend this existence of a duality of perceptual responses to algorithmic HRM may be a precursor to setting a harmonious collaboration between humans and algorithms in the HRM domain, contingent on appropriate levels of oversight and governance. Implications for theory and managerial pract
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The algorithm of friendship: literature review and integrative model of relationships between humans and artificial intelligence (AI)
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) tools become increasingly common and used in people's day-to-day lives, the relationships they develop with people will become deeper and more prevalent. This pattern is emphasised by AI technologies becoming more complex in understanding emotions and the human psyche. As we witness a wave of AI tools that enter almost all domains, it is crucial to understand these relationships, their antecedents, their outcomes, and how scholars and practitioners can design them better to improve people's experiences and promote well-being. Thus, we traced the existing scientific knowledge regarding the development of emotional relationships between people and AI agents, the types of such relationships, and their effect on humans. To do so, we conducted a systematic literature review that analysed 38 peer-reviewed empirical studies focusing on human-AI emotional relationships. We present a detailed integrative review of the results, propose a human AI relationship formation model, discuss some caveats in current research, and outline avenues for future research.

hot.title: Using Augmented Reality to Strengthen Consumer/Brand Relationships: The Case of Luxury Brands
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT Though augmented reality (AR) is increasingly adopted in marketing, its capacity to foster consumers' engagement and attachment remain tenuous, exposing an important literature‐based gap. Addressing this gap, we deploy social presence theory and luxury consumption theory to develop and test a model that proposes that consumers' engagement with AR‐deploying luxury brands drives the development of their perceived brand warmth, social value, and brand competence, in turn impacting their brand attachment. To explore these issues, we draw on survey data from a sample of 537 luxury apparel and automotive consumers. The results using structural equation modelling (SEM) show that first, luxury consumers who exhibit high engagement with the AR‐deploying brand perceive higher levels of brand warmth, ‐competence, and social value, in turn raising their attachment to the AR‐deploying luxury brand. Overall, the findings highlight AR's strategic capacity to engage consumers and raise the brand's perceived brand warmth, competence, and social value, in turn boosting individuals' attachment to the AR‐deploying brand.

hot.title: Luxury: Where Next?
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The luxury industry is undergoing a complex evolution in response to increasingly polarized societies, multicultural audiences, and frantically digitized marketplaces, balancing tradition with innovation and exclusivity with accessibility. As luxury consumption shifts from conspicuous to inconspicuous, from offline to online, and from traditional goods to experiences, consumer expectations are becoming increasingly nuanced. Addressing these new dynamic trends, this article provides insights into the current luxury research within marketing. We identify three major thematic areas shaping the field: the emergence of luxury identities, the integration of sustainability and ESG, and the acceleration of digital transformation. Each theme is enriched by sub‐themes addressing current and future challenges. We offer a forward‐looking research agenda that highlights significant theoretical and practical implications for luxury brand management in modern marketplaces, which are simultaneously democratized yet paradoxically exclusive. These multifaceted directions are aimed to foster the evolution of luxury research in alignment with societal and technological advancements.

hot.title: Food packaging business models as drivers for sustainability in the food packaging industry
hot.abstract: The global food packaging industry faces severe environmental challenges due to its reliance on plastics and the growing demand for convenience. In Europe, food packaging alone accounts for 40.5% of all plastic production, yet only 35% of this waste is recycled. The purpose of this study is to examine business models, technological innovations (like AI, IoT, and blockchain) and the relation with customers to support the transition to a circular economy in food packaging. The research focuses on models such as Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) and reusable and returnable packaging systems, evaluating their potential to minimize environmental impact. A key aspect of the investigation is consumer behavior. While consumers express a preference for sustainable options, actual purchasing decisions often prioritize cost and convenience. The study explores how emerging technologies are transforming packaging design by enhancing product safety and improving supply chain transparency. Additionally, regulatory frameworks, particularly within the European Union, such as the Single-Use Plastics Directive (SUPD) and the Circular Economy Action Plan (CEAP), are driving industry-wide changes toward sustainability. However, disparities in adoption and regulatory compliance on a global scale present significant challenges to implementation. The outcome of this study is a set of strategic recommendations aimed at policymakers, industry leaders, and researchers. These recommendations emphasize the importance of harmonizing global regulations to support sustainable packaging practices, increasing investment in innovation and infrastructure, and balancing the relation between industry and consumers to bridge the gap between intention or preferences and action or behavior.

latest.title: Pemanfaatan Microsoft Excel Dalam Pengelolaan Keuangan Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) Perspektif Hukum Ekonomi Syariah
latest.abstract: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) need orderly financial records to monitor business activities, assess performance, and make responsible economic decisions. For Muslim-owned or sharia-oriented MSMEs, financial administration also has a normative dimension: transactions should be recorded transparently, agreements should be clear, and business practices should avoid riba, gharar, and maysir. This article examines the use of Microsoft Excel in MSME financial management from the perspective of Islamic economic law. It applies a descriptive qualitative literature-review method combined with a normative-conceptual analysis of sharia business principles, relevant regulations, and studies on spreadsheet-based accounting and sharia-oriented MSMEs. The literature indicates that Excel can assist transaction recording, cash-flow monitoring, cost calculation, inventory control, and preparation of financial summaries. From an Islamic economic law perspective, these functions may support the principles of amanah, shiddiq, ‘adl, transparency, and protection of wealth (hifz al-mal), provided that the workbook records the substance of transactions accurately. For transactions using contracts such as murabahah, mudharabah, musyarakah, or ijarah, the records should identify the contract, parties, object, price or capital contribution, agreed margin or profit-sharing ratio, payment schedule, and outstanding obligations as relevant. Excel itself does not certify sharia compliance; that assessment depends on the validity of the contract and the actual conduct of the parties. The article concludes that Excel is a practical initial tool for MSMEs when supported by clear procedures, adequate user knowledge, internal checks, and accounting treatment appropriate to the transaction and

latest.title: Analysis of Instagram Digital Marketing and Product Quality, on Repurchase Intention in Tenpura Jakarta
latest.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effects of Instagram digital marketing and product quality on customers' repurchase intention at Tenpura Jakarta, a restaurant located in Blok M, South Jakarta. A quantitative research design with an associative approach was employed. Data were collected through questionnaires administered to 100 respondents selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression analysis with IBM SPSS Statistics. The results revealed that digital marketing had a positive and statistically significant relationship with repurchase intention, with a reported correlation coefficient (r) of 0.420 and a significance level of p < 0.001. Conversely, product quality was not significantly associated with repurchase intention (r = ?0.019, p = 0.849). The overall regression model was statistically significant (F = 10.492), with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.178, indicating that digital marketing and product quality collectively explained 17.8% of the variance in repurchase intention. These findings suggest that Instagram digital marketing was more strongly associated with customers' repurchase intention than product quality in the context of Tenpura Jakarta. The study highlights the importance of optimizing Instagram digital marketing strategies and recommends examining additional factors, such as brand image and customer experience, to better understand and potentially enhance customers' repurchase intention.

latest.title: Menjembatani Kesenjangan Sustainability Marketing melalui Perceived Sustainability Value
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini mengintegrasikan Price Sensitivity, Green Trust, dan Sustainability Awareness ke dalam satu model mediasi tunggal dengan Perceived Value Sustainability sebagai mekanisme penghubung menuju Sustainability Purchase Behavior, pada konteks konsumen Generasi Z Indonesia. Kesenjangan antara niat dan perilaku aktual menjadi persoalan mendasar yang membuat sustainability marketing di Indonesia belum berjalan efektif, meskipun survei terbaru menunjukkan mayoritas konsumen bersedia membayar lebih untuk produk ramah lingkungan. Studi ini menguji ketiga variabel tersebut membentuk Sustainability Purchase Behavior, baik secara langsung maupun lewat mediasi, pada konsumen Generasi Z produk food and beverage di Kota Semarang. Data dikumpulkan dari 150 responden mahasiswa Generasi Z yang pernah membeli produk F&B berkelanjutan melalui teknik accidental sampling, lalu dianalisis dengan Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) menggunakan SmartPLS 4. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Price Sensitivity berpengaruh negatif signifikan secara langsung terhadap Sustainability Purchase Behavior namun berbalik positif signifikan ketika dimediasi Perceived Value Sustainability, sebuah pola inconsistent mediation. Secara teoretis, temuan ini memperluas Value Belief Norm Theory dengan menunjukkan bahwa norma pribadi pendukung lingkungan hijau tidak otomatis berubah menjadi tindakan tanpa melewati proses evaluasi nilai Expectancy Disconfirmation terlebih dahulu, sehingga kedua teori tersebut dipahami sebagai proses berjenjang, bukan mekanisme yang bisa berdiri-sendiri. Implikasinya, strategi pemasaran tidak hanya sekadar edukasi kesadaran namun penguatan persepsi nilai keberlanjutan dan dapat dirasakan konsumen.

latest.title: The Mediating Role of Consumer Satisfaction in The Influence of Trust and Service Quality on Streetwear Purchase Decisions on Shopee
latest.abstract: Background: The rapid expansion of digital marketplaces has heightened the significance of consumer trust, service quality, and satisfaction in determining online purchase decisions, especially among Generation Z buyers who acquire streetwear products via Shopee. Objective: This research investigates the direct influence of consumer trust and service quality on purchase decisions and assesses the mediating function of consumer satisfaction among Generation Z consumers residing in Serang City. Methods: An explanatory quantitative survey involving 100 respondents chosen via purposive sampling was carried out. The data were gathered through a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and processed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 20, encompassing validity and reliability examinations, classical assumption tests, simple and multiple linear regression, t-tests, F-tests, coefficients of determination, and Sobel mediation analysis. Results: Both consumer trust and service quality exerted positive and significant direct effects on purchase decisions as well as on consumer satisfaction, whereas consumer satisfaction likewise positively and significantly influenced purchase decisions. The Sobel analyses verified significant mediation for trust (Z = 5.396) and for service quality (Z = 5.771). Within the simultaneous model, consumer satisfaction stayed significant, and the model accounted for 61.0% of the variance in purchase decisions. Conclusion: Consumer satisfaction occupies a pivotal mediating position in converting consumer trust and perceived service quality into streetwear purchase decisions on Shopee. These results suggest that sellers and marketplace managers ought to combine trust-building, service enhancement, and satisfaction management to reinforce purchasing outcomes.

latest.title: EVALUATING SERVICE PERFORMANCE AND PRICING PRACTICES IN BANJARMASIN CAR WASH SERVICES
latest.venue: INJOSEDU: International Journal of Social and Education
latest.abstract: This study examines how perceived service quality and price fairness contribute to customer satisfaction in Banjarmasin car wash services and identifies attributes with potential for managerial improvement. Using a focused reanalysis of cross-sectional survey responses from 200 customers selected through purposive sampling, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA) in SmartPLS 4, with Customer Satisfaction as the target construct. Both Service Quality and Price Fairness showed positive, statistically significant relationships with satisfaction (p < .001), and the model explained 59.3% of its variance. At the construct level, Service Quality demonstrated greater importance (0.642) and performance (75.03) than Price Fairness (importance 0.406; performance 68.40). Indicator-level analysis identified Empathy (SQ5) as the most important attribute, while Price Transparency (PF1) had the lowest perceived performance. These findings suggest that maintaining customer-oriented service standards and reviewing the clarity and perceived consistency of pricing are complementary managerial considerations. By integrating model-based importance with perceived performance, IPMA provides more targeted guidance than structural coefficients or customer ratings considered separately.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: PRICING STRATEGY OPTIMIZATION FOR TRADITIONAL SCENTED CANDLE PRODUCTS IN DIFFERENTIATED LUXURY GOODS MARKETS
latest.abstract: Pricing strategy was a factor of competitive advantage in the markets for luxury goods in which product value, brand and differentiation are determinants of consumer’s choices. The approach may allow premium positioning and competitive advantage. This research investigates Pricing Strategy Optimization (PSO) for traditional scented candles, focusing on Consumer Price Perception (CPP), Brand Equity (BE), Sales Volume (SV), Customer Retention (CR), and Overall Market Performance (OMP). The research was carried out with 285 respondents from various fields including marketing managers, executives, and managers working in luxury candle companies. 5-point Likert scale structured questionnaires were distributed through online and physical mediums. Quantitative data were analysed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) 27 through descriptive statistics, correlation, regression, and reliability analysis. It examined production costs, scent complexity, packaging exclusivity, and brand positioning as key pricing determinants. Results revealed positive correlations between pricing strategy optimization and overall market performance (r = 0.66), consumer price perception (r = 0.62), and brand equity (r = 0.58). Regression analysis indicated positive relationships with consumer price perception (β = 0.68), overall market performance (β = 0.65), brand equity (β = 0.62), customer retention (β = 0.59), and sales volume (β = 0.54). Reliability analysis demonstrated acceptable internal consistency across all variables. The results highlight the importance of including product differentiation, perceived value, and brand positioning into pricing decisions. This provides empirical findings to assist in pricing decisions, which may ultimately improve competitiveness and s

latest.title: Rethinking retail patronage: beyond customer loyalty towards reciprocal customer–retailer relationships
latest.venue: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This research clarifies retail patronage by combining consumer insights with bibliometric analysis to address conceptual fragmentation and support consistent measurement. Design/methodology/approach We combined qualitative interviews (n = 68) with a bibliometric analysis of 233 articles using Bibliometrix. Five experts provided an interpretive evaluation of the integrated findings. Findings Retail patronage emerges as a multidimensional relational construct integrating behavioural, intentional, and attitudinal components while remaining conceptually distinguishable from loyalty and love. The literature structures around antecedents and methodological foundations. Patronage occurs when repeated behaviour is relationally interpreted rather than situational. Practical implications Retailers should complement behavioural metrics with relational indicators to distinguish routine purchasing from genuine patronage and design relationship-focused loyalty programmes. Originality/value The study integrates consumer perspectives and intellectual foundations, positioning retail patronage as a reciprocal relational exchange construct to provide a basis for scale development. It explains why repetition can occur without loyalty and loyalty without patronage. The findings suggest that retail patronage extends beyond behavioural loyalty by reflecting reciprocal customer–retailer relationships grounded in ongoing relational exchange.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Tracking Every Dollar: How Do Information Sources Support Budgeting?
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Budgeting is widely recognized as a key contributor to financial well‐being, yet little is known about how people gather the information needed to track expenses, how this shapes the quality of expense records, or whether that quality matters for household finances. Using nationally representative data from the 2023 Survey and Diary of Consumer Payment Choice, we show that individuals rely on multiple information sources when recalling expenses, with 65% using several simultaneously. Employing more sources is associated with higher tracking data quality (fewer imprecise and incomplete records), and consulting financial records and receipts outperforms memory. We further find that greater precision in recorded amounts is associated with stronger household financial resilience, including absorbing an emergency expense and avoiding cash‐flow‐related fees. These findings offer new evidence on everyday budgeting and suggest that multi‐source tracking may strengthen budgeting effectiveness.

latest.title: ANALISIS PENGARUH HARGA, PROMOSI, DAN CITRA MEREK TERHADAP KEPUTUSAN PEMBELIAN KONSUMEN ES KRIM MIXUE DI KOTA JAYAPURA
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui variabel harga, promosi dan citra merek berpengaruh signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian es krim mixue di kota Jayapura. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kuantitatif deskriptif. Populasi dalam penelitian ini adalah konsumen es krim mixue di kota Jayapura. Sampel penelitian ini berjumlah 100 orang. Teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan teknik non probability sampling dengan metode purposive sampling. Teknik pengumpulan data yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini melalui penyebaran kuesioner. Data analisis menggunakan uji validasi, reliabilitas, normalitas, multikolinearitas, uji t, uji f, dan regresi linier berganda dengan bantuan SPSS versi 27.0. Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa: (1) variabel harga secara parsial berpengaruh dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian, (2) variabel promosi secara parsial berpengaruh dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian, (3) variabel citra merek secara parsial berpengaruh dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian, (4) variabel harga bukan merupakan variabel yang paling dominan terhadap keputusan pembelian.

latest.title: The Effect of Service Quality and Product Variety on Customer Loyalty with Customer Satisfaction as a Mediating Variable at Mitra Swalayan in Pujud District
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Technology and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study investigates whether service quality and product variety are associated with customer loyalty at Mitra Swalayan in Pujud District, Rokan Hilir, Riau, and whether customer satisfaction explains part of these relationships. A quantitative survey was conducted with 118 customers, and the data were examined through multiple regression, path analysis, and the Sobel test. The results show that service quality and product variety are positively and significantly related to customer satisfaction and customer loyalty. Customer satisfaction is also positively and significantly related to loyalty. The mediation tests indicate significant indirect relationships from service quality and product variety to loyalty through satisfaction. The findings highlight the importance of combining reliable service delivery with an assortment that fits customer needs. For retail management, attention to both operational service performance and relevant product choices can help strengthen satisfaction and customer loyalty
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: The influence of financial education on the co-holding puzzle
latest.abstract: We collect 36 RCT-studies with 213,000 participants that report the effects of financial education on both savings and borrowing. Financial education increases not just savings but also borrowing outcomes. These changes are positively correlated at the study level, consistent with the individual-level results from related literature establishing the co-holding puzzle. However, the relation between changes in saving and borrowing is significantly smaller in the subsample without financial institutions than in the subsample with financial institutions. This cautiously indicates that the kind of implementing institution may play a role if financial education is intended to moderate the co-holding puzzle.

latest.title: Social Media Marketing, Personal Selling, and Price Perception on Purchase Decision through Purchase Intention with Experience Environment as a Moderator
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of social media marketing, personal selling, and price perception on purchase decision, mediated by purchase intention and moderated by experience environment, within the Indonesian residential property sector. Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior, Servicescape theory, and the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, an integrative model is tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) on data collected from 304 confirmed buyers at CitraLand Tallasa City Makassar. Results confirm that price perception constitutes the dominant predictor of purchase intention, followed by social media marketing, while personal selling yields a non-significant sufficiency-based effect. Purchase intention and experience environment both exert significant direct effects on purchase decision. Purchase intention fully mediates the effects of price perception and social media marketing on purchase decision, whereas the hypothesised moderating role of experience environment is not supported. NCA establishes that all five constructs represent necessary conditions of medium magnitude, with experience environment imposing the most binding prerequisite constraint. The integrated NCA–PLS-SEM approach reveals that achieving superior purchase decision outcomes demands simultaneously adequate performance across all conditions. These findings advance theoretical understanding of high-involvement consumer decision-making and provide actionable guidance for property developers in emerging residential markets.

latest.title: Financial psychological characteristics and psychological well-being: The mediating role of financial well-being
latest.abstract: Psychological well-being plays an important role in many aspects of life, but its relationship with financial factors remains insufficiently explored. This study aims to examine whether financial well-being can serve as a mediator between five financial psychological characteristics and psychological well-being. Drawing on the conservation of resources theory, this research focuses on materialism, financial self-efficacy, financial risk tolerance, external locus of control, and propensity to plan as financial psychological characteristics. Data were collected from 157 respondents aged 18 to 60 years old in Indonesia who actively managed their finances, and analyzed using PLS-SEM. The results show that materialism, financial self-efficacy, and propensity to plan positively affect financial well-being, while financial risk tolerance and external locus of control do not. Furthermore, financial well-being can enhance psychological well-being and act as a mediator of the relationships between materialism, financial self-efficacy, and the propensity to plan on psychological well-being.

latest.title: Factors Influencing Online Purchase Decisions at SPAR Botswana: Evidence from Selected SPAR Stores in Botswana
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Business Studies
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of digital marketing has transformed consumer purchasing behaviour and the retail landscape globally. Although online shopping continues to expand across developed and developing economies, limited empirical evidence exists regarding the factors influencing online purchase decisions in Botswana's retail sector. This study investigated the factors influencing consumers' online purchase decisions at SPAR Botswana. The study was underpinned by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Uses and Gratification Theory (UGT). An interpretivist research philosophy, descriptive research design and qualitative research approach were adopted. Data were collected through structured interviews from 30 participants comprising twenty-five customers and five managers selected from Mogoditshane, Mmopane and Railpark SPAR stores using quota sampling. Thematic analysis was employed to analyse the data. The findings revealed that product pricing, product availability, convenience, delivery time, website usability, trust, payment security and online customer reviews were the major determinants influencing online purchase decisions. Product pricing emerged as the strongest determinant, followed by convenience and product availability. Consumers indicated that transparent pricing, authentic product reviews and secure payment systems enhanced purchase intentions, whereas delivery delays and concerns regarding online security reduced consumers' willingness to purchase online. The study concludes that online purchasing behaviour is influenced by economic, technological and psychological factors that retailers must address simultaneously. The study recommends that SPAR Botswana strengthen its digital marketing strategy through competitive pricing, enhanced website functionalit

latest.title: When Price Cuts Fail to Pay Off: Behavioral Mechanisms Mediating the Price Reduction-Purchase Behaviour Relationship in Multi-tier Fast-moving Consumer Goods Distribution
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Price cuts are widely used in FMCG distribution to stimulate purchasing, yet lower trade prices do not always translate into stronger buying decisions when retailers face inventory risk, cash-flow limits, and local market pressure. This study explains how price reduction influences purchase behaviour among retail outlet owners and wholesalers by examining the mediating roles of competitive perception, price policy, and stocking intention. A quantitative survey was conducted with 278 retail outlets and wholesalers in Manado, Palu, Kendari, and Makassar after data screening from the initial target sample. The proposed relationships were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) to assess the direct and mediating effects. The results show that price reduction significantly strengthens competitive perception, price policy evaluation, stocking intention, and purchase behaviour. Competitive perception and stocking intention significantly mediate the relationship between price reduction and purchase behaviour, while price policy shows a positive but insignificant mediating role. These findings suggest that FMCG suppliers should connect price reductions with margin logic, sell-out support, stock rotation planning, and local market positioning. This study extends behavioural pricing literature by showing that price cuts work through retailers’ interpretation of competitive usefulness and inventory feasibility.

latest.title: Determinants of financial well-being among Millennials and Generation Z in Indonesia
latest.abstract: Technological advancements have transformed the lives of Millennials and Generation Z, particularly in the realm of payments. The variety of payment methods has expanded to include QRIS, e-money, bank transfers, and cash. The growing convenience of payment requires enhanced consumer financial literacy. Moreover, perspectives on deferred payment and financial attitudes are essential for sustainable financial planning. This study seeks to analyze the determinants affecting financial well-being among Generation Z and Millennials in Indonesia. Both quantitative and qualitative methodologies were employed. Data collection using purposive sampling. Three hundred respondents were recruited. The instruments employed were assessed for validity and reliability. Instrument and hypothesis testing employed structural equation modeling with partial least squares (SEM-PLS). The hypothesis test results demonstrate that financial attitude is the predominant factor affecting financial well-being. Financial literacy does not directly affect financial well-being; rather, it influences it indirectly by mediating financial behavior. The attitude towards pay-later options does not significantly affect financial behavior or financial well-being. The originality of this study resides in its analysis of financial literacy, attitudes towards deferred payment, and financial attitudes concerning behavior and well-being.

latest.title: Faktor-Faktor yang Memengaruhi Keputusan Investasi dengan Perilaku Keuangan sebagai Variabel Moderasi
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the factors influencing students’ investment decisions, with financial behavior as a moderating variable. The independent variables include financial literacy, financial attitude, the use of financial technology, and risk tolerance. This research employs a causal associative quantitative approach involving 202 students of the Faculty of Economics and Management, Universitas Malahayati, class of 2022. Data were collected through online questionnaires using a 1–5 Likert scale and analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS version 3. The results indicate that financial literacy and risk tolerance have a significant effect on investment decisions, while financial attitude and financial technology usage have no significant effect. Financial behavior is proven to moderate the influence of financial literacy and risk tolerance on investment decisions.

latest.title: ANALISIS PENGARUH HARGA TERHADAP KEPUTUSAN PEMBELIAN KONSUMEN
latest.venue: Journal of Social and Economics Research
latest.abstract: Harga merupakan salah satu pertimbangan utama konsumen sebelum memutuskan membeli suatu produk, tetapi besarnya pengaruh harga berbeda pada setiap konteks pasar. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh harga terhadap keputusan pembelian konsumen berdasarkan temuan penelitian terdahulu. Metode yang digunakan adalah studi literatur dengan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif terhadap artikel jurnal nasional dan internasional yang terbit pada tahun 2023 sampai 2026 , dengan dukungan dua artikel klasik sebagai landasan teori. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa harga berpengaruh positif terhadap Keputusan pembelian melalui tiga jalur utama, yaitu keterjangkauan, perbandingan harga antarpenjual, dan kesesuaian harga dengan manfaat serta kualitas yang dipersepsikan. Pengaruh harga tidak berdiri sendiri. Kualitas produk, word of mouth, kepercayaan dan persepsirisiko ikut membentuk Keputusan, dan pada Sebagian konteks kualitas produk lebih dominan daripada harga. Strategis penetapan harga yang terukur, termasuk diskon, perlu disesuaikan dengan persepsi nilai konsumen agar meningkatkan pembelian tanpa mengorbankan keberlanjutan usaha.

latest.title: Kontribusi Live Streaming dan Influencer Terhadap Impulsive Buying Generasi Z di Tiktok Shop
latest.abstract: enelitian ini bertujuan untuk: 1) menguji dan menganalisis pengaruh live streaming terhadap impulsive buying produk fashion pada Generasi Z di Kecamatan Bulawa Kabupaten Bone Bolango; 2) menguji dan menganalisis pengaruh influencer terhadap impulsive buying; dan 3) menguji dan menganalisis pengaruh live streaming dan influencer secara simultan terhadap impulsive buying. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain asosiatif kausal. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 96 responden Generasi Z pengguna aktif TikTok Shop yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling berdasarkan rumus Lemeshow. Data primer dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner berskala Likert. Metode analisis yang digunakan adalah analisis deskriptif dan analisis regresi linier berganda. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa: 1) live streaming berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap impulsive buying, dengan nilai t hitung sebesar 2,322 dan signifikansi 0,022, sehingga hipotesis pertama diterima; 2) influencer berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap impulsive buying, dengan nilai t hitung sebesar 10,028 dan signifikansi 0,001, sehingga hipotesis kedua diterima; dan 3) live streaming dan influencer secara simultan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap impulsive buying, dengan nilai F hitung sebesar 74,711 dan signifikansi 0,001, sehingga hipotesis ketiga diterima. Koefisien determinasi (R²) sebesar 0,616 atau 61,6% berada pada interval 0,60?0,799 yang menunjukkan adanya tingkat hubungan yang kuat antara live streaming dan influencer dengan impulsive buying.

latest.title: Pengaruh Lokasi dan Harga terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen pada Maju Bersama MMTC Medan
latest.venue: Journal of Management and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the partial and simultaneous effects of location and price on consumer purchase decisions at Maju Bersama MMTC Medan. A quantitative approach with a causal associative design was used. The sample consisted of 62 respondents selected through incidental sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and observation and analyzed using multiple linear regression, supplemented by the t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The results show that location has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (B = 0.622; t = 12.034; p < 0.001). Price also has a positive and significant effect (B = 0.166; t = 2.858; p = 0.006). Simultaneously, location and price significantly affect purchase decisions (F = 231.432; p < 0.001), with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.887, indicating that the model explains 88.7% of the variation in purchase decisions. Based on the standardized beta coefficients, location (0.793) has a stronger relationship with purchase decisions than price (0.188). Management is advised to maintain accessibility, visibility, and parking comfort, and to evaluate customers' price perceptions regularly.

latest.title: The effect of financial literacy on cryptocurrency investment decision with the mediation of students' risk tolerance and risk taking
latest.venue: Journal of Management Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)
latest.abstract: The growth of cryptocurrency investment among college students has increased significantly. However, this trend is not always accompanied by sufficient understanding or preparedness to manage investment risks. This study examines the effects of financial literacy on cryptocurrency investment decisions, risk tolerance, and risk-taking behaviour, as well as the effects of risk tolerance and risk-taking behaviour on investment decisions and their mediating roles. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data collected from college students who have experience investing in cryptocurrency. The data were analysed using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) to examine the direct and mediating effects among the variables. The findings indicate that financial literacy significantly influences cryptocurrency investment decisions, risk tolerance, and risk-taking behaviour. Furthermore, risk tolerance and risk-taking behaviour significantly affect investment decisions and mediate the relationship between financial literacy and cryptocurrency investment decisions. This study contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence on the role of financial literacy and risk-related factors in shaping cryptocurrency investment decisions among college students, offering insights for improving students’ financial decision-making and risk management. Keywords: Behavioural Finance Theory; Financial Literacy; Investment Decision; Cryptocurrency; Risk Tolerance; Risk Taking Behaviour

latest.title: ปจจยทสงผลตอการตดสนใจเลอกใชบรการคลนกเสรมความงามของผชายกลมเมโทรเซกชวล ในกรงเทพมหานคร
latest.venue: Journal of the Association of Researchers
latest.abstract: Male grooming in urban Thailand has expanded steadily, and aesthetic clinics need to know which marketing elements shape men’s choice of provider. This quantitative study aimed to (1) examine the service marketing mix (7Ps) of aesthetic clinics in Bangkok, (2) study the decision-making process of metrosexual men in selecting aesthetic clinic services in Bangkok, and (3) analyze the service marketing mix factors affecting this decision-making process. The sample comprised 400 metrosexual men aged 20–50 years who lived, worked, or spent their daily lives in Bangkok and had used aesthetic clinic services. Respondents were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling and had to pass all five screening questions. Data were collected with an online questionnaire whose items all had IOC values above .50, with overall reliability coefficients of .89 for the service marketing mix and .86 for the decision-making process. Data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, mean, standard deviation, and multiple regression analysis. The results showed that (1) respondents rated the 7Ps at high to highest levels of importance, with physical evidence rated highest (M = 4.55) and price lowest (M = 4.40); (2) the overall decision-making process was at a high level (M = 4.49), and comparing quality and price before choosing a clinic received the highest mean; and (3) the seven factors jointly explained 64.1% of the variance in the decision-making process, with physical evidence (β = .461), price (β = .151), and place (β = .138) having significant effects, so the hypothesis was partially supported. The key finding is that factors consumers can verify or compare before receiving the service drive the decision, whereas promotion, although ranked second in importance, had no significant ef

latest.title: Relationship between Income Level and Price Sensitivity Among Consumers
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Abstract Price is one of the many factors that have an effect on the buying decisions of consumers. However, the impact of price on the decision-making process is quite dissimilar at various income levels. The current study seeks to understand the effects of consumer income levels on price sensitivity, in other words, how the financial standing of the consumer affects their perception of price and their willingness to pay for brands and buy generally. Specifically, the research aims to examine the degree of price responsiveness among people of different income levels. The primary data for the study will be collected through the means of a structured survey of consumers of various income levels. The use of descriptive statistics and correlation analysis, among other statistical measures, will be required in the examination of the effects of income on price sensitivity. Finally, the overall goal of this research is to shed light on the effects of income on price sensitivity. Such information is extremely helpful for business organizations in creating appropriate price strategies. This study looks at how a person's income shapes how sensitive they are to price changes. Price sensitivity is simply how much a customer's buying choices shift when a price goes up or down. When you look at how people shop, income is usually the biggest piece of the puzzle. It determines what someone can actually afford, which naturally shapes how much they’re willing—and able—to hand over at the register. How you react to a price change often comes down to your bank account. When money is tight, every single dollar counts. You automatically become more cautious—you check price tags twice, hunt for coupons, and hold off on buying until things go on sale. When you have a comfortable financial cus

latest.title: Internationalizing Marketing Management Education through Academic Exchange, Industry Engagement, and Community Empowerment: An International Community Service Program in Malaysia and Singapore
latest.abstract: International community service can connect marketing education with professional practice and cooperation. This program comprised an interinstitutional assignment to Malaysia and Singapore and academic–industry engagement at Karangkraf Malaysia. Implementation involved preparation, knowledge exchange, an industrial visit, reflective evaluation, and follow-up planning. Academics discussed digital marketing, while practitioners shared publishing management and business experience. Participants encountered editorial, design, printing, and distribution processes. Immediate outputs included industry insights, initial institutional communication, publication materials, and curriculum recommendations. Community empowerment took the form of reciprocal professional knowledge sharing. The program linked international engagement with industry-informed education.

latest.title: Kepuasan Konsumen pada Rumah Makan di Wilayah Non-Metropolitan: Peran Kualitas Produk, Persepsi Harga, dan Promosi di Purworejo
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of product quality, price perception, and promotion on consumer satisfaction at Rumah Makan Satu Satu Purworejo. Data were collected through a survey using closed-ended questionnaires based on a Likert scale, distributed to consumers aged at least 20 years who had visited the restaurant at least twice, resided in Purworejo Regency, and were willing to complete the questionnaire honestly and thoroughly. A total of 100 respondents were selected using purposive sampling, a sampling technique involving the deliberate selection of participants based on characteristics relevant to the study objectives. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics 25. Prior to the analysis, validity, reliability, and classical assumption tests were conducted. The residuals were found to be non-normally distributed, while the Glejser test indicated potential heteroscedasticity in the promotion variable. Therefore, partial coefficient testing was supplemented with 5,000 bootstrap resamples using simple sampling and 95% bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) confidence intervals. The F-test results indicated that the model was simultaneously significant (F = 79.022, Sig. = 0.000), with an R Square value of 0.712. Based on the bootstrap results, product quality had a positive but statistically insignificant coefficient (B = 0.143, p = 0.244). Price perception had a positive and significant effect on consumer satisfaction (B = 0.703, p less than 0.001), while promotion had a positive but statistically insignificant coefficient (B = 0.130, p = 0.376). Thus, H1 and H3 were not supported, whereas H2 was supported.

latest.title: The PPP Framework for Safe Launch Pricing: Premium, Promotion, Penetration
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: A new product faces a pricing dilemma: a high price may deter trial of an unproven brand, while a low price may generate trial but teach customers that this is the product's normal price, making later increases difficult. This paper proposes the PPP framework for safe launch pricing, which separates two functions of price: the positioning price, which signals the tier to which the product belongs, and the transaction price actually paid at launch. The Premium reference price is derived from the "product leader" in quality and image; the Penetration price is derived from the best-selling "market leader"; and a genuine, temporary promotion bridges the two, protecting the reference price from being replaced in customers' minds by the launch price. Price is then recovered gradually by reducing the discount in response to evidence of market acceptance rather than the passage of time. The paper presents the framework's six stages, a numerical example, a comparison with conventional penetration pricing, the literature that explains its mechanisms, and the conditions for its use and failure, including legal constraints on price reductions.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan, Kualitas Produk dan Variasi Menu Terhadap Kepuasan Pelanggan di Ask Coffee Marelan
latest.abstract: Penjualan Ask Coffee Marelan menurun dari Rp657,0 juta pada 2022 menjadi Rp504,7 juta pada 2025 di tengah persaingan coffee shop yang semakin ketat. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh kualitas pelayanan, kualitas produk, dan variasi menu terhadap kepuasan pelanggan Ask Coffee Marelan. Penelitian kuantitatif asosiatif ini mengumpulkan data melalui kuesioner dari 100 pelanggan, dengan ukuran sampel ditentukan menggunakan rumus Lemeshow, kemudian menganalisisnya dengan regresi linear berganda menggunakan SPSS versi 27. Kualitas pelayanan (B = 0,002; t = 0,039; p = 0,969) dan kualitas produk (B = −0,017; t = −0,255; p = 0,799) tidak berpengaruh signifikan secara parsial terhadap kepuasan pelanggan, sedangkan variasi menu berpengaruh positif dan signifikan (B = 0,527; β = 0,830; t = 6,013; p < 0,001). Secara simultan, ketiga variabel berpengaruh signifikan (F = 55,274; p < 0,001) dan menjelaskan 63,3% variasi kepuasan pelanggan. Tumpang tindih yang tinggi antara kualitas produk dan prediktor lain (VIF = 7,546) mengindikasikan bahwa kontribusi uniknya terserap oleh variasi menu. Ask Coffee Marelan perlu memprioritaskan pengembangan menu dengan tetap menjaga standar produk dan pelayanan.

latest.title: The Effect of Employee Service Quality on Customer Satisfaction Mediated by Price At the A2 Aluminum and Glass Shop MSME in Palembang City
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of employee service quality on customer satisfaction, mediated by price, at UMKM Toko Aluminium dan Kaca A2 in Palembang. As consumer expectations shift toward customization, consultative selling becomes crucial. A quantitative method with a purposive sampling of 100 respondents was employed. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Square (SEM-PLS) via SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that service quality significantly affects price perceptions and customer satisfaction. Furthermore, price significantly influences customer satisfaction and partially mediates the relationship between service quality and customer satisfaction. Effectively implementing consultative selling justifies pricing and enhances overall satisfaction.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: LOW-PURCHASE LONG-STAY BEHAVIOUR AT ZUS COFFEE: CROWDING, FAIRNESS AND REVISIT INTENTION
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: This study examines how low-purchase long-stay behaviour influences customer experience in urban coffee chains, using ZUS Coffee customers in Malaysia as the research context. As cafés increasingly function as informal work, study and social spaces, customers who purchase minimally but occupy seats for extended periods may affect other customers’ perceptions of crowding, service fairness, satisfaction and revisit intention. Drawing on servicescape, perceived crowding and service fairness perspectives, this study develops a conceptual model linking low-purchase long-stay behaviour to perceived crowding, perceived service fairness, customer satisfaction and revisit intention. A quantitative survey design is proposed among ZUS Coffee customers who have recently visited physical outlets in Malaysia. The study contributes to consumer behaviour and service management literature by examining café space consumption as part of the customer experience. The findings are expected to provide practical implications for coffee chain operators in managing seating, customer comfort and fairness without weakening the café’s role as a flexible third place.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Pengaruh Persepsi Harga Paket Data terhadap Kepuasan Pengguna Dalam Komunikasi Penawaran Telkomsel Prabayar pada Mahasiswa Pendidikan Fisika Universitas Sriwijaya
latest.venue: Journal of Communication and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh harga paket internet Telkomsel Prabayar terhadap kepuasan pelanggan pada mahasiswa Pendidikan Fisika Universitas Sriwijaya angkatan 2022–2024. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei. Populasi berjumlah 266 mahasiswa dan sampel terdiri atas 111 responden pengguna Telkomsel Prabayar. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner dan dianalisis menggunakan uji validitas, reliabilitas, uji asumsi, serta regresi linear sederhana. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa instrumen penelitian valid dan reliabel. Persamaan regresi yang diperoleh adalah Y = 1,826 + 0,717X, dengan pengaruh harga paket internet yang signifikan terhadap kepuasan pelanggan (p = 0,002). Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa penilaian mahasiswa terhadap harga paket internet berkaitan dengan kepuasan mereka terhadap layanan Telkomsel Prabayar. Abstract This study examines the effect of Telkomsel prepaid internet package prices on customer satisfaction among Physics Education students at Universitas Sriwijaya from the 2022–2024 cohorts. A quantitative survey was conducted among 111 Telkomsel prepaid users from a population of 266 students. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through validity and reliability tests, assumption tests, and simple linear regression. The instruments met the reported validity and reliability criteria. The regression equation was Y = 1.826 + 0.717X, and the reported significance value was p = 0.002, indicating a statistically significant relationship between internet package prices and customer satisfaction. The findings indicate that students’ evaluations of internet package prices are associated with their satisfaction with Telkomsel prepaid services.

latest.title: Statistical Analysis Of Consumer Purchase Intention For Managerial Decision-Making In Commodity Markets: Evidence From The Indian Steel Industry
latest.abstract: In Indian retail steel market, managerial decisions to position the brand, quality communication, price and access to the market require evidence on the factors associated with consumer purchase intention. This study delves into the same relationship with the help of structured questionnaire response from consumers of the Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities of Karnataka and Maharashtra. This difference between the number of observations (152 in SPSS tables; 150 in sampling description) needs to be checked against the original data set. Pearson correlations, multiple linear regressions and a brand-logo comparison were employed in the analysis of purchasing intentions. The model with five predictors explained 58.7% of the variance (with R² = 0.587). None of the adjusted non-significant variables were brand awareness, perceived quality and price perception. In the reported Logo comparison, the purchase intention was found to be lower in the Logo group (ArcelorMittal) when compared with the No Logo (control) group. Sustainability and digital communication are still important, proposed considerations but were not demonstrated to have independent impact by the regression outputs displayed. How the study has interpreted these findings are used as evidence for assessing priorities within marketing rather than causal sales or resource optimisation gains.

latest.title: DRIVING LOYALTY THROUGH SERVICE-QUALITY: DO AGE AND INCOME MATTER? EVIDENCE FROM MALAYSIA’S AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: Customer loyalty is essential for sustaining competitive advantage in the automotive service industry, where repeated post-sales interactions strongly influence long-term customer relationships. This study examines the relationship between service quality and customer loyalty in Malaysia's automotive service industry and investigates whether age and income moderate this relationship. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted using data collected from 385 customers of authorised automotive service centres in Malaysia. The data were analysed using multiple regression analysis. The findings reveal that service quality has a significant positive effect on customer loyalty, confirming that customers who perceive higher levels of service quality are more likely to remain loyal to their service providers. Although age exhibited a significant direct relationship with customer loyalty, neither age nor income significantly moderated the relationship between service quality and customer loyalty. These findings suggest that the influence of service quality on customer loyalty remains consistent across different demographic groups. This study contributes to the service marketing literature by providing evidence from an emerging market and offering practical implications for automotive service providers, highlighting the importance of consistently delivering high-quality services to strengthen customer loyalty rather than relying on demographic-based service differentiation.

latest.title: PENGARUH FINTECH DAN PERILAKU KONSUMTIF TERHADAP PENGELOLAAN KEUANGAN GEN- Z
latest.abstract: This study aims to empirically examine the influence of financial technology and consumer behavior on the financial management of Gen-Z students in Ambon City. This study used a quantitative approach. This study involved accounting students at several universities in Ambon City. The sample consisted of final-year students who had previously used digital payment applications (e-wallet, QRIS). Data collection was conducted by distributing online questionnaires using convenience sampling. Data analysis used multiple regression with SPSS. The results found that financial technology had a positive effect on Gen-Z financial management, while consumer behavior had no effect on Gen-Z financial management.

latest.title: Online Advertising Personalization, Price Perception, and Purchase Intention: Evidence from Prospective Tokopedia Customers in Mataram
latest.venue: International Journal of Business and Quality Research
latest.abstract: This study investigates how perceived online advertising personalization and price perception are associated with purchase intention toward Tokopedia among consumers in Mataram, Indonesia, who actively shop on competing e-commerce platforms but have never completed a purchase on Tokopedia. Grounded in the stimulus–organism–response perspective, a quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 100 purposively selected respondents. Data collected through a five-point Likert questionnaire were analyzed using multiple linear regression in IBM SPSS Statistics. Reanalysis of the item-level data confirmed significant positive relationships between online advertising personalization and purchase intention (B = 0.520, standardized β = 0.692, t = 11.231, p < .001), and between price perception and purchase intention (B = 0.245, β = 0.523, t = 8.492, p < .001). The two predictors jointly explained 64.0% of the observed variation in purchase intention (adjusted R² = 0.633). Both predictor constructs and purchase intention received mean ratings close to the neutral point, indicating scope for improving initial platform appeal. Advertising personalization was the stronger standardized predictor within this model. These findings suggest that relevance, credibility, and usefulness of advertising, alongside transparent price–value communication, may help Tokopedia engage prospective customers. The nonprobability design and self-reported intentions limit population generalization and causal interpretation.

latest.title: Pengaruh Word of Mouth, Persepsi Harga, dan Kualitas Hasil Cucian terhadap Keputusan Penggunaan Jasa pada Laundry Cleanfresh di Kabupaten Dompu
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Word of Mouth, Persepsi Harga, dan Kualitas Hasil Cucian terhadap Keputusan Penggunaan Jasa pada Laundry CleanFresh di Kabupaten Dompu, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui penyebaran kuesioner dengan menggunakan skala Likert. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan regresi linear berganda dengan bantuan program Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), meliputi uji validitas, uji reliabilitas, uji asumsi klasik, uji t, uji F, dan koefisien determinasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa secara parsial Word of Mouth tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Keputusan Penggunaan Jasa dengan nilai t hitung sebesar -0,035 dan signifikansi 0,972 > 0,05. Kualitas Hasil Cucian menjadi faktor yang memiliki pengaruh positif dan signifikan secara parsial terhadap Keputusan Penggunaan Jasa, sedangkan Word of Mouth dan Persepsi Harga tidak menunjukkan pengaruh signifikan secara parsial

latest.title: PENGARUH KUALITAS PRODUK, PROMOSI, PERSEPSI HARGA, KEPERCAYAAN PELANGGAN TERHADAP KEPUASAN PELANGGAN DAN LOYALITAS KONSUMEN PADA PUSAT OLEH-OLEH DAN KERIPIK BALADO
latest.venue: Journal of Practice Learning and Educational Development
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of: (1) product quality on customer satisfaction; (2) product quality on consumer loyalty; (3) promotion on customer satisfaction; (4) promotion on consumer loyalty; (5) price perception on customer satisfaction; (6) price perception on consumer loyalty; (7) customer trust on customer satisfaction; (8) customer trust on consumer loyalty; and (9) customer satisfaction on consumer loyalty. The results indicate that product quality has a significant effect on customer satisfaction and consumer loyalty. Promotion also has a significant effect on customer satisfaction and consumer loyalty. Price perception has a significant effect on both customer satisfaction and consumer loyalty. In contrast, customer trust has no significant effect on customer satisfaction or consumer loyalty. Furthermore, customer satisfaction has a significant effect on consumer loyalty. These findings indicate that product quality, promotion, price perception, and customer satisfaction play an important role in strengthening consumer loyalty, while customer trust does not have a direct significant effect in this research context.

latest.title: Literasi Keuangan dan Hifẓ al-Māl: Strategi Perempuan Pekerja Penerima PKH Mengelola Keuangan Keluarga
latest.abstract: Working women who receive Indonesia’s Family Hope Program (PKH) serve as breadwinners and household financial managers, making financial literacy essential to family welfare. This study examines financial education through the Family Capacity Building Meeting (P2K2) and its implications for family financial management from the perspective of hifẓ al-māl in maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah. Using a qualitative phenomenological approach in Palopo City, data were collected through in-depth interviews with six working-woman beneficiaries, three facilitators, and one program coordinator, supplemented by observation and documentation. Data were analyzed using Miles–Huberman–Saldaña procedures with NVivo assistance. The findings reveal that P2K2 introduces budgeting through the envelope technique, although its implementation is hindered by low attendance, time constraints, established spending habits, and facilitators’ heavy caseloads. All informants prioritize essential expenditures, particularly children’s education, but only two consistently implement planned budgets. Five of six respondents save from residual income and rely on neighbor loans (qarḍ) or gold pawning (rahn) to address financial emergencies. Productive asset ownership remains limited. Viewed through the five dimensions of hifẓ al-māl, financial literacy supports spending control but remains weak in wealth accumulation and protection. Therefore, integrating Sharia-compliant saving, financing, and investment education into P2K2 is necessary to strengthen family financial resilience.

latest.title: Brand Image, Service Quality, and Price Effects on Purchase Decisions through Consumer Satisfaction at Indomaret
latest.venue: GoodWill Journal of Economics Management and Accounting
latest.abstract: Modern retail competition requires firms to understand how brand image, service quality, and price shape consumer satisfaction and purchase decisions. However, understanding the role of consumer satisfaction as a mediating mechanism is essential for developing effective retail strategies. This study aimed to examine the effects of brand image, service quality, and price on purchase decisions, with consumer satisfaction as a mediating variable among Indomaret customers in Probolinggo City. A quantitative explanatory survey was conducted using purposive sampling of consumers who had experience purchasing products at Indomaret outlets. Primary data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling with SmartPLS. The results showed that brand image, service quality, and price had significant positive effects on consumer satisfaction. Brand image, service quality, price, and consumer satisfaction also had significant positive effects on purchase decisions. Furthermore, consumer satisfaction significantly mediated the relationships between brand image, service quality, and price and purchase decisions. These findings indicate that purchase decisions in modern retail are influenced by both direct transactional considerations and satisfaction-based evaluations. The study contributes to understanding consumer purchasing behavior by highlighting consumer satisfaction as an important mechanism linking brand image, service quality, and price to purchase decisions. Practically, the findings suggest that modern retail managers should maintain a favorable brand image, deliver consistent service quality, and offer competitive prices while enhancing consumer satisfaction to strengthen purchase decisions.

latest.title: Digital Payment and Promotion on Gen Z Consumptive Behavior: Pain of Paying as Mediator
latest.venue: Journal of Business and Economics Research (JBE)
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of digital financial technology has transformed transactional and consumption behaviour, particularly among Generation Z. This study examines the effects of digital payment and digital promotion on consumptive behaviour, with pain of paying as a mediating variable, among Generation Z consumers in Batam City. Using a quantitative causal approach and cross-sectional design, data were collected from 160 respondents aged 17–30 years through a structured online questionnaire and analysed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The results show that digital payment has a significant positive effect on consumptive behaviour (β = 0.342, p < 0.001), while digital promotion has no significant direct effect (p = 0.068). Digital payment does not significantly affect pain of paying (p = 0.096), whereas digital promotion has a significant positive effect on pain of paying (β = 0.359, p < 0.001). Pain of paying neither significantly affects consumptive behaviour nor mediates the relationships between digital payment, digital promotion, and consumptive behaviour. These findings indicate that Generation Z’s consumptive behaviour in Batam City is driven more directly by the convenience and frictionless nature of digital payments than by pain of paying. The study contributes to understanding consumer behaviour in the digital era and provides implications for financial literacy, digital payment services, and digital marketing practices.

latest.title: The Influence of Muslimah Friendly Branding, Product Quality, and Celebrity Endorser on Purchase Intention toward Cosmetic Products in the Era of Skincare-Makeup Hybrids
latest.venue: GoodWill Journal of Economics Management and Accounting
latest.abstract: The Indonesian cosmetics industry continues to develop alongside increasing consumer demand for products that provide not only decorative benefits but also skincare benefits. The growth of skincare-makeup hybrids reflects changing consumer preferences towards multifunctional and practical products with additional benefits. This development makes branding that meets Muslimah needs, product quality, and the use of celebrity endorsers relevant factors in shaping purchase intention. This study aims to analyse the influence of Muslimah Friendly Branding, Product Quality, and Celebrity Endorser on Purchase Intention for Cosmetic Products in the Era of Skincare-Makeup Hybrids. A quantitative method was employed involving 180 female respondents aged at least 18 years who were familiar with or used skincare-makeup hybrid cosmetic products. Data were collected through a questionnaire using a 1–10 semantic differential scale and analysed using multiple linear regression, t-tests, and the coefficient of determination. The results show that Muslimah Friendly Branding has a positive and significant effect on purchase intention, with a coefficient of 0.265 and a significance value of 0.000. Product Quality has a positive and significant effect, with a coefficient of 0.208 and a significance value of 0.000, while Celebrity Endorser has a positive and significant effect, with a coefficient of 0.196 and a significance value of 0.002. The Adjusted R Square value of 0.443 indicates that the three variables explain 44.3% of the variation in purchase intention. The study concludes that these three factors contribute to shaping purchase intention for cosmetic products in the era of skincare-makeup hybrids.

hot.title: Understanding the Role of Financial Literacy in Enhancing Economic Stability and Resilience in Montenegro: A Data-Driven Approach
hot.abstract: Financial literacy has emerged as a crucial factor in promoting economic stability and resilience, particularly in Montenegro. With the increasing complexity of financial products and the growing need for individuals to make sound financial decisions, the importance of financial literacy cannot be overstated. This study employs a quantitative, survey-based approach to explore the association between financial literacy levels and measures of economic stability, including savings rates, active debt management, and access to financial products. Data were collected through a representative, two-stage stratified sample of 1000 Montenegrin adults aged 18–79, ensuring comprehensive geographic coverage across all Montenegrin municipalities and balanced representation by gender and age. This stratification enables a detailed analysis of financial literacy trends across the population. Correlation analysis reveals that higher levels of financial literacy are associated with better financial practices, such as increased savings and responsible credit use, thereby enhancing economic resilience at the household level. Moreover, improved financial literacy contributes to sustainability by fostering long-term financial stability, reducing inequalities, and promoting inclusive economic growth. The findings suggest that financial literacy can mitigate the impact of economic shocks, emphasizing the need for policies that promote financial education as a tool for sustainable development. This study contributes to the literature on financial literacy in emerging economies and offers actionable insights for policymakers in Montenegro and similar contexts, highlighting financial education as a pathway to individual and national economic resilience.

hot.title: The Impact of Visual Elements of Packaging Design on Purchase Intention: Brand Experience as a Mediator in the Tea Bag Product Category
hot.abstract: While packaging design plays a vital role in experience-oriented markets, how multiple visual elements influence purchase intention through brand experience remains unclear. This study addresses this gap by employing innovative orthogonal experiments to examine the complex relationship between the visual elements of packaging design and purchase intention for low-involvement products, integrating both design and marketing perspectives. Through orthogonal experimental design, we developed 14 packaging prototypes as stimuli by systematically manipulating five visual elements (Colour, Graphics, Logo, Typography, and Layout). The framework and prototypes were validated through expert evaluation. Data were collected via a cross-sectional survey from 490 tea bag consumers and analysed using SPSS (version 29.0) for preliminary data processing and Mplus (version 8.3) for structural equation modelling. Our results reveal the direct effects of visual packaging elements on consumer purchase intention. Notably, Colour, Graphics, Logo, and Layout significantly influence purchase intention through brand experience mediation. Importantly, our multi-level analysis of visual elements unveils distinct patterns in how different design levels (e.g., colour harmony, graphic types) affect consumer responses. This study provides novel theoretical insights into how consumers make purchase decisions based on packaging design visual elements, addressing a significant gap in existing research. Unlike previous studies focusing on isolated design elements, our systematic classification and multi-level analysis offer both theoretical insights into packaging design mechanisms and practical guidelines for designers and practitioners.

hot.title: Factors influencing Generation Z’s intention to purchase sustainable clothing products in Vietnam
hot.abstract: The increasing awareness of environmental challenges has significantly influenced consumer behavior, with sustainable products, particularly sustainable clothing, becoming a top priority for Generation Z consumers. This study aims to investigate the factors influencing Generation Z's purchase intentions toward sustainable clothing in Vietnam, guided by the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) frameworks. Specifically, it examines the effects of green perceived value, green perceived quality, perceived price, social influence, product design, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge on purchase intentions. The study also explores the mediating roles of environmental attitude and product attitude in these relationships. The research employed a quantitative approach, using a Likert scale questionnaire to gather data from 641 Vietnamese Generation Z consumers. The study utilized exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM) to analyze the data. The results revealed that all proposed hypotheses were supported, indicating that all factors significantly impact environmental attitude and product attitude, which, in turn, influence purchase intention. The results emphasize the strong mediating role of environmental attitude and product attitude, suggesting that consumers with positive attitudes toward the environment and products are more likely to intend to purchase sustainable clothing. This research provides valuable insights into the psychological and contextual factors that influence Generation Z's sustainable consumption behavior.
